Job Title: Quality Systems Manager
Location: Frederica, Delaware

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Quality Management Systems (QMS) Manager is responsible for the development, implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the organization's Quality Management System, supplier quality, configuration management, and supporting quality processes for the Astrospace & Defense Solutions business. This role ensures compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, industry, and certification requirements, including AS9100D, while driving operational excellence, supplier performance, risk mitigation, and a culture of quality throughout the organization. The Quality Systems Manager is a people leader, with oversight of a team of approximately 5 employees. Communications among team members and external partners is critical for this role, in all forms. The incumbent has a wide latitude of discretion and significant influence and impact on the quality function as a whole.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain and continuously improve the Quality Management System (QMS) in accordance with AS9100D, ISO 9001, customer requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
  • Ensure organizational compliance with company quality policies, procedures, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), customer requirements, and regulatory obligations.
  • Develop, manage, and execute internal audit programs and coordinate external audits conducted by customers, certification bodies, and regulatory agencies.
  • Serve as the primary liaison with customers, certification bodies, and regulatory agencies on quality system and compliance matters.
  • Oversee document control processes to ensure quality documentation, procedures, work instructions, and records remain accurate, current, and compliant.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk identification, assessment, mitigation, and ongoing monitoring to support business and quality objectives.
  • Manage quality system processes, including corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), nonconformance management, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Develop, analyze, and report quality performance metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) to drive data-based decision-making and operational excellence.
  • Prepare and facilitate Management Review meetings and provide recommendations to leadership regarding quality system effectiveness and improvement opportunities.
  • Partner with Supply Chain, Engineering, and Operations to evaluate, qualify, approve, and monitor supplier performance.
  • Lead and develop Configuration Management personnel, assigning priorities and workload.
  • Responsible for controlling, documenting, and maintaining the integrity of a product’s configuration throughout its lifecycle. Ensuring drawings, specifications, BOMs, software versions, and documents are properly controlled.
  • Chair or participate in Configuration Control Boards and participate in the Project Development Team (PDT).
  • Lead supplier audits, assessments, surveillance activities, and supplier corrective action processes to ensure compliance with contractual, customer, and regulatory requirements.
  • Implement corporate quality initiatives and collaborate with site leadership to drive quality improvement programs and achieve business objectives.
  • Provide quality-related training and guidance to employees to promote compliance, quality awareness, and continuous improvement.
  • Participate on cross-functional teams and collaborate with customers, suppliers, and external partners to resolve quality issues and support strategic initiatives.
  • May provide leadership and direction for quality personnel, including recruitment, coaching, performance management, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Foster a culture of quality, accountability, customer focus, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

Requirements:

  • Must be able to access shared databases supporting U.S. Government programs. Due to U.S. export control regulations, applicants must qualify as a U.S. Person, defined as a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder), refugee, asylee, or otherwise be eligible to obtain any required U.S. Government authorizations.
  • Experience maintaining an AS9100-certified QMS, leading internal and external audits, corrective actions, and quality system improvement initiatives
  • Certified Six Sigma Green Belt or higher
  • Formal AS9100D Quality Management System training
  • AS9100D or ISO 9001 Internal Auditor or Lead Auditor certification

Core Competencies:

  • Understanding and wide application of technical principles, theories, and concepts related to Total Quality Management Systems and manufacturing operations
  • Solutions-oriented thinking for difficult, technical situations
  • Self-directed and proficient with time and project management
  • Demonstrated ability to lead either through authority or influence
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Excellent presentation skills
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite including Word, PowerPoint and Excel; Ability to adapt/ adjust to new technologies and methods

Preferences:

  • Working knowledge of aerospace customer, regulatory, and quality requirements
  • Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Quality Management, Industrial or related field of study.
  • 5+ years of quality management or quality assurance experience in manufacturing
  • Experience with configuration management


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Fully site based
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to work near moving mechanical parts; occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles; and chemicals or solutions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
  • The employee regularly sits, stands and walks.
  • The employee occasionally lifts and/or moves up to 20 pounds.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and talk or hear.
  • The employee will regularly use visual attention, eye focusing, visual perception.
  • The employee will regularly use reason, logic, and critical-thinking skills.

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Location: Southern Pines, NC

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
Keep production moving. Strengthen supplier partnerships. Make an impact where it matters. Ingersoll Rand is seeking a Material Buyer / Planner to play a key role in keeping production running smoothly at our Southern Pines facility. This dynamic position combines material buying and planning (60%) with production planning (40%), offering the opportunity to directly influence material availability, production schedules, inventory performance, and on-time customer delivery. You'll manage an assigned portfolio of approximately 30–50 suppliers, coordinate purchasing and inbound materials, resolve shortages and delivery challenges, and ensure components are available to support assembly operations and service-parts requirements. You'll also develop production schedules, respond to changing priorities, and collaborate across teams to keep manufacturing on track.

Supporting a diverse range of products—including precision fastening systems, power tools, material-handling equipment, and industrial pumps—you'll use QAD (MFG/PRO) and Excel to analyze material requirements, manage purchasing activity, monitor supplier performance, and identify opportunities to improve inventory efficiency. You'll also help coordinate engineering changes and work closely with Production, Engineering, Customer Service, and Supply Chain leadership. If you enjoy balancing supplier relationships, material planning, and production demands while solving challenges that directly impact manufacturing success, this is an opportunity to make a difference every day.

Responsibilities:

  • Procurement & Supplier Management: Perform timely, cost-effective procurement of production materials and inventory. Evaluate requisitions, select approved suppliers, onboard new suppliers, and ensure compliance with purchasing procedures and approval requirements.
  • Production Planning & Scheduling: Analyze production requirements, manufacturing capacity, material availability, and lead times to develop and maintain production schedules, workflow sequences, and resource plans.
  • Material Planning & Inventory Optimization: Maintain material plans to ensure continuity of supply, optimize inventory and safety stock levels, manage SOMI/VMI inventory, and improve working capital through effective replenishment strategies, including Kanban.
  • On-Time Delivery & Order Fulfillment: Maximize On-Time Shipment (OTS) performance by coordinating material deliveries with production schedules, expediting critical requirements, managing shortages, and providing accurate customer promise dates.
  • Supplier Performance & Issue Resolution: Monitor supplier performance, manage delivery exceptions (expedites, de-expedites, and cancellations), resolve invoicing discrepancies, and collaborate with Quality Assurance and Procurement to address supplier-related issues.
  • Forecasting & Supply Coordination: Communicate forecasts and replenishment plans to suppliers, maintain accurate item master lead times, evaluate material and capacity constraints, and coordinate with production planners and cross-functional teams to resolve delivery challenges.
  • Cost Reduction & Continuous Improvement: Identify and implement cost-saving, productivity, and cash flow improvement opportunities. Maintain project pipelines and financial records to track progress against corporate objectives.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration & Leadership: Partner with Production, Procurement, Quality, Accounting, and other functional teams to resolve operational challenges, improve planning and execution, and provide direction to others as needed to achieve organizational objectives.


Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED
  • 3+ years of experience in material planning, production planning, buying, and/or production / supplier scheduling, and knowledge of supplier processes within a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including proficiency in creating and working with formulas.
  • 1+ year of experience in manufacturing operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.
  • 1+ year of experience using MRP / ERP systems, such as QAD or Oracle.


Core Competencies

  • Materials Buying & Planning: Experience purchasing materials, managing supplier relationships, and ensuring timely material availability to support production requirements.
  • Production Planning & Scheduling: Ability to coordinate production schedules, evaluate material availability, and align inventory with manufacturing demands.
  • ERP / MRP Systems: Experience using ERP/MRP systems to manage purchase orders, inventory, material requirements, and supplier deliveries.
  • Excel & Data Analysis: Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas and data analysis to support purchasing, inventory management, and production planning.
  • Manufacturing or Distribution Operations: Understanding of manufacturing or distribution environments, inventory control, supply chain processes, and on-time delivery requirements.


Preferences:

  • Bachelor's Degree
  • APICS Certified in Planning and Inventory Management, CPIM, or an equivalent purchasing or supply management certification
  • Considerable knowledge of industry related supply base.
  • Visual management system experience
  • Ability to provide direction and training to peers as needed
  • Experience with rate based or flow line (non-MRP) and job shop manufacturing environments


Travel and Work Arrangements

  • This position is onsite in Southern Pines, NC
  • Travel less than 10%

Job Title: Data Analytics and Business Intelligence Analyst
Location: Davidson, NC

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Job Overview:
Turn business challenges into smarter solutions through data, analytics, and emerging AI technologies. Based in Davidson, NC, the Data Analytics and Business Intelligence Analyst is an exciting early- to mid-career opportunity offering a hybrid work arrangement and exposure across multiple business functions. Partnering with Finance, Engineering, Procurement, Commercial, and Operations teams, you will identify challenges, uncover opportunities for improvement, and translate business needs into actionable insights and practical analytics, automation, and business intelligence solutions.

Supporting the Compression Systems and Services North America (CSS NA) business unit, this is a business-focused analytics role centered on bridging the gap between business needs and technology. You will collaborate with stakeholders to understand operational challenges, gather requirements, and leverage business intelligence platforms such as Snowflake, Qlik, and KNIME, including their emerging AI capabilities, to develop solutions that improve processes, strengthen decision-making, and drive operational effectiveness. Rather than focusing primarily on software engineering, advanced programming, or AI model development, the emphasis is on applying existing technologies to solve real business problems. As part of a growing and evolving Analytics function, you will gain hands-on experience with business intelligence, data analytics, automation, and emerging AI technologies while contributing to the continued growth and maturity of the team's capabilities. Unlike traditional roles focused on narrowly defined technical tasks, this opportunity offers meaningful projects, exposure to experienced stakeholders across a complex manufacturing organization, and a strong foundation for long-term career growth.

The ideal candidate is a motivated, analytical professional who learns quickly, takes ownership, and follows through on commitments. You bring a foundational understanding of analytics and business intelligence technologies, practical exposure to AI-enabled tools, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to collaborate across functions. Success requires curiosity, adaptability, effective communication, and a genuine passion for using data and technology to solve business problems. Manufacturing experience is highly preferred but not required.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, maintain, and enhance dashboards, reports, data visualizations, and analytical applications using Qlik, Snowflake, Power BI and other emerging analytics technologies.
  • Build and validate reusable datasets and SQL queries
  • Investigate data discrepancies and test solution logic, AI-generated outputs, and handling of incomplete or ambiguous inputs.
  • Create and maintain shared definitions, mappings, and semantic views for consistent analysis in Snowflake, Qlik, and Excel.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand business workflows, identify manual steps and information gaps, and translate user needs into practical improvements.
  • Support ad hoc reporting requests and provide data-driven insights to stakeholders across the organization.
  • Help build and refine AI agents and self-service tools for finance and business teams; test with users and measure time saved, accuracy, and adoption.
  • Identify and assess opportunities to leverage AI and automation to improve reporting, business processes, operational efficiency, and decision-making.
  • Use approved AI-assisted development tools to accelerate development and troubleshooting while understanding and checking the resulting logic.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Finance, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of relevant professional experience, ideally 2–5 years in business analytics, business intelligence, financial or operational analytics, business systems, and/or process improvement. Relevant internship or co-op experience may be considered.
  • 2+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including formulas, data analysis, investigating discrepancies, and validating data accuracy.
  • 1+ years of practical experience analyzing business data, investigating discrepancies, identifying trends, and developing insights or solutions that support business decisions and operational improvements.
  • 1+ years of experience working with business stakeholders to understand processes, gather requirements, and translate business challenges into practical analytics, reporting, automation, or process improvement solutions.
  • 1+ years of hands-on experience using business intelligence, analytics, or automation tools to analyze data, support business decisions, or improve processes, including exposure to AI-enabled capabilities applied to business problems.


Core Competencies:

  • Business Acumen & Analytical Thinking: Ability to understand business processes, interpret data, identify trends, and translate findings into actionable insights that support business decisions.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to engage effectively with technical and nontechnical stakeholders, understand business requirements, and translate operational challenges into practical analytics and process improvement solutions.
  • Problem-Solving & Continuous Improvement: Demonstrates critical thinking, curiosity, and a solutions-oriented approach to identifying inefficiencies, resolving business challenges, and improving operational performance.
  • Adaptability & Learning Agility: Ability to quickly learn unfamiliar business processes, BI platforms, and emerging AI-enabled technologies and apply new knowledge to evolving business needs.
  • Ownership & Accountability: Demonstrates initiative, self-direction, attention to detail, and consistent follow-through on commitments, deliverables, and project responsibilities.
  • Communication & Knowledge Sharing: Ability to clearly explain analytical findings, communicate technical concepts to nontechnical audiences, and document solutions to support stakeholder understanding and adoption.


Preferences:

  • Experience with business intelligence, analytics, or business automation tools such as Snowflake, Qlik, Power BI, Streamlit, KNIME, Microsoft Forms, Power Automate, SharePoint, or comparable technologies.
  • Practical exposure to AI-enabled analytics, AI agents, application prototyping, or workflow automation used to solve business problems, improve processes, or support decision-making.
  • Experience developing dashboards, business reports, or analytical solutions that translate data into actionable insights for business stakeholders.
  • Experience supporting analytics, reporting, automation, or process improvement initiatives within manufacturing, operations, supply chain, finance, or other business functions.
  • Working knowledge of SQL, including interpreting queries, understanding joins, filters, and aggregations, and validating data accuracy and relationships.
  • Familiarity with data modeling, ETL processes, data integration, or fundamental data management concepts.


Work and Travel Arrangements:

  • This position is based from Davidson, NC.
  • It is a Hybrid role with Work-from-Home and regular in-office and attendance.

Job Overview:
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Sourcing Engineer to join our Compression Systems & Services Americas Sourcing Organization. This role involves supporting the development, implementation, and management of sourcing strategies to provide optimal supply assurance, pricing, flexibility, quality, and delivery performance. The Sourcing Engineer collaborates with engineering, operations, and quality teams, as well as key suppliers, to meet cost, quality, and delivery targets while fostering positive supplier relationships.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead supplier selection, negotiations, and RFP processes, including pricing, payment terms, lead times, and inventory programs, while fostering strong supplier relationships.
  • Identify and implement cost-saving opportunities through data analysis, hands-on material reviews, and continuous improvement ideation sessions aligned with plant priorities.
  • Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams to qualify new parts, address supplier performance issues, and ensure alignment with operational strategies like localization and plant rationalization.
  • Support new product development (NPD) activities by managing preliminary project costs, driving procurement efforts, and aligning with business cases through product launch.
  • Track and report sourcing activity metrics and savings, ensuring timely and accurate performance measurement while supporting plant teams in resolving escalated issues.
  • Coordinate with cross-functional teams—including commodity, materials, operations, engineering, finance, and quality—to complete projects within timelines and achieve expected benefits.
  • Represent the sourcing function in Value Analysis/Value Engineering (VAVE) and Major Model Review (MMR) events, ensuring post-event actions are executed effectively.
  • Promote continuous improvement through ideation sessions, aligning strategies to business priorities and addressing systemic supplier performance issues in quality, delivery, and warranty.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or equivalent.
  • 5+ years of industrial sourcing or supply chain materials experience.
  • Advanced negotiation skills and vendor assessment expertise.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word.
  • Ability to analyze, interpret, and present data for decision-making.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%.

Core Competencies:

  • Complex decision-making
  • Impeccable time management
  • Supply chain acumen
  • Project management
  • Relationship management

Preferences:

  • Advanced Excel skills preferred.
  • Oracle and SAP experience in a global environment is beneficial.

Job Title: Area Sales Manager
Location: Remote – Territory - CA, AZ, OR, WA, UT, NV, CO, ID, MT

About Us:
Welch Vacuum, a subsidiary of Ingersoll Rand since 1996, is a global leader with over a century of history in high-performance vacuum technologies. We specialize in vacuum pumps, systems, and components for laboratories, life sciences, and industrial manufacturing. Operating within Ingersoll Rand's medical and laboratory division, we combine the engineering strengths of US-based Welch Vacuum Technology and Germany's Ilmvac GmbH.

Job Overview:
We are seeking a dynamic Area Sales Manager to lead our Sales Engineering function across the US West Coast, Mexico, and potentially South America. Requiring up to 75% travel, this role drives the promotion and sale of diverse vacuum technologies and OEM components. You will champion solution-based selling to distributors, manufacturers, system integrators, and end-users across vital sectors—including Life Sciences, Medical, Chemical, and General Manufacturing.

Responsibilities

  • Drive Business Growth: Expand market share using modern prospecting methods, structured toll-gate sales processes, and solution-selling best practices.
  • Manage & Acquire Accounts: Nurture the existing distributor base and partner with dealer reps while aggressively pursuing new distribution, reseller, and OEM/system integrator opportunities.
  • Provide Technical Support: Serve as a trusted technical advisor to OEMs, large end-users, and academic research institutions to guide the pump specification and selection process directly in customer labs.
  • Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Partner closely with Field Sales Support, Application Engineering, Product Management, Operations, Quality, Finance, and Demand Generation to secure new business and drive profitable growth.
  • Lead Commercial Negotiations: Manage major pricing negotiations, define technical specifications, and ensure alignment across complex commercial agreements.
  • Build Multi-Level Relationships: Interface confidently with diverse customer departments on a technical and commercial level, including Engineering, Purchasing, Quality, and decision makers and leadership.
  • Maintain Data Integrity: Manage accurate sales forecasts and maintain up-to-date internal CRM reporting to support strategic growth objectives.
  • Apply Subject Matter Expertise: Leverage technical sales experience and vacuum pump technology knowledge to develop business and promote the Welch brand to new customers.
  • Execute Strategic Agility: Perform other responsibilities as assigned or required to support evolving business needs.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, Life Sciences, or a related technical field.
  • 3+ years of customer-facing vacuum sales experience, with a proven track record of growth.

Core Competencies

  • Strategic Selling: Ability to execute sophisticated sales strategies and drive new business development.
  • Problem Solving: Creative problem-solver skilled at resolving technical challenges and open issues.
  • Collaboration: Strong relationship builder with both external clients and internal support teams.
  • Organization: Exceptional multi-tasking abilities with sharp attention to detail, organization, and analysis.
  • Technology: Proficient in Microsoft Office and CRM systems (Salesforce preferred).
  • Languages: Professional fluency in English is required; Spanish proficiency is a strong plus.


Preferences:

  • Industry Expertise: Experience in the Laboratory, Analytical, and Life Sciences markets.
  • Technical Knowledge: Proven sales or application experience with vacuum pump technologies (or closely related industrial systems).
  • Account Management: Demonstrated success in prospecting, securing, and managing enterprise-level accounts.
  • Drive: High-energy self-starter with a goal-oriented mindset.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Remote with the ability to travel up to 50% within the West region.

The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Position: Manufacturing Engineer

Job Overview
The Manufacturing Engineer is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving manufacturing processes to support the production of power generation enclosure systems. This role will work closely with operations, quality, project management, and supply chain teams to improve safety, quality, productivity, and cost performance while supporting new product introductions and ongoing manufacturing operations.

Responsibilities
Manufacturing Process Development
Develop and implement efficient manufacturing processes for fabrication, welding, paint, and assembly operations.
Create and maintain work instructions, process documentation, and manufacturing standards.
Design and optimize production workflows to improve throughput and reduce waste.
Support facility and production line layout development to maximize operational efficiency.
Evaluate and implement new manufacturing technologies and equipment.
Production Support
Provide day-to-day technical support to manufacturing operations.
Troubleshoot production issues and implement corrective actions to minimize downtime.
Collaborate with supervisors and operators to improve process performance and product quality.
Analyze manufacturing data to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement.
Support capacity planning and resource utilization initiatives.
Continuous Improvement
Lead Lean Manufacturing initiatives focused on safety, quality, delivery, and cost improvements.
Conduct time studies and process evaluations to improve labor efficiency and productivity.
Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs).
Implement waste reduction and process optimization projects.
Facilitate root cause analysis and corrective action activities.
New Product Introduction & Engineering Changes
Support new product launches from concept through production implementation.
Develop manufacturing processes and tooling requirements for new products.
Review engineering drawings and specifications for manufacturability.
Coordinate engineering change implementation with production and quality teams.
Create and maintain Bills of Material (BOMs), routings, and manufacturing documentation.
Equipment & Tooling Management
Specify, procure, and implement manufacturing equipment and tooling.
Coordinate equipment installation, validation, and startup activities.
Support preventive maintenance and equipment reliability initiatives.
Identify automation opportunities to improve operational performance.

Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related field required.
Minimum 3-5 years of manufacturing engineering experience in a production environment.
Experience supporting fabrication, welding, assembly, or industrial manufacturing operations preferred.
Experience with Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, equipment, and production systems.
Technical Knowledge
Manufacturing process development
Lean Manufacturing principles
Root cause analysis and problem-solving techniques
Production workflow optimization
CAD software and engineering drawings
ERP/MRP systems
Process documentation and work instructions
Capacity and production planning
Tooling and equipment design
Statistical process control (SPC)
Preferred Certifications
Lean Manufacturing Certification
Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
Certified Manufacturing Engineer (CMfgE)
Project Management training or certification

Core Competencies
Technical problem-solving
Continuous improvement mindset
Project management skills
Data analysis and decision-making
Communication and collaboration
Attention to detail
Time management
Organizational skills
Adaptability and innovation

Location: Charlotte/Davidson, NC (preferred); West Chester, PA; Ocala, FL

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gases, and powders – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview
Ingersoll Rand’s CSS North America business is seeking a Product Manager, Air Treatment, with demonstrated experience in compressed-air treatment products and applications. This role leads the business performance, portfolio strategy, and lifecycle management of assigned Air Treatment product families, including equipment and aftermarket offerings.

Acting as the business leader for the assigned portfolio, the Product Manager is accountable for profitable growth through product strategy, pricing, innovation, and multi-year roadmap execution. This role combines air treatment knowledge with customer, market, competitive, and channel insights to develop differentiated products and lifecycle solutions that strengthen market position and deliver customer value.

Responsibilities

• Own business performance for assigned Air Treatment product families, including revenue, bookings, margin, market share, and price realization. Monitor results, identify performance gaps, and implement actions to achieve growth and profitability objectives.
• Develop and maintain portfolio strategies and multi-year product roadmaps that balance customer needs, technology trends, competitive differentiation, financial returns, and business priorities.
• Analyze market conditions, customer applications, competitive offerings, and channel feedback to identify opportunities for new products, enhancements, and portfolio expansion.
• Lead Voice of Customer initiatives through customer engagement, application reviews, and collaboration with Sales, Service, and channel partners. Translate findings into product requirements, value propositions, and commercial objectives.
• Partner with Engineering throughout the new product development process to align technical requirements with customer needs and commercial objectives. Support stage-gate reviews, prioritization, and development decisions.
• Manage lifecycle strategies across equipment, replacement parts, consumables, upgrades, retrofit kits, and service-related offerings, including portfolio rationalization and end-of-life transitions.
• Identify opportunities to expand recurring revenue and installed-base penetration through aftermarket products, upgrades, replacement strategies, and service-related solutions.
• Collaborate with Sales, Service, and Engineering to develop lifecycle offerings that improve equipment performance, customer retention, and lifetime value.
• Develop value-based pricing recommendations using customer value, competitive positioning, product costs, and margin objectives. Monitor pricing effectiveness and recommend adjustments to improve price realization and profitability.
• Partner with Sales, Finance, and Operations to develop forecasts that support business planning, manufacturing requirements, inventory management, and product transitions.
• Drive execution without direct authority.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field.
• 5+ years of experience in Product Management, Product Marketing, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, or similar commercial roles.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results.
• Demonstrated ability to manage products, programs, or portfolios and drive business results.
• Experience with distribution/channel-based businesses.

Core Competencies

• Business Ownership: Takes accountability for portfolio performance and connects product decisions to profitable growth.
• Technical and Application Understanding: Uses air treatment knowledge to evaluate customer needs, guide product decisions, and communicate product value.
• Customer Focus: Understands customer applications and priorities and translates insights into solutions customers value.
• Strategic Thinking: Balances near-term business needs with long-term portfolio direction and investment priorities.
• Cross-Functional Leadership: Builds effective relationships and aligns teams around shared commercial and product objectives.
• Execution: Turns strategy into clear priorities, actionable plans, and measurable results.

Preferences

  • Experience in air treatment, compressed air, filtration, drying technologies, gas generation, or industrial equipment.
  • Experience managing both equipment and aftermarket portfolios, including replacement parts, consumables, upgrades, or service offerings.
  • Experience working with industrial distributors, channel partners, and direct sales teams.
  • Familiarity with stage-gate product development processes and new product commercialization.
  • Experience developing value-based pricing strategies and installed-base growth initiatives.
  • MBA or advanced business degree.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

• This position is based in Charlotte/Davidson, NC (preferred); West Chester, PA; or Ocala, FL.
• Travel expectations to be confirmed.

Pay Range
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $110,000–$130,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicants will be eligible to receive annual incentive compensation.

Location: Bentleyville, PA

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:

The Supplier Quality Engineer III works under limited supervision, responsible for performing a variety of duties efficiently with high-quality results. The Supplier Quality Engineer will be expected to perform duties as Supplier Quality Engineer and Quality Engineer.

Responsibilities:
  • Works under limited supervision to complete tasks in an efficient timeframe with high quality. 
  • Must be a US citizen and able to obtain government security clearance. 
  • Expected to be able to obtain DOD clearance in a reasonable amount of time after being hired.  
  • Read new customer contracts and conduct (commercial and DOD) a peer review of new contracts from a quality / compliance standpoint. ?Review the flow down of customer’s coded notes / standard clauses, that speak to quality requirements. 
  • Compile order control folders to collect required documentation for (lot/heat, NDE and Inspection) certification document retention requirements 
  • Verifies material certificates of conformance are provided and accurate. 
  • Scan and file certificates of conformance on the network using approved file structure. 
  • Receive certificates of conformance and material certifications into database. 
  • Process Quality Notifications for non-conforming material, working with Buyer and Planner to obtain replacement part and/or vendor debit 
  • Detailed writing and issuing of Quality Non-Conformances, Including Root Cause – Corrective Action requests. 
  • First Article Inspection (FAI) documentation 
  • Will work closely with engineering and assembly teams to troubleshoot problems, determine root cause, and create corrective and preventative actions.  
  • Conduct final inspection on all packages to ensure compliance with the customers’ requirements 
  • Process SAP Warehouse Management and Inventory Management transactions accurately. 
  • Place material in storage location in accordance with SAP Warehouse Management location. 
  • Keeps an organized work area by performing various housekeeping and maintenance functions following 5S philosophies. 
  • Follows all safety rules and regulations, environmental regulating procedures and utilizes required safety equipment when appropriate. 
  • Adhere to GD Nash’s ISO 9001-2015 quality system, and Government Contract requirements. 
  • Participate in ISO 9001-2015 audits and any customer required audits 
  • Performs other duties as required. 
  Requirements:

  • High school diploma or trade school graduate 
  • 5+ years of experience in Quality Assurance or Quality Control in an ISO 9001-2015 manufacturing environment. 
  • 5+ years working knowledge of computers, quality inspection, and inventory management. 
  • 5+ years working knowledge of Government Contract requirements related to technical flow downs, including FAR / DFAR regulations and other standard clauses and coded notes. 
  • 5+ years of advance knowledge and understanding of Military Quality / Manufacturing Specifications and Navy Technical Publications including those for Weld and Non-Destructive Testing. 
  • Incumbents must follow all safety rules, environmental procedures and utilize required safety equipment. 
Core Competencies:
  • Working knowledge of Excel, Word, and PowerPoint 
  • Must be able to read and write English, and have basic math competencies including geometry 
  • Must be able to read and interpret manufacturing drawings (including geometric tolerancing and dimensioning), 3D models, and assembly blueprints 
Preferences:

  • Proficient in the use of standard inspection equipment. (Micrometer, caliper, depth gauge, thread gauge, etc. 
  • Able to use advanced inspection equipment (Faro, Romer, Keyence…) 
  • Pulls and stages material in designated staging areas, for both shipping and production use. 
  • Responsible for packaging shipments, this includes the use of nail guns and saw equipment.  
  • Place material in storage location in accordance with SAP Warehouse Management location. 
  • Physically unpacks crates and boxes of incoming parts. 
  • Place material in storage location in accordance with SAP Warehouse Management location. 
  • Material handling abilities on a forklift and overhead cranes. 
  • Working knowledge of Non-Destructive Testing Methods and reviewing reports (PMI, VT, PT) preferred 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 
  • This position may require up to 25% travel to supplier locations for quality audits, inspections, and issue resolution activities.

job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances. 

Job Title: Material Planner / Buyer                    
Location:  Southern Pines, NC
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Keep production moving. Strengthen supplier partnerships. Make an impact where it matters.  Ingersoll Rand is seeking a Material Buyer / Planner to play a key role in keeping production running smoothly at our Southern Pines facility. This dynamic position combines material buying and planning (60%) with production planning (40%), offering the opportunity to directly influence material availability, production schedules, inventory performance, and on-time customer delivery. You'll manage an assigned portfolio of approximately 30–50 suppliers, coordinate purchasing and inbound materials, resolve shortages and delivery challenges, and ensure components are available to support assembly operations and service-parts requirements. You'll also develop production schedules, respond to changing priorities, and collaborate across teams to keep manufacturing on track.

Supporting a diverse range of products—including precision fastening systems, power tools, material-handling equipment, and industrial pumps—you'll use QAD (MFG/PRO) and Excel to analyze material requirements, manage purchasing activity, monitor supplier performance, and identify opportunities to improve inventory efficiency. You'll also help coordinate engineering changes and work closely with Production, Engineering, Customer Service, and Supply Chain leadership. If you enjoy balancing supplier relationships, material planning, and production demands while solving challenges that directly impact manufacturing success, this is an opportunity to make a difference every day.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement & Supplier Management: Perform timely, cost-effective procurement of production materials and inventory. Evaluate requisitions, select approved suppliers, onboard new suppliers, and ensure compliance with purchasing procedures and approval requirements.
  • Production Planning & Scheduling: Analyze production requirements, manufacturing capacity, material availability, and lead times to develop and maintain production schedules, workflow sequences, and resource plans.
  • Material Planning & Inventory Optimization: Maintain material plans to ensure continuity of supply, optimize inventory and safety stock levels, manage SOMI/VMI inventory, and improve working capital through effective replenishment strategies, including Kanban.
  • On-Time Delivery & Order Fulfillment: Maximize On-Time Shipment (OTS) performance by coordinating material deliveries with production schedules, expediting critical requirements, managing shortages, and providing accurate customer promise dates.
  • Supplier Performance & Issue Resolution: Monitor supplier performance, manage delivery exceptions (expedites, de-expedites, and cancellations), resolve invoicing discrepancies, and collaborate with Quality Assurance and Procurement to address supplier-related issues.
  • Forecasting & Supply Coordination: Communicate forecasts and replenishment plans to suppliers, maintain accurate item master lead times, evaluate material and capacity constraints, and coordinate with production planners and cross-functional teams to resolve delivery challenges.
  • Cost Reduction & Continuous Improvement: Identify and implement cost-saving, productivity, and cash flow improvement opportunities. Maintain project pipelines and financial records to track progress against corporate objectives.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration & Leadership: Partner with Production, Procurement, Quality, Accounting, and other functional teams to resolve operational challenges, improve planning and execution, and provide direction to others as needed to achieve organizational objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED
  • 3+ years of experience in material planning, production planning, buying, and/or production / supplier scheduling, and knowledge of supplier processes within a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including proficiency in creating and working with formulas.
  • 1+ year of experience in manufacturing operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.
  • 1+ year of experience using MRP / ERP systems, such as QAD or Oracle.

Core Competencies
  • Materials Buying & Planning: Experience purchasing materials, managing supplier relationships, and ensuring timely material availability to support production requirements.
  • Production Planning & Scheduling: Ability to coordinate production schedules, evaluate material availability, and align inventory with manufacturing demands.
  • ERP / MRP Systems: Experience using ERP/MRP systems to manage purchase orders, inventory, material requirements, and supplier deliveries.
  • Excel & Data Analysis: Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas and data analysis to support purchasing, inventory management, and production planning.
  • Manufacturing or Distribution Operations: Understanding of manufacturing or distribution environments, inventory control, supply chain processes, and on-time delivery requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelor's Degree
  • APICS Certified in Planning and Inventory Management, CPIM, or an equivalent purchasing or supply management certification 
  • Considerable knowledge of industry related supply base.
  • Visual management system experience 
  • Ability to provide direction and training to peers as needed
  • Experience with rate based or flow line (non-MRP) and job shop manufacturing environments

Job Overview:

The Supplier Quality Engineer III works under limited supervision, responsible for performing a variety of duties efficiently with high-quality results. The Supplier Quality Engineer will be expected to perform duties as Supplier Quality Engineer and Quality Engineer.

Responsibilities:
  • Works under limited supervision to complete tasks in an efficient timeframe with high quality. 
  • Must be a US citizen and able to obtain government security clearance. 
  • Expected to be able to obtain DOD clearance in a reasonable amount of time after being hired.  
  • Read new customer contracts and conduct (commercial and DOD) a peer review of new contracts from a quality / compliance standpoint. ?Review the flow down of customer’s coded notes / standard clauses, that speak to quality requirements. 
  • Compile order control folders to collect required documentation for (lot/heat, NDE and Inspection) certification document retention requirements 
  • Verifies material certificates of conformance are provided and accurate. 
  • Scan and file certificates of conformance on the network using approved file structure. 
  • Receive certificates of conformance and material certifications into database. 
  • Process Quality Notifications for non-conforming material, working with Buyer and Planner to obtain replacement part and/or vendor debit 
  • Detailed writing and issuing of Quality Non-Conformances, Including Root Cause – Corrective Action requests. 
  • First Article Inspection (FAI) documentation 
  • Will work closely with engineering and assembly teams to troubleshoot problems, determine root cause, and create corrective and preventative actions.  
  • Conduct final inspection on all packages to ensure compliance with the customers’ requirements 
  • Process SAP Warehouse Management and Inventory Management transactions accurately. 
  • Place material in storage location in accordance with SAP Warehouse Management location. 
  • Keeps an organized work area by performing various housekeeping and maintenance functions following 5S philosophies. 
  • Follows all safety rules and regulations, environmental regulating procedures and utilizes required safety equipment when appropriate. 
  • Adhere to GD Nash’s ISO 9001-2015 quality system, and Government Contract requirements. 
  • Participate in ISO 9001-2015 audits and any customer required audits 
  • Performs other duties as required. 
  Requirements:

  • High school diploma or trade school graduate 
  • 5+ years of experience in Quality Assurance or Quality Control in an ISO 9001-2015 manufacturing environment. 
  • 5+ years working knowledge of computers, quality inspection, and inventory management. 
  • 5+ years working knowledge of Government Contract requirements related to technical flow downs, including FAR / DFAR regulations and other standard clauses and coded notes. 
  • 5+ years of advance knowledge and understanding of Military Quality / Manufacturing Specifications and Navy Technical Publications including those for Weld and Non-Destructive Testing. 
  • Incumbents must follow all safety rules, environmental procedures and utilize required safety equipment. 
Core Competencies:
  • Working knowledge of Excel, Word, and PowerPoint 
  • Must be able to read and write English, and have basic math competencies including geometry 
  • Must be able to read and interpret manufacturing drawings (including geometric tolerancing and dimensioning), 3D models, and assembly blueprints 
Preferences:

  • Proficient in the use of standard inspection equipment. (Micrometer, caliper, depth gauge, thread gauge, etc. 
  • Able to use advanced inspection equipment (Faro, Romer, Keyence…) 
  • Pulls and stages material in designated staging areas, for both shipping and production use. 
  • Responsible for packaging shipments, this includes the use of nail guns and saw equipment.  
  • Place material in storage location in accordance with SAP Warehouse Management location. 
  • Physically unpacks crates and boxes of incoming parts. 
  • Place material in storage location in accordance with SAP Warehouse Management location. 
  • Material handling abilities on a forklift and overhead cranes. 
  • Working knowledge of Non-Destructive Testing Methods and reviewing reports (PMI, VT, PT) preferred 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 
  • This position may require up to 25% travel to supplier locations for quality audits, inspections, and issue resolution activities.

Location: Davidson, NC - 525 Harbour Place Dr. Davidson, NC 28036 (Hybrid)

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Summary:
The Pricing and Tools Manager is responsible for the ongoing ownership, maintenance, enhancement, and support of the CARE Calculator, a Salesforce-based tool supporting service agreement opportunities. This role will serve as the primary business owner for the CARE Calculator, working closely with Salesforce development teams, CARE stakeholders, channel users and sales leadership to ensure the tool remains accurate, effective, scalable, and aligned with evolving business needs. The pricing and tools manager will translate business requirements into actionable enhancements, support the development and testing process, validate and approve changes prior to release, and provide ongoing support to users when questions, issues, or improvement opportunities arise.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the CARE Calculator/CPQ tool, including business rules, calculation logic, data integrity, and roadmap.
  • Prioritize enhancements based on business needs, user feedback, and CARE strategy.
  • Maintain governance, documentation, and standard work for ongoing tool management.
  • Integrate new products, offerings, pricing, and commercial requirements into the tool.
  • Own the quote-to-agreement execution process and drive improvements across the workflow.
  • Align tool changes with Sales, Service, Finance, Pricing, IT, and CARE stakeholders.
  • Troubleshoot tool issues and distinguish training, data, process, and system causes.
  • Translate business needs into clear requirements and acceptance criteria for Salesforce developers.
  • Partner with development on solution design, enhancements, defect resolution, and releases.
  • Lead user acceptance testing, approve changes, and validate post-release performance.
  • Serve as the primary contact for day-to-day questions, issues, and enhancement requests.
  • Communicate launches of new offerings, tool updates, releases, and known issues.
  • Create user guidance, FAQs, training, and release communications.
  • Monitor adoption, accuracy, and recurring support issues to identify improvements.
  • Gather stakeholder feedback and maintain a prioritized enhancement backlog.
  • Simplify workflows, improve usability, and reduce manual effort.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • 3+ years of expereince with analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly with pricing, costing, quoting, or commercial calculation tools.


Core Competencies:

  • Salesforce / CRM knowledge
  • CARE business acumen
  • Analytical problem solving
  • Project and priority management
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Channel/customer orientation
  • Continuous improvement
  • Change management and communication


Preferences:

  • Experience with CARE agreements, aftermarket services, service contracts, or industrial equipment.
  • Knowledge of Salesforce development/enhancement processes.
  • Experience supporting sales or service organizations and distributor/channel partners.
  • Familiarity with pricing models, service agreement costing, profitability, and commercial decision-support tools.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be hybrid with no travel for the role

Job title: Buyer
Location: Springfield, MO (onsite)

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:

The Buyer is an integral part of a dynamic and a highly communicative cross-functional team environment working together to build a seamless supply chain. This position performs duties related to day-to-day inventory replenishment planning and purchasing from multiple vendors (Domestic and International). A Buyer’s primary goal is to ensure the highest level of customer service while achieving high inventory turnover at the lowest total cost. This position will work closely and collaborate with the Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain, Production, Customer Service, Distribution/Operations, Product Management, Accounting and Vendors.

Responsibilities

  • Manage inventory/service level fill rates by maintaining appropriate stock levels- on hand, safety stock, open purchase orders, transfer stock to have the right inventory at the right place at the right time for the customer.
  • Prepare and issue purchase orders according to company purchasing policies and procedures including meeting supplier prepaid freight/PO value minimums and/or maximize container utilization.
  • Confirm purchase order information (price, estimated delivery date, order quantity, unit of measure etc.). Rack all purchase orders and update the estimated delivery date on a real-time basis with Order Acknowledgements
  • Expedite PO’s as needed with various departments and suppliers to ensure material availability.
  • Analyze material availability issues and take immediate corrective action.
  • Maintain and update all relevant planning/MRP data within SAP. Maintain accurate material master, vendor master and purchasing data in SAP.
  • Support the sourcing team and product management team on all product life cycle related issues to include new product launches, transitions and end of life in order to ensure product availability and reduce the likeliness of obsolete inventory.
  • Collaborate/leverage product sourcing team on purchasing activities including, but not limited to, issues related to sourcing, pricing, MOQ (minimum order quantities), vendor dispute resolution, etc.
  • Conduct vendor lead time and performance analysis. Participate in vendor performance review and act as vendor liaison
  • Resolve Accounts Payable issue related to vendor shipping discrepancies, pricing discrepancies etc. using Basware software.
  • Work with the warehouse teams to ensure timely receipts of goods in transit and accurate on-hand inventory records in SAP and reconciliation of receipt discrepancies
  • Source data from multiple sources, prepare reports, and create/utilize planning tools (Excel, Access) to analyze large amounts of data for planning/purchasing activities


Requirements:

  • 3+ years of purchasing experience in manufacturing
  • 3 + years relevant experience in inventory management, purchasing, production planning, can be substituted for degree
  • Prior purchasing experience in a manufacturing environment
  • Ability and willingness to work fully onsite
  • Ability to manage high email volume and multitask quickly in a fast-paced environment
  • ERP systems knowledge required
  • MS office proficiency required, advanced level preferred

Core Competencies:

  • Experience in purchasing products from multiple vendors (Domestic & International)
  • Proven ability to understand best practices:
  • Demand & forecast
  • Purchasing & inventory planning
  • MRP, safety stock, reorder-point, ABC analysis
  • Customer centric team player
  • Ability source data from multiple sources and analyze large amounts of data
  • Ability to collaborate with cross functional teams


Preferences:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred
  • APICS CPIM certification preferred
  • SAP experience preferred


Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to stand/walk/sit for long periods of time.
  • Work environment includes inside and outside of an office environment.
  • Ability to communicate information effectively through oral and written presentation. Can convey detailed instructions to others.
  • Able to operate a computer and other handheld technology devices.


Travel and Work Requirements:
This role is fully onsite based in Springfield, MO

Job Title: Quality Inspector

Location: Milford, NH.

Shift: 6:30AM to 3:30PM Monday thru Friday (occasional Saturday when required)

 

Position Summary:

We are seeking a Mechanical Inspector to join our team! This individual will be responsible for dimensional, visual, and surface finish, inspections of machined parts and assemblies, consisting of first article, in process, and final inspection. Must be detailed orientated in recording all inspections performed accurately and timely, as well as assuring all non-conformance reports are recorded.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Self-motivated, organized individual with ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.
  • Positive attitude with the ability to work with a sense of urgency.
  • Ability to multi-task
  • Time management skills.
  • Demonstrates a strong work ethic, integrity and personal accountability.
  • Must possess excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Interacts with all departments to assure product is correct and on schedule.
  • Commercial Standard Practices apply.
  • First Article, In-Process, and Final Inspection of complex parts and assemblies.
  • Dimensional, visual and surface finish inspection of assemblies, sub-assemblies, finished and semi-finished components, identifying any and all issues with material, workmanship, or process.
  • Mechanical inspection using digital calipers, micrometers, height and depth gages, microscopes, Starrett vision machine, and typical shop gaging. Familiar with the tools and equipment and shall have demonstrated proficiency in their use.
  • Must be able to understand and interpret geometric tolerance.
  • Identify and document non-conforming parts using our ERP system
  • Additional duties as assigned.
  • Programming experience with a Starrett Coordinate Measuring machine a plus.
  • Experience working with revision-controlled drawings.
  • Adherence to safety procedures/guidelines at all times.
  • Capable of determining the calibration status of inspection and measuring equipment is in proper condition for use, and that inspection, examination and test procedures are approved.
  • ERP system usage/knowledge a plus.
  • Ability to evaluate and troubleshoot the process and trends of machined parts and offer suggestions/solutions to continue quality of product.
  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment
 

Physical Requirements:

  • Work is performed in standing position involving some walking, bending, stooping, and handling of material.

    • 05 lbs. constantly

  • Regular exposure to heat, dirt, grease and fumes.
  • Regular exposure to noise levels exceeding 85 db. (hearing protection required when exposure exceeds 85db) 
Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 3 or more years’ experience in a manufacturing quality-controlled environment conducting mechanical inspections to Commercial Standards.
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work order instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials, Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel)

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirement

  • Teamwork

job.title: Machine Operator
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.




Job Summary

Set up and operate a variety of machine tools to produce precision parts. Applies knowledge of mechanics, shop mathematics, metal properties, and machining procedures. Construct, assemble, or rebuild machines, such as blowers, pumps, boosters, and similar equipment used in such industries as transportation, manufacturing or wastewater treatment.

Responsibilities

  • Calculate dimensions and tolerances using knowledge of mathematics and instruments such as micrometers and calipers.
  • Create, utilize and improve Standard Work combinations sheets to document machining and assembly processes to ensure consistency and repeatability.
  • Participate in the 5 Why Process to ensure real time problem solving and drive continuous improvement.
  • Align and secure holding fixtures, cutting tools, attachments, accessories, and materials onto machines.
  • Select the appropriate tools, machines, and materials to be used in preparation of machinery work.
  • Machine parts to specifications using machine tools such as lathes, milling machines, shapers, or grinders.
  • Set up, adjust, and operate all of the basic machine tools and many specialized or advanced variation tools to perform precision machining operations.
  • Measure, examine, and test completed parts to detect defects and ensure conformance to specifications, using precision instruments such as micrometers.
  • Set controls to regulate machining, or enter commands to retrieve, input, or edit computerized machine control media.
  • Position and fasten work pieces.
  • Position and align components for assembly, manually or using hoists.
  • Set and verify parts clearances.
  • Rework, repair, and replace damaged parts or assemblies.
  • Reads, interprets and follows Bill of Material to pull parts for assembly and submits corrections as needed.
  • Assemble units of a variety of sizes and models through use of standard work and interpretation of Engineering controlled documents.
  • Check work pieces to ensure that they are properly lubricated and cooled.
  • Confer with engineering, supervisory, and manufacturing personnel to exchange technical information.
  • Operate equipment to verify operational efficiency.
  • Clean and lubricate machines, tools, and equipment to remove grease, rust, stains, and foreign matter.
  • Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned.

Education Requirements / Certifications

  • 1-2 years’ experience working in a manufacturing environment preferred
  • 1-2 years’ assembly and or CNC machining preferred

Experience / Skill Requirements

  • Mechanical - Knowledge of machines and tools, including their designs, uses, and maintenance.
  • Production and Processing - Knowledge of raw materials, production processes, quality control, costs, and other techniques for maximizing the effective manufacture and distribution of goods.
  • Mathematics - Knowledge of arithmetic and algebra.
  • Operation Monitoring - Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.
  • Quality Control Analysis - Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.
  • Operation and Control - Controlling operations of equipment or systems.
  • Troubleshooting - Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.
  • Equipment Maintenance - Performing routine maintenance on equipment.

Tools/Technology Requirements:

  • Ability to read blueprints, including geometric dimensioning and tolerance.
  • Ability to determine and complete offsets through basic mathematics.

Key Competencies

  • Knowledge of inventory processes.
  • Process driven and systematic in their approach to completing their work.
  • Ability to identify and solve problems.
  • Ability to pass certification for Powered Industrial Vehicle license.

Job Overview:

The Material Control Manager is responsible for the planning, organizing and controlling of the receiving, raw material warehouse, inventory control, and shipping (if applicable) to maximize productivity on assigned shifts and areas.? Prepares schedules for shipping and receiving materials to control flow of goods and regulate warehouse space. ?In addition, this position is accountable for warehouse inventory accuracy and cycle counting routines to drive accurate perpetual records on the material stored in the warehouse.? Also included in the responsibility is the oversight of the shipping department to ensure they follow the guidelines established by the logistics organization.


Responsibilities:

  • Recommend improvements to reduce cost and drive productivity within the department.
  • Design and implement space-efficient warehouse layouts tailored to material needs, improving material flow, reducing handling time, and supporting lean manufacturing principles.
  • Ensure timely unloading, receiving, storage and delivery of material to the production areas.
  • Evaluate demand forecasts and order inputs against production schedules, work orders, and plant capacity to proactively identify workload distribution and ensure alignment between warehousing and manufacturing operations.
  • Maintains inventory and product loss control, coordinates timely and accurate shipping and receiving, and ensures safety/operational guidelines are met.
  • Maintain cycle count standard work goals with the long term objective of achieving cycle count certification

  • Implement and enforce standard work across the functions
  • Drive continuous improvement activities in all functional areas
  • Provide leadership in selecting, developing and evaluating personnel to ensure the efficient operation of the function
  • Manage suppliers and service providers that support receiving, warehousing and shipping functions

  • Organize activities & assigning jobs according to the staff requirements.
  • Works with plant management and other supervisory staff to assign, direct, review and monitor work of supervised staff to maximize productivity warehouse and shipping department.
  • Motivate staff to make an effective and efficient team
  • Engages in the typical responsibilities of a manager requiring planning, evaluating, organizing, integrating and delegating
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Job Title: Assistant Controller
Location: Charleroi, PA

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability.
