Job Overview:
Step into an Assistant Controller role where Finance directly influences the performance of a complex, multi-site manufacturing business. Supporting Ingersoll Rand’s Nash business across three distinct product areas, this position provides financial and commercial oversight of highly engineered solutions serving commercial, industrial, and U.S. Navy applications. Working at the intersection of Finance, Sales, Operations, order management, and project management, the Assistant Controller will turn financial insights into stronger business decisions and improved project outcomes.

The role supports multi-million-dollar, engineer-to-order projects from initial order through final delivery, including percentage-of-completion accounting, revenue recognition, milestone billing, backlog reporting, pricing and quoting, cost of goods sold, working capital, and cash flow. The Assistant Controller will proactively identify and resolve credit and billing blocks, delayed project costs, incomplete job-cost activity, and other obstacles affecting the order-to-cash process. Success requires progressive commercial controllership experience in manufacturing, strong financial and operational acumen, and a clear understanding of how sales orders, project costs, pricing, revenue, inventory, and business performance connect. The ideal candidate is analytical, inquisitive, and proactive, with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable insights, build credibility, and influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.

Offering meaningful ownership and a path toward future Controller responsibility, this role will drive financial process improvements, strengthen business partnerships, and support revenue growth, margin expansion, working capital optimization, and Annual Operating Plan objectives through Ingersoll Rand’s IRX tools and processes.
U.S. citizenship is required due to the position’s involvement with U.S. Navy-related business.

Responsibilities:

Managerial Reporting: Provide insightful month end analytical reporting which delivers context as well as implications of the financial results, trends, risks and opportunities.

  • Examples of key managerial reporting include monthly operating review, weekly shipping trends, order rates, backlog management, and NWC metrics such as inventory performance and contract asset/liability balances.

Control Environment: Champion strong financial controls through strict adherence to all existing SOX narratives and promote a pro-active partnership with both internal and external audit teams in the identification and resolution of current or future gaps. Maintain a strong culture of compliance.

  • Examples of key processes include revenue cut-off, warranty, obsolescence and other valuation reserves, account reconciliations.

Project Accounting (POC / ASC 606): Own revenue recognition for Engineered-to-Order contracts accounted for over time.

Review contracts at order booking to identify performance obligations and confirm over-time criteria (enforceable right to payment, no alternative use).

Lead monthly EAC / estimate-to-complete reviews with project managers and operations, analyzing margin fade/gain and documenting changes in estimates.

Account for contract modifications and change orders, and for variable consideration such as liquidated damages, penalties, and incentives and identify and record loss contract provisions promptly.

Manage contract asset/liability (unbilled / billings in excess) balances, including uninstalled materials and cost-to-cost input exclusions.

Maintain SOX-compliant controls and documentation over POC estimates, and act as primary point of contact for internal and external audit on project accounting.

Forecasting / Budgeting: Support the administration of timely and accurate forecasts of commercial outlooks. Developing close relationships with multiple financial and business stakeholders by assessing risk and opportunities both on the P&L and balance sheet with a key focus on Engineered-to-Order (ETO) projects which operate using percent-of-complete (POC) accounting.

Key forecast deliverables include estimation of revenue, shipments, incorporation of conversion and material price variances as well as direct and indirect spending.

Key budget deliverables include timely development and top line growth expectations and corresponding production and spend data in accordance with corporate guidance

Development and management of financial expectations for POC projects, based on collaborations with operations/project management and historical performance

Liaison to PFT and Corporate leadership: Facilitate timely and appropriate response to requests originating from shared financial service, corporate FP&A, and PFT leadership to ensure optimal business performance.

  • Examples of functional liaison include support for Intercompany Profit elimination, insurance programs, treasury collaboration, managing PD AR via Shared Services, and other initiatives to support business objectives.


Business Partnership: Participation and leadership in business processes such as IRX (Ingersoll Rand Execution Excellence) for the realization of both tactical and strategic objectives. An example of business process leadership includes development and leadership of a swim lane in support of one or more Impact Daily Management teams.

Liaise with plant and cross functional leadership teams to support those functions by providing analytical and business decision support to drive margin expansion, financial forecasts, operating plans, and strategic goals.

Deploy Talent: Foster a work environment that aligns the team in the achievement of corporate objectives while developing personnel, building redundancy, and ensuring business continuity.

  • Examples of team development include succession planning, personnel development plans, engagement enhancement through identification and resolution of potential impediments to progress. The role is a coach and mentor indirect reports (junior finance employee, project mgmt. or other functions/roles to improve financial understanding).


Requirements:

  • B.S. in Accounting, Finance, or related Business Concentrations.
  • 5+ years of progressive commercial controller experience in manufacturing revenue recognition, pricing,
  • 4+ years of work experience within a manufacturing environment.
  • Must be a US Citizen due to the position’s involvement with U.S. Navy-related business


Core Competencies:

  • Ability to drive performance through others and support colleagues in pursuit of the team goal while ensuring a focus on deliverables
  • Effective communication skills, both written and verbal, including the ability to influence and coach teams towards financial objectives.
  • Strong numerical skills, analytical thinking, careful structured approach applying accounting acumen related to a manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with project managers and challenge cost-to-complete estimates.


Preferences:

  • MBA, CMA, CFA, CPA certification.
  • Audit experience (partnering both internally and externally).
  • Experience working with ASC 606 (percent of complete accounting)
  • Familiarity and experience with SAP and HFM


Work and Travel Arrangements:

  • Approximately 5% travel required

You'll play a key role in improving processes, strengthening safety and productivity, and ensuring materials and products move seamlessly through the operation. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact through hands-on leadership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee daily warehouse operations to ensure products are received, stored, and shipped safely, accurately, and efficiently.
  • Enforce OSHA, company, and regulatory safety standards. Conduct safety training, warehouse inspections, incident investigations, and implement corrective actions.
  • Lead, train, coach, and evaluate warehouse personnel. Assign daily tasks, monitor performance, and coordinate staffing and work schedules.

  • 2+ years of experience managing inventory accuracy, cycle counts, and resolving inventory discrepancies.
  • 2+ years of experience applying warehouse safety practices, OSHA regulations, and safe material handling procedures.


Core Competencies

  • Warehouse Operations & Inventory Management
  • Team Leadership & Development
  • Safety Compliance & Risk Management
  • Operational Efficiency & Continuous Improvement


Preferences:

  • Experience monitoring warehouse performance metrics (KPIs), identifying operational improvements, and managing competing priorities.


Travel and Work Arrangements

This role offers the opportunity to develop account management skills and take on broader account responsibilities as experience and capabilities grow.

  • Participation in a structured sales training or development program.
  • Experience preparing or supporting presentations, line reviews, or proposals for external buying teams.

Job Title: Quality Inspector

Location: Milford, NH.

Shift: 6:30AM to 3:30PM Monday thru Friday (occasional Saturday when required)

 

Position Summary:

We are seeking a Mechanical Inspector to join our team! This individual will be responsible for dimensional, visual, and surface finish, inspections of machined parts and assemblies, consisting of first article, in process, and final inspection. Must be detailed orientated in recording all inspections performed accurately and timely, as well as assuring all non-conformance reports are recorded.

  • Positive attitude with the ability to work with a sense of urgency.
  • Ability to multi-task
  • Time management skills.
  • Demonstrates a strong work ethic, integrity and personal accountability.
  • Must possess excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Interacts with all departments to assure product is correct and on schedule.
  • Commercial Standard Practices apply.

  • Dimensional, visual and surface finish inspection of assemblies, sub-assemblies, finished and semi-finished components, identifying any and all issues with material, workmanship, or process.

  • Must be able to understand and interpret geometric tolerance.
  • Identify and document non-conforming parts using our ERP system
  • Additional duties as assigned.

  • Regular exposure to noise levels exceeding 85 db. (hearing protection required when exposure exceeds 85db) 
Qualifications:

  • 3 or more years’ experience in a manufacturing quality-controlled environment conducting mechanical inspections to Commercial Standards.
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses

Title: Welder
Location: West Chester, PA (Zeks Compressed Air - 1302 Goshen Pkwy. West Chester, PA 19380)
Shift: 1st Shift (Monday-Friday 6am-2:30pm)





Position Summary

The Welder is responsible for setting up and operating welding equipment to fabricate, assemble, and repair metal components and structures according to engineering drawings, work instructions, and quality standards. This position plays a key role in ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production while supporting continuous improvement initiatives.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Perform welding operations using MIG, TIG, Flux-Core, Stick, or other welding processes as required.
  • Read and interpret blueprints, engineering drawings, work orders, and welding symbols.
  • Set up welding machines and adjust settings based on material type, thickness, and specifications.
  • Fabricate, assemble, and repair metal parts, components, and structures.
  • Inspect welds for dimensional accuracy, strength, and compliance with quality standards.
  • Use measuring instruments such as tape measures, calipers, squares, and gauges.
  • Operate related equipment including grinders, saws, lifting devices, and other fabrication tools.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area in accordance with company safety policies.
  • Report equipment malfunctions, quality concerns, and safety hazards promptly.
  • Work collaboratively with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, and Production teams to meet production goals.
  • Participate in continuous improvement and lean manufacturing initiatives.
  • Follow all company policies, procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements.

Qualifications Required

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Minimum 1-3 years of welding experience in a manufacturing or fabrication environment.
  • Ability to read blueprints and welding symbols.
  • Knowledge of various welding processes and metal fabrication techniques.
  • Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations and measurements.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, and reach throughout the shift.
  • Ability to lift and move materials up to 50 pounds, with assistance for heavier loads.
  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment with exposure to heat, noise, fumes, and moving equipment.
  • Required use of personal protective equipment (PPE), including welding helmet, safety glasses, gloves, and steel-toed footwear.

Job Title: Quality Inspector

Location: Milford, NH.

Shift: 6:30AM to 3:30PM Monday thru Friday (occasional Saturday when required)

 

Position Summary:

We are seeking a Mechanical Inspector to join our team! This individual will be responsible for dimensional, visual, and surface finish, inspections of machined parts and assemblies, consisting of first article, in process, and final inspection. Must be detailed orientated in recording all inspections performed accurately and timely, as well as assuring all non-conformance reports are recorded.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Self-motivated, organized individual with ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.
  • Positive attitude with the ability to work with a sense of urgency.
  • Ability to multi-task
  • Time management skills.
  • Demonstrates a strong work ethic, integrity and personal accountability.
  • Must possess excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Interacts with all departments to assure product is correct and on schedule.
  • Commercial Standard Practices apply.
  • First Article, In-Process, and Final Inspection of complex parts and assemblies.
  • Dimensional, visual and surface finish inspection of assemblies, sub-assemblies, finished and semi-finished components, identifying any and all issues with material, workmanship, or process.
  • Mechanical inspection using digital calipers, micrometers, height and depth gages, microscopes, Starrett vision machine, and typical shop gaging. Familiar with the tools and equipment and shall have demonstrated proficiency in their use.
  • Must be able to understand and interpret geometric tolerance.
  • Identify and document non-conforming parts using our ERP system
  • Additional duties as assigned.
  • Programming experience with a Starrett Coordinate Measuring machine a plus.
  • Experience working with revision-controlled drawings.
  • Adherence to safety procedures/guidelines at all times.
  • Capable of determining the calibration status of inspection and measuring equipment is in proper condition for use, and that inspection, examination and test procedures are approved.
  • ERP system usage/knowledge a plus.
  • Ability to evaluate and troubleshoot the process and trends of machined parts and offer suggestions/solutions to continue quality of product.
  • Maintain a clean and safe work environment
 

Physical Requirements:

  • Work is performed in standing position involving some walking, bending, stooping, and handling of material.
  • Lifting/pushing/pulling/carrying up to
    • 05 lbs. constantly
    • 35 lbs. frequently
    • 50 lbs. occasionally
  • Hazards are· serious cuts, burns, bruises and possible permanent injury; operator required to wear goggles and heavy gloves. While the job has definite hazards, caution by the operator will reduce hazards to a minimum
  • Regular exposure to heat, dirt, grease and fumes.
  • Regular exposure to noise levels exceeding 85 db. (hearing protection required when exposure exceeds 85db) 
Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 3 or more years’ experience in a manufacturing quality-controlled environment conducting mechanical inspections to Commercial Standards.
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work order instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials, Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirement

  • Fully site based
 

Key Competencies

  • Communication
  • Efficiency
  • Productivity
  • Accuracy
  • Teamwork
  • Integrity
  • Problem Solving
  • Detail Oriented
  • Gauges and Instruments
  • Blueprints

Job title: Lead Operator
Location: Flexan, 4752 West California Avenue, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
Department: Production | Reports to: Production Supervisor | Status: Hourly, non-exempt
Shift: Monday–Thursday, 5:00 AM–3:30 PMy

About Us:

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies — from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powders — to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:

The Lead Operator performs hands-on production work while guiding team members through daily operations. You will operate equipment, support quality and safety standards, train operators and coordinate assignments to help the team meet production goals and complete finished goods.

Responsibilities:

  • Work directly on the production line, operate equipment, verify process settings and support hourly and shift production goals.
  • Coordinate daily assignments and adjust team tasks and resources to meet the production schedule; provide supervisor backup and team communication as needed.
  • Onboard and train employees through on-the-job training in safe work practices, SOPs, standard work and quality expectations.
  • Troubleshoot process issues within approved limits; promptly escalate safety, quality and equipment concerns and support investigations and corrective actions.
  • Verify correct materials and identification; follow traceability, line-clearance and process-control procedures and approved drawings and production packets.
  • Complete production documentation accurately, close work orders and enter ERP data daily.
  • Follow and reinforce cleanroom gowning, contamination control, safety, housekeeping and 5S procedures to maintain an organized and safe workplace.
  • Identify opportunities to improve productivity, quality and waste reduction; recognize performance concerns and communicate them to the supervisor. Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements

  • Read and understand drawings, production packets, SOPs and work instructions.
  • Demonstrate attention to detail, multitasking, problem-solving and fine hand dexterity for handling small parts.
  • Communicate effectively with employees and management, work cooperatively and follow through on assigned tasks.
  • Recognize safety risks and quality concerns; follow approved processes and escalate issues appropriately.
  • Meet the scheduled work hours and maintain dependable attendance.
  • Perform the essential physical duties, with or without reasonable accommodation: frequent standing, walking and reaching; occasional bending, stooping and crouching; extended sitting or standing; lifting 25–50 pounds and push/pull operations on tools up to 75 pounds; and visual inspection of parts using a microscope.

Core Competencies:

  • Hands-on leadership, safety awareness, collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement. Demonstrate ownership, bold aspirations with humility and integrity, commitment to customer success and inspired teamwork.

Preferences:

  • Approximately 1–2 years of leadership experience and 2–3 years of manufacturing experience, as discussed during intake; final classification and flexibility to be aligned with approved compensation.

Travel and Work Arrangements Requirements:

  • Fully on site, approximately 90% at the California Avenue location. Occasional coverage at Medron, 1518 Gladiola Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, approximately 1.2 miles away, generally with about two weeks or more advance notice.
  • Monday–Thursday, 5:00 AM–3:30 PM, with two paid 15-minute breaks and one 30-minute unpaid lunch. Voluntary overtime may include Fridays or Saturdays.
  • Cleanroom environment with required gowning and contamination controls; occasional warehouse work and exposure to moving mechanical parts.
  • No relocation assistance or company vehicle.

Job Title: Operations Manager
Location: Sidney, OH

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview
The Operations Manager is responsible for leading all production operations at the Sidney manufacturing facility, ensuring the safe, efficient, and cost-effective production of power generation products. This role will establish manufacturing systems, develop production teams, and drive operational excellence to achieve world-class performance in safety, quality, delivery, inventory, and productivity. As a key member of the site leadership team, the Operations Manager will play a critical role in facility startup, workforce development, capacity expansion, and implementation of Lean Manufacturing principles to support business growth and customer satisfaction.

Responsibilities
Manufacturing Operations Leadership

  • Lead daily production activities across assembly, test, packaging, and shipping operations.
  • Ensure achievement of plant KPIs related to Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Inventory, and Productivity.
  • Develop and implement production plans that support customer demand and business objectives.
  • Monitor labor utilization, throughput, and capacity while driving operational efficiency improvements.
  • Identify production constraints and implement corrective actions to maximize output and on-time delivery performance.


Site Startup and Growth

  • Support facility startup activities, including equipment commissioning, workforce onboarding, process implementation, and production ramp-up.
  • Establish standard operating procedures, visual management systems, and metrics for operational performance.
  • Partner with Engineering and Supply Chain teams to support new product introduction and capacity expansion initiatives.


Continuous Improvement

  • Lead Lean Manufacturing initiatives, including value stream mapping, kaizen events, waste reduction, and standard work implementation.
  • Drive improvements in productivity, quality, inventory turns, and equipment utilization.
  • Utilize data and operational metrics to identify improvement opportunities and support decision-making.


People Leadership

  • Recruit, develop, and retain a high-performing manufacturing workforce.
  • Coach supervisors and production leaders to improve team effectiveness and accountability.
  • Foster a culture of employee engagement, safety ownership, continuous learning, and operational excellence.


Safety and Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, and company safety requirements.
  • Promote proactive safety behaviors and a zero-injury culture.
  • Lead investigations and corrective actions for safety, quality, or operational incidents.


Requirements

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field required.
  • Minimum 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience within industrial, power generation, electrical equipment, heavy equipment, or engineered-products environments.
  • Minimum 5 years of leadership experience managing production operations and manufacturing teams.
  • Demonstrated success leading operations in a medium-to-large manufacturing site.
  • Experience supporting plant startup, facility expansion, significant production ramp-up, or manufacturing transfers preferred.
  • Experience managing operating budgets and achieving productivity improvements.


Core Competencies

  • Strategic thinking and execution
  • Change leadership
  • Employee development and coaching
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Data-driven decision making
  • Strong communication and problem-solving skills
  • Strong knowledge of:
  • Lean Manufacturing Systems
  • Six Sigma and Continuous Improvement methodologies
  • Capacity and workforce planning
  • Production control and scheduling
  • Quality management systems
  • Material flow and inventory management
  • OSHA and EHS requirements
  • Experience utilizing ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, LN, or similar platforms.


Preferences

  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
  • APICS Certification
  • PMP Certification


Travel & Work Arrangements

  • This position is based on site in Sidney, OH

job.title: Service Technician - Centrifugal
job.description:
Job title: Centrifugal Service Technician
Location: Kansas City, MO; Denver, CO or any major city in the Upper Midwest Region.
Schedule: Monday - Friday, 7:30 AM - 4:30 PM (may vary based on customer and project needs)
Hourly Range: $35.00 - $50.00 weekly, based on experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location. In addition to base pay, Ingersoll Rand offers a comprehensive benefits package, career development opportunities, and company-sponsored training. $3000 Sign On Bonus!

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Centrifugal Service Technician is a highly skilled field-based technical professional responsible for installing, commissioning, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining Ingersoll Rand centrifugal and reciprocating compressor systems. This role primarily supports our Centac® and Turbo Air® product lines, along with dryers, cooling towers, filtration systems, and associated compressed air equipment.
As a trusted technical advisor, you will work directly with customers across a variety of industrial environments, providing hands-on service, start-up support, diagnostics, major overhauls, and technical training. Successful candidates possess strong mechanical and electrical aptitude, excellent customer service skills, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced field service environment.

Responsibilities:
• Install, commission, inspect, troubleshoot, maintain, and repair centrifugal compressors, compressed air systems, and related equipment at customer locations nationwide.
• Perform advanced mechanical, electrical, and controls diagnostics using precision measuring instruments, technical drawings, wiring schematics, and OEM documentation.
• Lead equipment start-ups, major overhauls, upgrades, preventative maintenance, and corrective repairs to maximize equipment reliability and performance.
• Serve as a trusted technical advisor by providing customers with equipment assessments, operational recommendations, technical training, and exceptional service support.
• Accurately document service activities, technical findings, labor, parts usage, expenses, and recommendations while ensuring timely submission of all required reports and records.
• Maintain compliance with all safety standards and customer site requirements while effectively managing travel schedules, customer commitments, and ongoing technical training and development.

Requirements:
• High school diploma or GED required.
• Minimum 3 + years of experience troubleshooting and repairing industrial or commercial mechanical systems.
• Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting skills.
• Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics, and service manuals.
• Experience working independently in customer-facing service environments.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
• Proficiency using Microsoft Office applications, mobile devices, and digital reporting systems.
• Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.

Preferences:

Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of the electronic QMS (e.g., MasterControl) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.


Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., MasterControl), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ/OQ/PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.
  • Support cross-functional and cross-site quality initiatives, special projects, and foster a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.



Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Quality, Life Sciences, or a related technical field
  • 1+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or a similar role within a medical device or regulated manufacturing environment


Preference:

  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements
  • Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as MasterControl or similar preferred
  • Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including development and revision of SOPs, work instructions, validation documents, and quality records
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Lead Auditor Certification is an advantage

About Us:  
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Overview:
Turn Demand into a Plan That Delivers. At Ingersoll Rand, the Master Scheduler connects customer demand with what the factory can deliver—helping ensure the right products move through production at the right time. Your decisions will influence delivery reliability, inventory levels, and how effectively the plant uses its people, materials, and equipment. In this role, you’ll turn business forecasts into a realistic production plan, anticipate bottlenecks, and guide trade-offs as priorities change. You’ll work across Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to balance immediate customer needs with longer-term manufacturing capacity, bringing clarity to competing demands and helping teams act before constraints become disruptions.

This opportunity is ideal for an analytical manufacturing professional who enjoys solving complex problems and influencing decisions across teams. You’ll take ownership of the production plan, work independently, and use data, manufacturing knowledge, and sound judgment to strengthen production flow, improve planning accuracy, and help the factory deliver on its commitments.

Responsibilities:
  • Translate the monthly SIOP consensus plan by product family to a detailed weekly master production schedule (MPS) with a 12-18 month planning horizon into the ERP for weekly MRP generation
  • Incorporate inter-company demand and backlog into SIOP supply planning process to ensure capacity and resources are available to meet demand requirements.
  • Monitor and drive resolution of MRP processing errors.
  • Support customer service with exception request analysis and expediting resolution.
  • Create and publish daily/weekly/monthly factory schedule adherence, capacity, and inventory reports.
  • Serve as a factory subject matter expert (SME) for ERP production planning and scheduling modules.
  • Identification and resolution of Constraints - Capacity, Resource & Material.
  • Facilitates long term capacity assessment (RCCP) and development of countermeasure/action plans.
 
Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in analyzing data relating to product forecasting, master scheduling, or shipment forecasting.
  • Experience with rate-based or flow line (non-MRP) and job shop manufacturing environments.
  • Experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.

Core Competencies:
  • Ability to effectively make complex decisions with limited time and information and can determine decision making criteria based on priorities.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple disciplines with internal and external resources.
  • Strong analytical capabilities, with a basic understanding of statistical analysis techniques.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, independent problem resolution, proven leadership ability, and the ability to manage the requirement of others.
  • Comfortable leading discussion and debate both within peer group and with matrix business partners, operational partners and leaders.

Preferences:
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM) required or hiring commitment to obtain in first 18 months of employment.
  • Experience with visual management systems.
  • Working knowledge of ERP system.
  • Data access/retrieval skills with extensive experience in data analysis, data manipulation using MS Excel and/or other tools as provided.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Onsite.

Location: Charlotte, NC

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
Ready to lead where materials strategy directly impacts customers, operations, and results? As Materials Manager, you will lead an experienced team of Buyer-Planners responsible for purchasing, materials planning, inventory, supplier performance, and aftermarket kit readiness within a complex manufacturing operation. Your leadership will help ensure the right materials are in the right place at the right time—supporting both legacy and next-generation compressor products.

This is more than a scheduling role. You will be the go-to leader when materials issues get difficult—supplier delays, held orders, inventory concerns, source changes, planning gaps, or cross-functional breakdowns. You will dig into root causes, drive solutions, build sustainable processes, and empower your team to prevent issues from recurring. You will also own key materials priorities including inventory performance, on-time delivery, supplier past dues, labor productivity, and continuous improvement, while partnering across Sourcing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Order Management, and Customer Service. With an Oracle-to-SAP transition ahead, you will have a meaningful opportunity to shape processes, strengthen performance, and lead the team through significant operational change.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of people leadership and hands-on materials expertise. You know how to develop talent, establish accountability, and set clear priorities—but you are equally comfortable stepping into the details when the business needs you. Most importantly, you can demonstrate where you have solved complex materials problems, identified root causes, implemented lasting improvements, and measured the results. You bring the technical credibility, analytical mindset, and leadership presence to bring clarity to complexity and turn challenges into sustainable operational improvement.

If you are ready to lead a strong team, solve meaningful operational challenges, and make a measurable impact across the business, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead all site materials management activities, including production scheduling, purchasing, inventory control, material movement, indirect materials, and supplier performance.
  • Drive end-to-end material fulfillment from production planning and procurement through warehousing and product shipment.
  • Implement, sustain, and ensure compliance with Materials and SIOP standard work, processes, and systems.
  • Manage materials, suppliers, and inventory within a Lean Six Sigma manufacturing environment, leveraging MRP to improve flow, availability, and inventory performance.
  • Monitor key materials and supplier performance, identify gaps and root causes, and implement countermeasures that deliver measurable, sustainable improvement.
  • Lead, develop, and organize a team of 12–15 Material Planners/Buyers, including performance management, workload allocation, coaching, succession planning, and professional development.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Sourcing, Engineering, Accounting, Marketing, Operations, Quality, and Global Procurement to support business priorities, supplier selection, and strategic goals.
  • Strengthen supplier relationships and foster a culture of problem solving, accountability, Daily Management, and continuous improvement across the materials organization.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or another relevant discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience in the integrated functions of a manufacturing environment that has embraced lean concepts, MRP manufacturing practices, and progressive supplier relationships.
  • 3+ years in managerial experience focusing on standardizing planning & execution, reducing sourcing complexity, and talent development.
  • 2+ years experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.
  • 1+ years experience with visual management systems.


Core Competencies
Success in this role requires the following core capabilities and demonstrated strengths.

  • Materials Systems & Manufacturing Flow – Strong knowledge of manufacturing material flow and integrated systems supporting materials management, production planning, procurement, and distribution; proficiency with MRP/ERP systems and Microsoft Excel.
  • Leadership & Change Management – Ability to motivate and develop teams, foster collaboration, and lead change while applying Lean methodologies and continuous improvement principles.
  • Problem Solving & Business Impact – Decisive, proactive problem solver who can identify issues, drive solutions, and influence bottom-line results.
  • Communication & Cross-Functional Partnership – Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across functions, support internal customers, and effectively resolve conflict.
  • Execution & Adaptability – Highly organized and able to manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions, and perform effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure manufacturing environment.


Preferences:

  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM)


Travel and Work Arrangements

  • This is an onsite role based from our Distribution and Logistics Center

Aperçu du poste / Job Overview

Le préposé à la manutention / journalier général soutient les activités de production et de logistique d'entrepôt en assurant la réception, le déplacement, l'entreposage et le suivi précis des matériaux. Ce rôle comprend l'utilisation de chariots élévateurs, l'approvisionnement des lignes de production, les comptages d'inventaire et le maintien d'un environnement de travail sécuritaire et efficace.

The Material Handler / General Labourer supports warehouse and production operations by ensuring the efficient movement, storage, and tracking of materials throughout the facility. This role is responsible for receiving inventory, operating forklifts, supplying production lines with materials, conducting inventory counts, and maintaining a safe and organized work environment.

Responsabilités / Responsibilities

  • Recevoir et inspecter les marchandises entrantes, vérifier les quantités et enregistrer les transactions dans le système ERP.
    Receive incoming shipments, verify quantities, inspect for damage, and record transactions in the ERP system.
  • Maintenir l'exactitude de l'inventaire grâce à l'identification, l'étiquetage et l'entreposage adéquats des matériaux.
    Maintain inventory accuracy through proper identification, labeling, and storage practices.
  • Utiliser les chariots élévateurs en toute sécurité pour déplacer, charger, décharger et entreposer les matériaux et produits finis.
    Safely operate forklifts and material handling equipment to move, load, unload, and store materials and finished goods.
  • Préparer et distribuer les pièces et matériaux nécessaires aux activités de production.
    Pick, stage, and deliver materials and components to support production schedules.
  • Effectuer des comptages cycliques et des vérifications d'inventaire afin d'assurer l'exactitude des stocks.
    Perform cycle counts and inventory audits while investigating discrepancies.
  • Maintenir l'organisation de l'entrepôt et soutenir les initiatives d'amélioration continue.
    Support warehouse organization and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Effectuer des tâches générales de nettoyage et d'entretien afin de maintenir un environnement de travail sécuritaire.
    Perform housekeeping and general labour duties to maintain a safe working environment.
  • Respecter les politiques de santé, sécurité, qualité et environnement en tout temps.
    Adhere to all safety, quality, and environmental procedures and policies.

Exigences / Requirements

  • Certificat valide de conduite de chariot élévateur.
    Valid Forklift Operator Certification.
  • Expérience dans un environnement manufacturier, d'entrepôt ou de manutention de matériaux.
    Experience in a warehouse, manufacturing, or material handling environment.
  • Connaissance de base de l'informatique et expérience avec un système ERP ou un logiciel de gestion d'entrepôt.
    Basic computer skills and experience with ERP or warehouse management systems.
  • Grande attention aux détails et exactitude dans les transactions d'inventaire.
    Strong attention to detail and inventory accuracy.
  • Capacité à soulever et déplacer des charges de 50 à 70 lb (23 à 32 kg).
    Ability to lift and move materials weighing 50-70 lbs (23-32 kg).
  • Capacité à travailler debout et à effectuer des tâches physiques durant de longues périodes.
    Ability to stand and perform physical work throughout the workday.
  • Bonne compréhension des pratiques de santé et sécurité au travail.
    Strong understanding of workplace safety procedures.

Compétences clés / Core Competencies

  • Souci du détail / Attention to Detail
  • Contrôle et exactitude de l'inventaire / Inventory Accuracy
  • Sens de la sécurité / Safety Awareness
  • Travail d'équipe / Teamwork & Collaboration
  • Fiabilité et sens des responsabilités / Reliability & Accountability
  • Organisation et gestion du temps / Organization & Time Management
  • Flexibilité et adaptabilité / Adaptability
  • Amélioration continue / Continuous Improvement

Qualifications souhaitées / Preferences

  • Expérience avec SAP, Oracle, NetSuite ou tout autre système ERP ou WMS.
    Experience with SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or similar ERP/WMS systems.
  • Expérience dans les secteurs manufacturier, d'assemblage, de distribution ou d'entreposage.
    Experience in manufacturing, assembly, distribution, or warehouse operations.
  • Expérience en comptages cycliques et rapprochement d'inventaire.
    Experience performing cycle counts and inventory reconciliation.
  • Connaissance des principes Lean Manufacturing ou d'amélioration continue.
    Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement practices.
  • Bilinguisme français/anglais considéré comme un atout.
    Bilingual French/English skills are considered an asset.

Job Title: Materials Manager            
Location:  Charlotte, NC 
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Ready to lead where materials strategy directly impacts customers, operations, and results?  As Materials Manager, you will lead an experienced team of Buyer-Planners responsible for purchasing, materials planning, inventory, supplier performance, and aftermarket kit readiness within a complex manufacturing operation. Your leadership will help ensure the right materials are in the right place at the right time—supporting both legacy and next-generation compressor products.

This is more than a scheduling role. You will be the go-to leader when materials issues get difficult—supplier delays, held orders, inventory concerns, source changes, planning gaps, or cross-functional breakdowns. You will dig into root causes, drive solutions, build sustainable processes, and empower your team to prevent issues from recurring. You will also own key materials priorities including inventory performance, on-time delivery, supplier past dues, labor productivity, and continuous improvement, while partnering across Sourcing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Order Management, and Customer Service. With an Oracle-to-SAP transition ahead, you will have a meaningful opportunity to shape processes, strengthen performance, and lead the team through significant operational change.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of people leadership and hands-on materials expertise. You know how to develop talent, establish accountability, and set clear priorities—but you are equally comfortable stepping into the details when the business needs you. Most importantly, you can demonstrate where you have solved complex materials problems, identified root causes, implemented lasting improvements, and measured the results. You bring the technical credibility, analytical mindset, and leadership presence to bring clarity to complexity and turn challenges into sustainable operational improvement.

If you are ready to lead a strong team, solve meaningful operational challenges, and make a measurable impact across the business, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities: 
  • Lead all site materials management activities, including production scheduling, purchasing, inventory control, material movement, indirect materials, and supplier performance.
  • Drive end-to-end material fulfillment from production planning and procurement through warehousing and product shipment.
  • Implement, sustain, and ensure compliance with Materials and SIOP standard work, processes, and systems.
  • Manage materials, suppliers, and inventory within a Lean Six Sigma manufacturing environment, leveraging MRP to improve flow, availability, and inventory performance.
  • Monitor key materials and supplier performance, identify gaps and root causes, and implement countermeasures that deliver measurable, sustainable improvement.
  • Lead, develop, and organize a team of 12–15 Material Planners/Buyers, including performance management, workload allocation, coaching, succession planning, and professional development.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Sourcing, Engineering, Accounting, Marketing, Operations, Quality, and Global Procurement to support business priorities, supplier selection, and strategic goals.
  • Strengthen supplier relationships and foster a culture of problem solving, accountability, Daily Management, and continuous improvement across the materials organization.

Requirements: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or another relevant discipline. 
  • 5+ years of experience in the integrated functions of a manufacturing environment that has embraced lean concepts, MRP manufacturing practices, and progressive supplier relationships. 
  • 3+ years in managerial experience focusing on standardizing planning & execution, reducing sourcing complexity, and talent development. 
  • 2+ years experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes. 
  • 1+ years experience with visual management systems. 

Core Competencies
Success in this role requires the following core capabilities and demonstrated strengths. 
  • Materials Systems & Manufacturing Flow – Strong knowledge of manufacturing material flow and integrated systems supporting materials management, production planning, procurement, and distribution; proficiency with MRP/ERP systems and Microsoft Excel.
  • Leadership & Change Management – Ability to motivate and develop teams, foster collaboration, and lead change while applying Lean methodologies and continuous improvement principles.
  • Problem Solving & Business Impact – Decisive, proactive problem solver who can identify issues, drive solutions, and influence bottom-line results.
  • Communication & Cross-Functional Partnership – Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across functions, support internal customers, and effectively resolve conflict.
  • Execution & Adaptability – Highly organized and able to manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions, and perform effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure manufacturing environment.

Preferences: 
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM)

Travel and Work Arrangements  
  • This is an onsite role based from our Distribution and Logistics Center

Job Title: Sr. Molding Engineer (LSR and HCR molding)

Location: Lincolnshire, IL

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Overview:
The Molding Engineer is responsible for the development, optimization and sustaining robust molding processes for liquid silicone rubber (LSR) and high consistency rubber (HCR) utilizing injection, transfer and compression molding processes.

The Molding Engineer plays a key role in driving process capability, optimizing cycle times, reducing scrap, troubleshooting production issues and ensuring stable manufacturing performance across all molding work centers.

The Molding Engineer collaborates closely with the Tooling, Production, Quality, NPI and Maintenance teams to ensure successful product launches, consistent quality and efficient manufacturing processes.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop, validate, and optimize LSR and HCR molding processes (injection, compression, transfer) using scientific molding principles and DOE methodologies.
  • Establish robust process parameters, including injection/fill profiles, pack/hold strategies, cure cycles, and thermal controls to improve capability (Cp/Cpk) and reduce variation.
  • Troubleshoot complex molding defects (flash, short shots, voids, knit lines, shrinkage, dimensional variation, and cure issues) using structured root cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Partner with tooling and maintenance teams to qualify molds, optimize gate/vent designs, improve thermal management, and ensure validated equipment performance.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, scrap minimization, OEE improvement, material yield optimization, and Lean/Kaizen implementation.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) through feasibility assessments, mold trials, process qualification, production launch, and transition to manufacturing.
  • Develop and maintain process documentation, standardized parameter sheets, work instructions, and SPC-based process monitoring while training operators and technicians on best practices.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Production, Quality, and Estimating teams to improve manufacturability, manage process changes, and ensure quality, customer, and business objectives are achieved.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in an Engineering (Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, Plastics, Polymer)
  • 5+ years’ direct experience in silicone and/or rubber molding


Competences:

  • Liquid Silicone Rubber (LSR) injection.
  • High Consistency Rubber (HCR) molding.
  • Compression and transfer molding.
  • Cure cycles, post-cure and material behavior.
  • Tool design elements (cavitation, gating, venting, steel types).
  • Experience using DOE, SPC and statistical tools for process improvement.
  • Strong ability to interpret engineering drawings, GD & T, CAD models, customer and regulatory specifications.
  • Demonstrated success in troubleshooting complex molding issues.


Preferences:

  • Experience with SolidWorks or other 3D modelling software.
  • Experience with mold flow analysis (or ability to interpret results).
  • Background in medical, automotive, aerospace or industrial silicone components.
  • Experience supporting APQP, PPAP and customer audits.
  • Experience with automation, vision inspection and deflashing /trimming technologies.
  • Background with adhesion/bonding techniques, multi-shot molding and over molding.
  • RJG/Paulson certification or silicone-specific molding training.
  • Familiarity with ISO13485 and clean room procedures would be beneficial.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Fully onsite based - Lincolnshire, IL

At Ingersoll Rand, the Master Scheduler connects customer demand with what the factory can deliver—helping ensure the right products move through production at the right time. Your decisions will influence delivery reliability, inventory levels, and how effectively the plant uses its people, materials, and equipment. In this role, you’ll turn business forecasts into a realistic production plan, anticipate bottlenecks, and guide trade-offs as priorities change. You’ll work across Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to balance immediate customer needs with longer-term manufacturing capacity, bringing clarity to competing demands and helping teams act before constraints become disruptions.

This opportunity is ideal for an analytical manufacturing professional who enjoys solving complex problems and influencing decisions across teams. You’ll take ownership of the production plan, work independently, and use data, manufacturing knowledge, and sound judgment to strengthen production flow, improve planning accuracy, and help the factory deliver on its commitments.

Responsibilities:
  • Translate the monthly SIOP consensus plan by product family to a detailed weekly master production schedule (MPS) with a 12-18 month planning horizon into the ERP for weekly MRP generation
  • Incorporate inter-company demand and backlog into SIOP supply planning process to ensure capacity and resources are available to meet demand requirements.
  • Monitor and drive resolution of MRP processing errors.
  • Support customer service with exception request analysis and expediting resolution.
  • Create and publish daily/weekly/monthly factory schedule adherence, capacity, and inventory reports.
  • Serve as a factory subject matter expert (SME) for ERP production planning and scheduling modules.
  • Identification and resolution of Constraints - Capacity, Resource & Material.
  • Facilitates long term capacity assessment (RCCP) and development of countermeasure/action plans.
 
Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in analyzing data relating to product forecasting, master scheduling, or shipment forecasting.
  • Experience with rate-based or flow line (non-MRP) and job shop manufacturing environments.
  • Experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.

Core Competencies:
  • Ability to effectively make complex decisions with limited time and information and can determine decision making criteria based on priorities.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple disciplines with internal and external resources.
  • Strong analytical capabilities, with a basic understanding of statistical analysis techniques.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, independent problem resolution, proven leadership ability, and the ability to manage the requirement of others.
  • Comfortable leading discussion and debate both within peer group and with matrix business partners, operational partners and leaders.

Preferences:
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM) required or hiring commitment to obtain in first 18 months of employment.
  • Experience with visual management systems.
  • Working knowledge of ERP system.
  • Data access/retrieval skills with extensive experience in data analysis, data manipulation using MS Excel and/or other tools as provided.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Onsite.

Job Title: Industrial Integration Specialist - IoT

Location: Remote, US

About Us
Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry's most difficult problems.

EcoPlant is our pioneering SaaS technology division and is at the forefront of innovation. Harnessing the power of Internet of Things (IoT) technology and predictive analytics, we seamlessly automate air compressor systems, elevating energy efficiency, boosting system reliability, and enhancing off-site productivity. We're leading the charge in a sustainable industrial revolution, where cutting-edge technology meets eco-friendly solutions, transforming the very essence of how factories operate.

Job Overview:
There's a sustainability movement underway in manufacturing that leverages control systems to proactively monitor mission-critical equipment, evaluating and improving efficiency while predicting and preventing downtime and equipment failures. If you're looking to be at the leading edge of that progress, we're seeking a technically skilled and self-driven IoT Field Engineer to join our growing EcoPlant deployment team.

As an Industrial Integration Specialist - IoT, you will own the on-site installation and commissioning of EcoPlant hardware, ensuring each system is properly installed, connected, and communicating data before you leave the customer site. A strong mechanical and technical aptitude, as well as familiarity with computers and networking fundamentals, and the ability to work independently and resolve issues on your own, is necessary in this position as you will frequently be the sole Ecoplant representative on-site.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the On-Site Installation: Take ownership of each EcoPlant installation, delivering high-quality workmanship that performs reliably in demanding industrial environments. You will frequently work independently as the on-site EcoPlant representative.
  • Install Instrumentation and Sensors: Install the field instrumentation that feeds data to the EcoPlant platform, including air sensors and power monitoring equipment. Terminate and land wiring to its respective locations in accordance with provided documents for Ethernet, Modbus, discrete I/O, etc., while maintaining clean connections and reliable signal integrity.
  • Deploy Edge Hardware: Mount and install edge devices, provision power, and position cellular antennas for optimal signal quality,
  • Commission and Verify Connectivity: Configure network settings, confirm each device is communicating as expected, validate that data is flowing into the platform, and coordinate with technical support to resolve any connectivity issues prior to site departure.
  • Maintain Documentation: Produce accurate records, redlines, and photographs to support the development and maintenance of each site’s P&ID and system diagram.
  • Adhere to Safety Standards: Follow site and standard electrical safety practices, including lockout/tagout (LOTO) and appropriate PPE, when working around energized equipment and pressurized compressed air systems.


Requirements

  • High School Diploma and/or combination of education
  • 2+ years’ related industrial controls installation experience required.
  • 2+ years’ experience deploying IoT and/or edge hardware in industrial environments.



Core Competencies:

  • Demonstrated mechanical and technical aptitude, with the ability to work hands-on and reason through how systems integrate. Relevant experience may come from field service, a technical degree, and/or substantial hands-on technical experience.
  • Familiarity with computers and networking fundamentals, including configuring network interfaces (i.e. understanding of how IP addressing/subnetting works), and basic Linux/ Windows command-line navigation.
  • Demonstrated understanding of IoT communication protocols (such as Modbus, CANbus, Profibus, and discrete I/O), networking, and data security.
  • Ability to read and work from schematics, P&IDs, and wiring diagrams, including terminating and landing wiring to terminals per drawings.
  • Understanding of network communications and protocols, switches, routers, and mobile equipment.
  • Electrical troubleshooting experience and comfort working with low-voltage control wiring.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and resolve issues independently in the field.
  • Exceptional customer service skills coupled with the ability to work collaboratively with internal teams to achieve a shared mission.
  • Proven ability to work independently — self-driven, organized, and able to manage an installation from start to finish with minimal supervision.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Physical demands: This position requires working in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, heights, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage). This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling. It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.


Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related technical field, such as Engineering or Engineering Technology.
  • Experience with industrial compressed air systems.
  • A genuine interest in developing technically within the industrial automation and IoT space.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position is eligible for remote work in the continental United States.
  • Interested candidates should have access to a major airport for travel.
  • Extensive travel across North America required (up to 75%)


Pay Range
The total pay range for this role is $85,000 - $100,000. The actual pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Job Overview:
The Engineering Technician provides hands-on support for silicone molding and manufacturing engineering activities within a regulated medical device environment. With a primary focus on LSR injection molding, and additional support for compression molding, transfer molding, transfer injection molding, and extrusion operations, this role assists with process development, mold trials, validations, equipment qualification, troubleshooting, data collection, and continuous improvement initiatives. The Engineering Technician works closely with Engineering, Tooling, Maintenance, Quality, and Production teams to develop, optimize, and sustain manufacturing processes while supporting new product introductions and ongoing production.

Responsibilities:

  • Support process development for LSR injection molding, compression molding, transfer molding, transfer injection molding, extrusion, assembly, and secondary operations, including equipment setup and operation.

  • Assist with equipment and tooling installation, startup, qualification, maintenance, and repairs; support mold disassembly, cleaning, inspection, reassembly, and equipment improvements.
  • Perform dimensional inspections, engineering testing, and sample evaluations using precision measurement equipment; prepare samples, document results, and support gauge, fixture, and measurement system evaluations.

  • Associate degree in Engineering Technology, Manufacturing Technology, Industrial Technology, or related field preferred; equivalent manufacturing experience considered.

Job Overview:

The Product Development Engineer II is a mid-level engineer who independently researches, designs, tests, and develops pump products and systems. This role applies engineering expertise to solve moderately complex problems, evaluates design factors for performance and cost, and utilizes simulations and analysis tools to optimize solutions. The Engineer II collaborates closely with cross-functional teams, prepares technical documentation and reports, and ensures products meet quality and reliability standards. This position also supports project management activities and may provide technical guidance to less experienced engineers. Independently researches, designs, tests, and develops products and systems, applying engineering principles to solve moderately complex problems. Contributes technical expertise to projects and collaborates with cross-functional teams to ensure product performance and quality.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the development of conceptual and detailed product specifications for pump products based on performance data and customer requirements.
  • Evaluate design factors such as function, materials, performance, cost, efficiency, and compliance with contractual obligations.
  • Apply scientific analysis and mathematical modeling to predict and assess design outcomes and alternatives.
  • Interpret and validate test results, conduct failure analysis, and recommend qualification procedures to ensure product reliability and safety.
  • Utilize simulations and predictive models to verify and optimize design concepts.
  • Provide technical guidance and documentation for engineering teams, ensuring adherence to standards and best practices.
  • Prepare and review technical reports, procedures, and customer proposals.
  • Manage project milestones, cost, and schedule, implementing corrective actions as needed.
  • Identify and resolve design errors and deficiencies, recommending revisions and improvements.
  • Mentor junior engineers and share specialized knowledge with colleagues.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline from an accredited institution.
  • 4+ years of relevant engineering experience minimum, preferably in pump design, fluid handling, or related mechanical systems.

Preferences:

  • Proficiency in engineering design tools (such as SolidWorks, AutoCAD, or similar) and experience with simulation or analysis software.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently execute engineering tasks and contribute to cross-functional projects.
  • Experience with product testing, troubleshooting, and documentation.
  • Experience with FEA/FEM software solutions for electromagnetic, computational fluid dynamics, and static and dynamic mechanical simulation preferred
  • Certifications such as PMP or Six Sigma are a plus.
  • Self-driven & organized: proactive, strong prioritization/multitasking, communicates with urgency.

  • Communication & presentations: excellent written/verbal skills and ability to deliver impactful product presentations.
  • Analytical problem-solver: strong problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.
  • Technical engineering depth: strong engineering fundamentals, mechanical comprehension, fluid power (hydraulics/pneumatics/electromechanical), prototype development/testing.
  • Collaborative leadership: leads through influence, works effectively through others, manages cross-functional teams; manufacturing processes/materials knowledge.

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Overview:
Ready to lead where materials strategy directly impacts customers, operations, and results?  As Materials Manager, you will lead an experienced team of Buyer-Planners responsible for purchasing, materials planning, inventory, supplier performance, and aftermarket kit readiness within a complex manufacturing operation. Your leadership will help ensure the right materials are in the right place at the right time—supporting both legacy and next-generation compressor products.

This is more than a scheduling role. You will be the go-to leader when materials issues get difficult—supplier delays, held orders, inventory concerns, source changes, planning gaps, or cross-functional breakdowns. You will dig into root causes, drive solutions, build sustainable processes, and empower your team to prevent issues from recurring. You will also own key materials priorities including inventory performance, on-time delivery, supplier past dues, labor productivity, and continuous improvement, while partnering across Sourcing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Order Management, and Customer Service. With an Oracle-to-SAP transition ahead, you will have a meaningful opportunity to shape processes, strengthen performance, and lead the team through significant operational change.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of people leadership and hands-on materials expertise. You know how to develop talent, establish accountability, and set clear priorities—but you are equally comfortable stepping into the details when the business needs you. Most importantly, you can demonstrate where you have solved complex materials problems, identified root causes, implemented lasting improvements, and measured the results. You bring the technical credibility, analytical mindset, and leadership presence to bring clarity to complexity and turn challenges into sustainable operational improvement.

If you are ready to lead a strong team, solve meaningful operational challenges, and make a measurable impact across the business, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities: 
  • Lead all site materials management activities, including production scheduling, purchasing, inventory control, material movement, indirect materials, and supplier performance.
  • Drive end-to-end material fulfillment from production planning and procurement through warehousing and product shipment.
  • Implement, sustain, and ensure compliance with Materials and SIOP standard work, processes, and systems.
  • Manage materials, suppliers, and inventory within a Lean Six Sigma manufacturing environment, leveraging MRP to improve flow, availability, and inventory performance.
  • Monitor key materials and supplier performance, identify gaps and root causes, and implement countermeasures that deliver measurable, sustainable improvement.
  • Lead, develop, and organize a team of 12–15 Material Planners/Buyers, including performance management, workload allocation, coaching, succession planning, and professional development.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Sourcing, Engineering, Accounting, Marketing, Operations, Quality, and Global Procurement to support business priorities, supplier selection, and strategic goals.
  • Strengthen supplier relationships and foster a culture of problem solving, accountability, Daily Management, and continuous improvement across the materials organization.

Requirements: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, or another relevant discipline. 
  • 5+ years of experience in the integrated functions of a manufacturing environment that has embraced lean concepts, MRP manufacturing practices, and progressive supplier relationships. 
  • 3+ years in managerial experience focusing on standardizing planning & execution, reducing sourcing complexity, and talent development. 
  • 2+ years experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes. 
  • 1+ years experience with visual management systems. 

Core Competencies
Success in this role requires the following core capabilities and demonstrated strengths. 
  • Materials Systems & Manufacturing Flow – Strong knowledge of manufacturing material flow and integrated systems supporting materials management, production planning, procurement, and distribution; proficiency with MRP/ERP systems and Microsoft Excel.
  • Leadership & Change Management – Ability to motivate and develop teams, foster collaboration, and lead change while applying Lean methodologies and continuous improvement principles.
  • Problem Solving & Business Impact – Decisive, proactive problem solver who can identify issues, drive solutions, and influence bottom-line results.
  • Communication & Cross-Functional Partnership – Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across functions, support internal customers, and effectively resolve conflict.
  • Execution & Adaptability – Highly organized and able to manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions, and perform effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure manufacturing environment.

Preferences: 
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM)

Travel and Work Arrangements  
  • This is an onsite role based from our Distribution and Logistics Center

Location: U.S. Remote - prefer Central Midwest region

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability.
