Job Overview:

The Connected Manufacturing & Field Service Engineer plays a critical role in supporting, integrating, and optimizing Precision Fastening Tools, Controllers, and Connected Manufacturing solutions within customer production environments. This position serves as the technical liaison between customers, service teams, and engineering organizations, ensuring reliable operation, seamless system integration, and exceptional customer satisfaction.

The engineer will be responsible for installation, commissioning, troubleshooting, testing, and support of fastening systems and related manufacturing technologies. This includes integration with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), PLCs, industrial networks, and digital I/O interfaces.

Through direct customer engagement and hands-on technical expertise, the Connected Manufacturing & Field Service Engineer helps drive operational excellence, product reliability, and continuous improvement while supporting Ingersoll Rand's commitment to making life better through innovative manufacturing solutions.

Responsibilities

Connected Manufacturing & Systems Integration

  • Ensure reliable wired & wireless communication between fastening tools and controllers.
  • Support integration & troubleshooting of communication between IR products and plant MES systems using open protocols like Power Focus Open Protocol (PFOP) and ToolsNet, and proprietary protocols for Ford, Volkswagen, Toyota, Stellantis and more.
  • Verify traceability, production reporting, recipe management, and quality data collection requirements.
  • Collaborate with customer automation, IT, quality, and manufacturing engineering teams to ensure reliable system performance.
  • Support Industry 4.0 and Smart Factory initiatives through deployment of connected manufacturing solutions.


Field Service & Customer Support

  • Travel to customer facilities to install, commission, maintain, and troubleshoot precision fastening systems, controllers, and software solutions.
  • Provide onsite and remote technical support for customers, distributors, and internal service teams.
  • Diagnose and resolve software, hardware, networking, and process-related issues in production environments.
  • Conduct equipment assessments and recommend corrective actions to improve system performance and uptime.
  • Deliver customer training on product operation, software functionality, troubleshooting, and best practices.
  • Support production launch activities and ensure successful implementation of connected manufacturing solutions.

Digital I/O & Automation Support

  • Configure and troubleshoot digital I/O communications between fastening controllers, PLCs, conveyors, robots, and automation equipment.
  • Verify machine interlocks, cycle complete signals, fault outputs, part-present inputs, and process control functions.
  • Support industrial communication protocols including Ethernet/IP, Profinet, Modbus, and OPC-UA.
  • Assist with factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), and production startup support.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify recurring field issues and provide feedback to engineering and product management teams.
  • Support the development of service procedures, technical documentation, and best practices.
  • Stay current on manufacturing technology trends, industrial automation, and connected factory solutions.
  • Mentor service technicians and junior engineers as needed.


Qualifications:

  • 5+ Years of experience with MES with power tools communicating with PFOP
  • 5+ Years of experience with Digital I/O configuration and troubleshooting
  • 5+ Years of experience with Fieldbus communications with Profinet or EthernetIP
  • 5+ Years of experience with Software installation and validation
  • 5+ Years of experience with Configuring devices for Wi-Fi communications & troubleshooting


Core Competencies:

  • Strong customer-facing communication skills
  • Ability to characterize, diagnose and resolve complex technical issues
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills
  • Self-motivated and capable of working independently
  • Effective collaboration across engineering, service, and customer teams
  • Willingness to travel extensively to support customer operations


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Joints, fasteners, power tools
  • Must be very comfortable with customer interaction! Will have a sales incentive bonus.
  • Exposure to industrial automation with OPC-UA, MES and Fieldbus protocols
  • Experience with devices communicating over Zigbee or 802.15.4
  • Experience with mobile app communications with devices over BLE or USB


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Regular Travel by car and plane to our customer sites in the US and Canada. Must have a valid passport or ability to get one. You will be provided with a company vehicle.

Job Title:
Industrial Equipment Assembler

Location:

Ivyland, PA

About Us:

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems.

Job Summary:

We are currently seeking a reliable and motivated individual to join our YZ Assembly team. This role will be responsible for assembling, inspecting, and packaging products on an assembly line or independently in a manufacturing facility. A YZ Assembler works with a team to ensure the efficient and accurate assembly of products while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is consistent, a team player, a great communicator, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

Responsibilities:


Assembly:

  • Assemble components and parts following detailed instructions
  • Read and understand the bill of materials and work order instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Complete assembly tasks, use various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses (may use cranes and hoists); Responsibilities may also include specialized work such as tube bending and soldering
  • Stay updated on changes in assembly processes and product specifications
  • Meet or exceed production targets and quotas
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets

Quality Control:

  • Inspect finished products for quality and adherence to specifications
  • Test and troubleshoot assemblies
  • Perform quality checks by established quality procedures and ISO requirements
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the assembly process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality

Inventory Management:

  • Monitor and request materials and components as needed for assembly
  • Keep track of inventory levels and report shortages

Training and Development:

  • Participate in training programs to improve assembly skills and product knowledge
  • Attend monthly EHS trainings
  • Follow all policies and procedures (i.e. report on time and ready to work - Start/Lunch/Breaks)

Safety Compliance:

  • Follow all safety guidelines, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Report any safety hazards or incidents to supervisors promptly.
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000

Cleanliness and Organization:

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Follow 5S principles (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain)

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 0 – 2 years’ experience in assembly or other fast paced operations, preferred
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Fully site based
  • Climate controlled manufacturing plant
  • Protective eyewear and footwear required

Key Competencies:

  • Communication
  • Efficiency
  • Productivity
  • Accuracy
  • Teamwork
  • Integrity
  • Problem Solving
  • Decision Making
  • Detail Oriented
  • Results Driven
  • Documentation
  • Adaptability

An Engineering Technician is crucial in running lab tests and technical evaluations in the research department. They are responsible for assisting with product testing and maintaining engineering lab equipment and calibration.

Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineers, designers, and project managers, to achieve project objectives.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in industrial maintenance, automotive, or rotary machinery

  • Knowledge and experience with basic hand tools

  • Ability to build, operate, and test industrial equipment
  • Mechanical aptitude

  • Writing
  • Troubleshooting/Problem Solving
  • Self-Discipline
  • Attention to Detail


Preferneces

  • Technical degree preferred

  • This position will be based at our offices in Quincy, IL, with minimal anticipated travel less than 10% expected (primarily domestic to Ingersoll Rand testing and manufacturing facilities).

job.description:

Job Title: Plant Controller
Location: Sidney, OH

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview
Lead Financial Performance. Help Shape What Comes Next. Join LeROI, an Ingersoll Rand Center of Excellence for gas compression technology, manufacturing compressors and packaged solutions for the Oil & Gas and Biogas industries. We’re seeking an experienced Plant Controller to lead all aspects of plant finance at our Sidney facility during a significant period of growth. With revenue expected to more than double, new product lines planned, and a proposed facility expansion, you’ll help guide growth while strengthening the existing operation.

In this highly visible, hands-on role, you’ll develop the finance team and partner directly with plant leadership, Operations, and Materials to strengthen financial discipline and improve manufacturing performance. You’ll go beyond reporting results to understand what drives them—and turn those insights into action. Strong accounting and manufacturing finance expertise, attention to detail, and sound business judgment will help you identify risks, challenge assumptions, and uphold GAAP, internal controls, and reporting standards. You’ll thrive here with intellectual curiosity, an ownership mindset, and the agility to learn quickly and navigate changing priorities. An experienced Finance Leader who previously held the role will provide hands-on transition guidance.

Help shape the financial direction of a growing manufacturing operation—and expand your leadership impact.

Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Business Partnership:

  • Lead, develop, and manage the Sidney finance team.
  • Serve as the primary financial business partner to plant leadership, providing financial insight and recommendations to support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, Commercial, and other functions to drive business performance.
  • Provide clear and actionable analysis of financial results, risks, and opportunities.
  • Support and challenge the organization to achieve financial and operational commitments.

Accounting, Reporting & Controls:

  • Lead the monthly financial close and reporting process, ensuring timely and accurate results.
  • Oversee journal entries, account reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP, SOX requirements, company policies, and internal controls.
  • Lead and coordinate site activities related to internal and external audits.
  • Maintain strong financial controls and proactively identify opportunities to strengthen processes and reduce risk.

Planning & Financial Analysis:

  • Lead development of the facility's Annual Operating Plan (AOP), as well as monthly and quarterly forecasting processes.
  • Analyze financial and operational performance against plan, forecast, and prior periods.
  • Identify key drivers of performance, including manufacturing and plant variances, and partner with operational leaders to understand root causes and implement corrective actions.
  • Provide financial modeling and analysis to support business decisions and continuous improvement initiatives.

Cost Accounting & Inventory:

  • Provide leadership and oversight of plant cost accounting activities.
  • Lead the annual standard cost process and ensure accurate product costing.
  • Establish standard costs for new parts and review proposed cost changes for existing products.
  • Monitor and analyze material, labor, overhead, purchase price, and other manufacturing variances.
  • Lead quarterly excess and obsolete inventory reviews and work with cross-functional teams to proactively manage inventory exposure.

Capital & Asset Management:

  • Provide financial oversight of capital expenditures, including business case analysis, spending controls, and project tracking.
  • Oversee fixed asset accounting and ensure appropriate capitalization and asset controls.
  • Partner with plant leadership to prioritize investments and evaluate financial returns.

Continuous Improvement:

  • Identify opportunities to improve financial processes, reporting, controls, and business intelligence.
  • Drive standardization, simplification, and automation where appropriate.
  • Support ad-hoc financial analysis and business initiatives as needed.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • 7+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including increasing responsibility for month-end close, financial reporting, U.S. GAAP compliance, and internal controls.
  • 3+ years of accounting or finance experience in a plant or manufacturing environment, including direct partnership with Operations, Materials, Production, or Supply Chain.
  • 3+ years of experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and variance analysis, supported by advanced Microsoft Excel skills, such as PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, complex formulas, financial modeling, and analysis of large financial data sets.
  • 1+ year of practical manufacturing cost-accounting experience, including working knowledge of standard costs and manufacturing, production, inventory, or purchase price variances.
  • 1+ year of demonstrated leadership experience through direct supervision, people management, team leadership, or leadership of significant cross-functional initiatives.


Core Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Ability to communicate financial concepts to financial and non-financial audiences
  • Cross-functional relationship building and influence
  • Ability to manage competing priorities
  • Learning agility and comfort with ambiguity
  • Sound business judgment and professional courage
  • Ability to challenge business decisions appropriately when they conflict with U.S. GAAP or internal controls


Preferences:

  • Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Professional certification such as CPA or CMA.
  • Experience with SAP.
  • Experience with Hyperion (Forecasting sys) or similar financial consolidation and reporting systems.


Travel and Work Arrangements:

  • This position is based onsite in Sidney, OH.

The pay range for this role, excluding incentive opportunities, is a base of $120,000 - $140,00 annually. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

job.description:

Job Title: Design Engineer II – Reciprocating

Location: Campbellsville, KY or Davidson, NC


About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview
As a Design Engineer II for Reciprocating Products, you will be responsible for the design, development, analysis, testing, and continuous improvement of reciprocating compressor products and related systems. This role focuses on the mechanical design of compressor components and assemblies, supporting new product development, product enhancements, and sustaining engineering initiatives.

The successful candidate will apply mechanical engineering principles to develop innovative and reliable compressor solutions that meet performance, quality, cost, manufacturability, and customer requirements. This position requires close collaboration with manufacturing, testing, sourcing, quality, service, and product management teams.


Responsibilities

  • Design and develop reciprocating compressor components and assemblies.
  • Create and maintain engineering drawings, 3D models, specifications, and bills of materials using CAD tools.
  • Perform engineering calculations, analytical studies, and simulations to validate component strength, durability, thermal behavior, vibration characteristics, and overall system performance.
  • Support product development activities from concept through prototype validation, testing, production launch, and field support.
  • Evaluate compressor designs for performance, reliability, safety, manufacturability, and cost optimization.
  • Investigate product performance issues through root cause analysis and develop corrective actions for field and manufacturing concerns.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing and supply chain teams to improve production efficiency, reduce product cost, and enhance quality.
  • Develop and participate in compressor performance testing, design verification, and validation activities.
  • Ensure designs comply with applicable industry standards, customer requirements, and engineering best practices.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on product reliability, durability, efficiency, and customer satisfaction.
  • Manage engineering projects and workstreams with limited supervision while meeting project schedules and business objectives.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and engineering support personnel.
  • Work cross-functionally with global engineering, operations, quality, testing, and service organizations to deliver successful product outcomes.


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or Agricultural, Mining engineering discipline
  • 2+ years of engineering experience in mechanical design, product development, sustaining engineering, or related mechanical systems.
  • 2+ years of experience creating or interpreting engineering drawings, 3D models, specifications, and bills of materials (BOM).


Preferred Qualifications

  • Proficiency with 3D CAD software and engineering documentation practices.
  • Working knowledge of engineering calculations, GD&T, and manufacturing processes.
  • Experience with compressors, pumps, engines, rotating equipment, reciprocating equipment, pressure systems, or industrial machinery.
  • Experience supporting design verification, validation testing, performance testing, or simulation and analysis activities.
  • Exposure to reliability, durability, vibration, thermal, fatigue, airflow, or pressure-related design considerations.
  • Experience working across manufacturing, quality, sourcing, service, testing, or product management teams.
  • Familiarity with Design for Manufacturing/Assembly, value engineering, cost reduction, or continuous improvement initiatives.


Key Competencies

  • Strong mechanical engineering aptitude with the ability to analyze complex technical challenges, develop practical solutions, and drive continuous improvement in product performance, reliability, and quality.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage engineering projects and product development activities of moderate to high complexity, balancing technical, schedule, and business objectives.
  • Effective collaborator and communicator who works successfully across multidisciplinary teams and influences stakeholders to achieve project goals.
  • Results oriented professional with strong organizational skills and a customer-focused mindset, committed to delivering high-quality engineering solutions throughout the product lifecycle.


Travel & Work Arrangements / Requirements

  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 10-15%, primarily to manufacturing facilities, testing laboratories, customer sites, and supplier locations.
  • Occasional hands-on support of prototype builds, testing activities, and field investigations.


What We Offer?

Job Title: Plant Controller
Location: Sidney, OH

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Lead Financial Performance. Help Shape What Comes Next. Join LeROI, an Ingersoll Rand Center of Excellence for gas compression technology, manufacturing compressors and packaged solutions for the Oil & Gas and Biogas industries. We’re seeking an experienced Plant Controller to lead all aspects of plant finance at our Sidney facility during a significant period of growth. With revenue expected to more than double, new product lines planned, and a proposed facility expansion, you’ll help guide growth while strengthening the existing operation.

In this highly visible, hands-on role, you’ll develop the finance team and partner directly with plant leadership, Operations, and Materials to strengthen financial discipline and improve manufacturing performance. You’ll go beyond reporting results to understand what drives them—and turn those insights into action. Strong accounting and manufacturing finance expertise, attention to detail, and sound business judgment will help you identify risks, challenge assumptions, and uphold GAAP, internal controls, and reporting standards. You’ll thrive here with intellectual curiosity, an ownership mindset, and the agility to learn quickly and navigate changing priorities. An experienced Finance Leader who previously held the role will provide hands-on transition guidance.

Help shape the financial direction of a growing manufacturing operation—and expand your leadership impact.

Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Business Partnership:
  • Lead, develop, and manage the Sidney finance team.
  • Serve as the primary financial business partner to plant leadership, providing financial insight and recommendations to support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, Commercial, and other functions to drive business performance.
  • Provide clear and actionable analysis of financial results, risks, and opportunities.
  • Support and challenge the organization to achieve financial and operational commitments.
Accounting, Reporting & Controls:
  • Lead the monthly financial close and reporting process, ensuring timely and accurate results.
  • Oversee journal entries, account reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP, SOX requirements, company policies, and internal controls.
  • Lead and coordinate site activities related to internal and external audits.
  • Maintain strong financial controls and proactively identify opportunities to strengthen processes and reduce risk.
Planning & Financial Analysis:
  • Lead development of the facility's Annual Operating Plan (AOP), as well as monthly and quarterly forecasting processes.
  • Analyze financial and operational performance against plan, forecast, and prior periods.
  • Identify key drivers of performance, including manufacturing and plant variances, and partner with operational leaders to understand root causes and implement corrective actions.
  • Provide financial modeling and analysis to support business decisions and continuous improvement initiatives.
Cost Accounting & Inventory:
  • Provide leadership and oversight of plant cost accounting activities.
  • Lead the annual standard cost process and ensure accurate product costing.
  • Establish standard costs for new parts and review proposed cost changes for existing products.
  • Monitor and analyze material, labor, overhead, purchase price, and other manufacturing variances.
  • Lead quarterly excess and obsolete inventory reviews and work with cross-functional teams to proactively manage inventory exposure.
Capital & Asset Management:
  • Provide financial oversight of capital expenditures, including business case analysis, spending controls, and project tracking.
  • Oversee fixed asset accounting and ensure appropriate capitalization and asset controls.
  • Partner with plant leadership to prioritize investments and evaluate financial returns.
Continuous Improvement:
  • Identify opportunities to improve financial processes, reporting, controls, and business intelligence.
  • Drive standardization, simplification, and automation where appropriate.
  • Support ad-hoc financial analysis and business initiatives as needed.

Requirements:
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • 7+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including increasing responsibility for month-end close, financial reporting, U.S. GAAP compliance, and internal controls.
  • 3+ years of accounting or finance experience in a plant or manufacturing environment, including direct partnership with Operations, Materials, Production, or Supply Chain.
  • 3+ years of experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and variance analysis, supported by advanced Microsoft Excel skills, such as PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, complex formulas, financial modeling, and analysis of large financial data sets.
  • 1+ year of practical manufacturing cost-accounting experience, including working knowledge of standard costs and manufacturing, production, inventory, or purchase price variances.
  • 1+ year of demonstrated leadership experience through direct supervision, people management, team leadership, or leadership of significant cross-functional initiatives.

Core Competencies
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Ability to communicate financial concepts to financial and non-financial audiences
  • Cross-functional relationship building and influence
  • Ability to manage competing priorities
  • Learning agility and comfort with ambiguity
  • Sound business judgment and professional courage
  • Ability to challenge business decisions appropriately when they conflict with U.S. GAAP or internal controls

Preferences:
  • Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Professional certification such as CPA or CMA.
  • Experience with SAP.
  • Experience with Hyperion (Forecasting sys) or similar financial consolidation and reporting systems.

Travel and Work Arrangements:
  • This position is based onsite in Sidney, OH.
The pay range for this role, excluding incentive opportunities, is a base of $120,000 - $140,00 annually. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

PRODUCTION OPERATOR - ELECTRONIC

  • Contribute to the upkeep of the service and repair facility.
  • Ensure that all tasks are completed to meet or exceed specifications.
  • Collaborate with certified trades technicians in various maintenance projects.

Job Title: Systems Engineering Technologist
Location: Frederica, DE


About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview
This position sits within the engineering organization supporting the development, qualification, production, and sustainment of space flight hardware. The Systems Technologist supports verification activities and technical documentation throughout the product life cycle. In addition, there is a secondary role serving as a test conductor and/or test technician for verification activities.

The role works within established engineering processes while exercising independent technical judgment appropriate to experience. The Systems Technologist collaborates closely with design engineering, materials and processes, manufacturing and quality to perform verification test activities at the development, acceptance and qualification levels. This position is well suited for an individual seeking broad technical ownership, cross-functional leadership experience, and long-term growth in requirements-driven development of mission-critical products. The test conductor performs testing activities under established Quality processes and procedures, using sound judgment to ensure the safe and compliant handling of flight hardware. Successful candidates will have opportunities to develop into systems engineering, integration and testing, or technical leadership roles.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and support verification and validation activities, including definition of verification methods, test objectives, acceptance criteria, compliance matrices, and closure evidence.
  • Participate in technical reviews such as test readiness reviews, configuration reviews, and certification or customer reviews.
  • Generate and maintain test plans, test procedures, verification documents, engineering reports, change packages, and other product-definition records.
  • Communicate technical information clearly to team members, cross-functional partners, leadership, suppliers, and external customers.
  • Conduct suit testing activities including manned and unmanned operations. Support other ILC product testing on an as needed/availability basis
  • Perform suit hardware assembly and disassembly activities as part of testing.


Requirements

  • Must be able to access shared databases supporting U.S. Government programs. Due to U.S. export control regulations, applicants must qualify as a U.S. Person, defined as a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder), refugee, asylee, or otherwise be eligible to obtain any required U.S. Government authorizations.

Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.



Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ / OQ / PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.
  • Support cross-functional and cross-site quality initiatives, special projects, and foster a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.
  • Implement and maintain SPC strategy for manufactured products.
  • Perform Process Capability Studies (Cp,Cpk) for manufactured products.
  • Act as Quality Manager when QM is offsite


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Quality, Life Sciences, or a related technical field
  • 1+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or a similar role within a medical device or regulated manufacturing environment
  • Must have knowledge and understanding of SPC strategies.

Preference:

  • Working knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including document control, training systems, record retention, and audit support
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements
  • Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as Master Control or similar preferred
  • Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including development and revision of SOPs, work instructions, validation documents, and quality records
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Lead Auditor Certification is an advantage
  • Knowledge and understanding of Manufacturing Lean Tools (6S, Gemba, Kaizen, etc…)

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based

Job Overview:
Turn Demand into a Plan That Delivers. At Ingersoll Rand, the Master Scheduler connects customer demand with what the factory can deliver—helping ensure the right products move through production at the right time. Your decisions will influence delivery reliability, inventory levels, and how effectively the plant uses its people, materials, and equipment. In this role, you’ll turn business forecasts into a realistic production plan, anticipate bottlenecks, and guide trade-offs as priorities change. You’ll work across Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to balance immediate customer needs with longer-term manufacturing capacity, bringing clarity to competing demands and helping teams act before constraints become disruptions.

This opportunity is ideal for an analytical manufacturing professional who enjoys solving complex problems and influencing decisions across teams. You’ll take ownership of the production plan, work independently, and use data, manufacturing knowledge, and sound judgment to strengthen production flow, improve planning accuracy, and help the factory deliver on its commitments.

Responsibilities:
  • Translate the monthly SIOP consensus plan by product family to a detailed weekly master production schedule (MPS) with a 12-18 month planning horizon into the ERP for weekly MRP generation
  • Incorporate inter-company demand and backlog into SIOP supply planning process to ensure capacity and resources are available to meet demand requirements.
  • Monitor and drive resolution of MRP processing errors.
  • Support customer service with exception request analysis and expediting resolution.
  • Create and publish daily/weekly/monthly factory schedule adherence, capacity, and inventory reports.
  • Serve as a factory subject matter expert (SME) for ERP production planning and scheduling modules.
  • Identification and resolution of Constraints - Capacity, Resource & Material.
  • Facilitates long term capacity assessment (RCCP) and development of countermeasure/action plans.
 
Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in analyzing data relating to product forecasting, master scheduling, or shipment forecasting.
  • Experience with rate-based or flow line (non-MRP) and job shop manufacturing environments.
  • Experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.

Core Competencies:
  • Ability to effectively make complex decisions with limited time and information and can determine decision making criteria based on priorities.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple disciplines with internal and external resources.
  • Strong analytical capabilities, with a basic understanding of statistical analysis techniques.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, independent problem resolution, proven leadership ability, and the ability to manage the requirement of others.
  • Comfortable leading discussion and debate both within peer group and with matrix business partners, operational partners and leaders.

Preferences:
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM) required or hiring commitment to obtain in first 18 months of employment.
  • Experience with visual management systems.
  • Working knowledge of ERP system.
  • Data access/retrieval skills with extensive experience in data analysis, data manipulation using MS Excel and/or other tools as provided.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Onsite.

Job Title: Plant Controller
Location: Sidney, OH

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview
Lead Financial Performance. Help Shape What Comes Next. Join LeROI, an Ingersoll Rand Center of Excellence for gas compression technology, manufacturing compressors and packaged solutions for the Oil & Gas and Biogas industries. We’re seeking an experienced Plant Controller to lead all aspects of plant finance at our Sidney facility during a significant period of growth. With revenue expected to more than double, new product lines planned, and a proposed facility expansion, you’ll help guide growth while strengthening the existing operation.

In this highly visible, hands-on role, you’ll develop the finance team and partner directly with plant leadership, Operations, and Materials to strengthen financial discipline and improve manufacturing performance. You’ll go beyond reporting results to understand what drives them—and turn those insights into action. Strong accounting and manufacturing finance expertise, attention to detail, and sound business judgment will help you identify risks, challenge assumptions, and uphold GAAP, internal controls, and reporting standards. You’ll thrive here with intellectual curiosity, an ownership mindset, and the agility to learn quickly and navigate changing priorities. An experienced Finance Leader who previously held the role will provide hands-on transition guidance.

Help shape the financial direction of a growing manufacturing operation—and expand your leadership impact.

Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Business Partnership:
  • Lead, develop, and manage the Sidney finance team.
  • Serve as the primary financial business partner to plant leadership, providing financial insight and recommendations to support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, Commercial, and other functions to drive business performance.
  • Provide clear and actionable analysis of financial results, risks, and opportunities.
  • Support and challenge the organization to achieve financial and operational commitments.
Accounting, Reporting & Controls:
  • Lead the monthly financial close and reporting process, ensuring timely and accurate results.
  • Oversee journal entries, account reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP, SOX requirements, company policies, and internal controls.
  • Lead and coordinate site activities related to internal and external audits.
  • Maintain strong financial controls and proactively identify opportunities to strengthen processes and reduce risk.
Planning & Financial Analysis:
  • Lead development of the facility's Annual Operating Plan (AOP), as well as monthly and quarterly forecasting processes.
  • Analyze financial and operational performance against plan, forecast, and prior periods.
  • Identify key drivers of performance, including manufacturing and plant variances, and partner with operational leaders to understand root causes and implement corrective actions.
  • Provide financial modeling and analysis to support business decisions and continuous improvement initiatives.
Cost Accounting & Inventory:
  • Provide leadership and oversight of plant cost accounting activities.
  • Lead the annual standard cost process and ensure accurate product costing.
  • Establish standard costs for new parts and review proposed cost changes for existing products.
  • Monitor and analyze material, labor, overhead, purchase price, and other manufacturing variances.

Job Overview:
Turn Demand into a Plan That Delivers. At Ingersoll Rand, the Master Scheduler connects customer demand with what the factory can deliver—helping ensure the right products move through production at the right time. Your decisions will influence delivery reliability, inventory levels, and how effectively the plant uses its people, materials, and equipment. In this role, you’ll turn business forecasts into a realistic production plan, anticipate bottlenecks, and guide trade-offs as priorities change. You’ll work across Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to balance immediate customer needs with longer-term manufacturing capacity, bringing clarity to competing demands and helping teams act before constraints become disruptions.

This opportunity is ideal for an analytical manufacturing professional who enjoys solving complex problems and influencing decisions across teams. You’ll take ownership of the production plan, work independently, and use data, manufacturing knowledge, and sound judgment to strengthen production flow, improve planning accuracy, and help the factory deliver on its commitments.

Responsibilities:
  • Translate the monthly SIOP consensus plan by product family to a detailed weekly master production schedule (MPS) with a 12-18 month planning horizon into the ERP for weekly MRP generation
  • Incorporate inter-company demand and backlog into SIOP supply planning process to ensure capacity and resources are available to meet demand requirements.
  • Monitor and drive resolution of MRP processing errors.
  • Support customer service with exception request analysis and expediting resolution.
  • Create and publish daily/weekly/monthly factory schedule adherence, capacity, and inventory reports.
  • Serve as a factory subject matter expert (SME) for ERP production planning and scheduling modules.
  • Identification and resolution of Constraints - Capacity, Resource & Material.
  • Facilitates long term capacity assessment (RCCP) and development of countermeasure/action plans.
 
Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in analyzing data relating to product forecasting, master scheduling, or shipment forecasting.
  • Experience with rate-based or flow line (non-MRP) and job shop manufacturing environments.
  • Experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.

Core Competencies:
  • Ability to effectively make complex decisions with limited time and information and can determine decision making criteria based on priorities.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple disciplines with internal and external resources.
  • Strong analytical capabilities, with a basic understanding of statistical analysis techniques.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, independent problem resolution, proven leadership ability, and the ability to manage the requirement of others.
  • Comfortable leading discussion and debate both within peer group and with matrix business partners, operational partners and leaders.

Preferences:
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM) required or hiring commitment to obtain in first 18 months of employment.
  • Experience with visual management systems.
  • Working knowledge of ERP system.
  • Data access/retrieval skills with extensive experience in data analysis, data manipulation using MS Excel and/or other tools as provided.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Onsite.

Job Title: Senior Mechanical Design Engineer

Location: Charleroi, PA; Quincy, IL or Davidson, NC

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gases, and powders – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end markets, including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview

As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer supporting centrifugal blowers, you will provide hands-on product engineering and technical leadership for centrifugal blower products and related industrial equipment. This role combines detailed sustaining engineering with advanced analysis, testing, engineering-tool development, and ownership of complex product, manufacturing, supplier, and field issues.

You will move between drawings, bills of material, engineering changes, shop-floor troubleshooting, test work, analytical studies, and cross-functional coordination. The successful candidate is highly self-directed and able to establish the technical path, coordinate the right resources, and drive difficult work through closure with limited day-to-day direction.

Responsibilities

  • Own complex sustaining-engineering, manufacturing, supplier, test, and field problems from initial definition through investigation, corrective action, documentation, and closure.
  • Provide hands-on engineering support for centrifugal blowers, blower packages, and related mechanical systems, including work in production, assembly, and test environments.
  • Create and revise three-dimensional models, engineering drawings, specifications, bills of material, and product documentation.
  • Prepare and process engineering changes while maintaining accurate design records and product configuration.
  • Lead root-cause investigations and develop practical corrective actions that balance technical quality, schedule, cost, manufacturing, and customer needs.
  • Plan and execute mechanical, performance, vibration, temperature, pressure, and functional testing.
  • Develop test plans, test specifications, acceptance criteria, data-reduction methods, and test reports.
  • Investigate and apply applicable performance-test methods and standards, including ASME PTC 10 and ASME PTC 13 where relevant.
  • Perform or lead advanced engineering analysis such as computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, rotor dynamics, vibration analysis, thermal analysis, and blower-performance evaluation based on project needs and individual expertise.
  • Analyze test and field data, reconcile differences between predictions and measured results, and document technical conclusions and recommendations.
  • Identify repetitive or inefficient engineering processes and develop calculators, scripts, automated workflows, or internal engineering applications to improve speed, consistency, and capability.
  • Provide technical project ownership across Manufacturing, Quality, Sourcing, Service, Product Management, Application Engineering, suppliers, and other stakeholders.
  • Maintain priorities, action items, technical risks, and follow-up needed to drive assigned work to completion, and communicate schedule or resource concerns early.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentoring to other engineers and support design reviews and engineering decision-making.
  • Support product quality, cost reduction, standardization, obsolescence, and design-improvement activities.
  • Improve engineering standards, templates, calculators, test methods, and technical documentation.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline.
  • 7+ years of relevant experience in product design, sustaining engineering, testing, rotating equipment, or industrial machinery. Demonstrated capability and ownership are more important than a rigid year requirement.
  • 2+ years in fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, mechanics of materials, and machine design.
  • 2+ years of experience creating or revising three-dimensional models, engineering drawings, specifications, tolerances, and bills of material.
  • 2+ years of experience supporting manufactured or assembled mechanical products and resolving production, supplier, test, or field issues.
  • 2+ years of experience with technical project ownership, including planning engineering work, coordinating across functions, maintaining priorities and action items, and communicating technical or schedule risks.
  • 1+ year of demonstrated analytical engineering capability in at least one relevant area, such as CFD, FEA, rotor dynamics, vibration, thermal analysis, fluid-flow analysis, testing, or rotating-equipment performance.

Core Competencies

  • Ownership and follow-through in driving ambiguous, complex technical issues through documented closure.
  • Application of sound mechanical engineering fundamentals to hands-on sustaining, analysis, testing, and design work.
  • Practical problem-solving that balances product performance, reliability, manufacturability, schedule, cost, and customer needs.
  • Data-driven decision making using analysis, test results, production information, supplier input, and field performance.
  • Technical project leadership across cross-functional stakeholders without requiring direct supervisory authority.
  • Clear communication of technical conclusions, risks, priorities, actions, and resource needs.
  • Continuous improvement through reusable engineering standards, tools, methods, calculators, and documentation.
  • Technical guidance and mentoring that helps less-experienced engineers develop sound engineering judgment.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently own complex technical problems and drive them through closure with limited day-to-day direction.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and willingness to perform detailed sustaining work as well as advanced technical work.
  • Experience developing and executing test plans or test specifications and analyzing measured data.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineering and non-engineering audiences.


Preferences

  • Experience with centrifugal or multistage blowers, compressors, pumps, fans, turbines, vacuum equipment, or other rotating machinery.
  • Experience with CFD software and aerodynamic or internal-flow analysis.
  • Experience with FEA, rotor-dynamic and bearing analysis, vibration and acoustic troubleshooting, or thermal analysis.
  • Knowledge of ASME PTC 10, ASME PTC 13, or comparable rotating-equipment performance-test standards.
  • Experience developing engineering calculators, data-reduction programs, automated workflows, or internal engineering applications.
  • Experience using Python, MATLAB, VBA, or similar tools for engineering analysis and automation.
  • Experience using company-approved AI-assisted development tools for coding, data review, research, or technical documentation.
  • Experience using Creo, Inventor, SolidWorks, or a similar three-dimensional CAD system.
  • Experience using Windchill, SAP, or comparable PLM and ERP tools.
  • Hands-on use of vibration analyzers, pressure transducers, flow-measurement equipment, temperature instruments, electrical measurement equipment, or data-acquisition systems.
  • Experience with castings, machined components, fabricated assemblies, bearings, seals, shafts, impellers, gears, or lubrication systems.
  • Experience leading root-cause investigations using 5-Why, fishbone analysis, fault-tree analysis, or 8D.
  • Experience mentoring engineers or providing technical leadership without direct supervisory responsibility.

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Hybrid position based in Charleroi, PA; Quincy, IL or Davidson, NC. Two remote days per week of your choosing.
  • Regular on-site interaction with engineering, manufacturing, production, assembly, and test activities is required.
  • Occasional travel may be required to support suppliers, customers, field investigations, or other company locations.

Job Overview
In this role as a Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of production processes. The Manufacturing Engineer is tasked with designing and refining manufacturing methods to boost productivity while maintaining high-quality standards and ensuring safety protocols. They work closely with various departments, such as design, quality, and operations, to implement improvements that reduce costs and streamline workflows.

Responsibilities

  • Design and optimize manufacturing processes to enhance efficiency, quality, and safety in line with Ingersoll Rand's standards.
  • Analyze current production methods to identify and implement improvements that reduce costs and increase productivity.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including design, quality, and operations, to ensure seamless integration of new processes.
  • Ensure all manufacturing processes comply with Ingersoll Rand's company standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Stay updated on industry trends and technological advancements to introduce innovative manufacturing techniques.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues related to manufacturing processes to minimize downtime and ensure consistent production quality.
  • Prepare and maintain detailed documentation of processes, improvements, and best practices.
  • Train and support production staff on new and revised manufacturing processes to ensure smooth implementation.
  • Monitor and evaluate production performance metrics to drive continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions for any process deviations or quality issues.
  • Support the development and implementation of Lean Manufacturing principles to optimize workflows.
  • Participate in new product development projects to ensure manufacturability and scalability of designs.
  • Coordinate with suppliers to ensure the availability and quality of materials and components.
  • Utilize data analysis and Six Sigma methodologies to drive process improvements and achieve operational excellence.



Requirements

  • High school diploma or GED
  • 5 years of experience in manufacturing engineering
  • 2+ yrs of hydraulic and pneumatic systems and applications


Core Competencies

  • Technical Expertise: knowledge of manufacturing processes and technologies.
  • Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills to develop effective solutions.
  • Project Management: Ability to manage projects from start to finish efficiently.
  • Collaboration: Excellent teamwork skills to work with cross-functional teams.
  • Continuous Improvement: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.
  • Communication: Clear and effective verbal and written communication.
  • Adaptability: Flexibility to embrace new technologies and processes.
  • Attention to Detail: Meticulous to ensure quality and compliance.
  • Innovation: Creative thinking to introduce new manufacturing solutions.
  • Leadership: Ability to train and guide production staff.
  • Safety Awareness: Strong understanding of and commitment to safety protocols.



Preferences

  • Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing engineering, Industrial or Mechanical engineering.
  • Working knowledge of Six Sigma
  • Lean Six Sigma Green or Black Belt
  • Demonstrated ability to continuously improve manufacturing processes
  • Understanding & application of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerance

Job Overview:
Turn Demand into a Plan That Delivers. At Ingersoll Rand, the Master Scheduler connects customer demand with what the factory can deliver—helping ensure the right products move through production at the right time. Your decisions will influence delivery reliability, inventory levels, and how effectively the plant uses its people, materials, and equipment. In this role, you’ll turn business forecasts into a realistic production plan, anticipate bottlenecks, and guide trade-offs as priorities change. You’ll work across Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to balance immediate customer needs with longer-term manufacturing capacity, bringing clarity to competing demands and helping teams act before constraints become disruptions.

This opportunity is ideal for an analytical manufacturing professional who enjoys solving complex problems and influencing decisions across teams. You’ll take ownership of the production plan, work independently, and use data, manufacturing knowledge, and sound judgment to strengthen production flow, improve planning accuracy, and help the factory deliver on its commitments.

Responsibilities:
  • Translate the monthly SIOP consensus plan by product family to a detailed weekly master production schedule (MPS) with a 12-18 month planning horizon into the ERP for weekly MRP generation
  • Incorporate inter-company demand and backlog into SIOP supply planning process to ensure capacity and resources are available to meet demand requirements.
  • Monitor and drive resolution of MRP processing errors.
  • Support customer service with exception request analysis and expediting resolution.
  • Create and publish daily/weekly/monthly factory schedule adherence, capacity, and inventory reports.
  • Serve as a factory subject matter expert (SME) for ERP production planning and scheduling modules.
  • Identification and resolution of Constraints - Capacity, Resource & Material.
  • Facilitates long term capacity assessment (RCCP) and development of countermeasure/action plans.
 
Requirements:
  • Bachelor's degree in business or engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in analyzing data relating to product forecasting, master scheduling, or shipment forecasting.
  • Experience with rate-based or flow line (non-MRP) and job shop manufacturing environments.
  • Experience in operations, inventory management, MRP and lean manufacturing processes.

Core Competencies:
  • Ability to effectively make complex decisions with limited time and information and can determine decision making criteria based on priorities.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple disciplines with internal and external resources.
  • Strong analytical capabilities, with a basic understanding of statistical analysis techniques.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, independent problem resolution, proven leadership ability, and the ability to manage the requirement of others.
  • Comfortable leading discussion and debate both within peer group and with matrix business partners, operational partners and leaders.

Preferences:
  • APICS Certification in Production and Inventory Management (CPIM) required or hiring commitment to obtain in first 18 months of employment.
  • Experience with visual management systems.
  • Working knowledge of ERP system.
  • Data access/retrieval skills with extensive experience in data analysis, data manipulation using MS Excel and/or other tools as provided.

Job Overview

As a Sustaining Engineer focused on Production & Configuration Support, you will provide responsive engineering support for the production, assembly, inspection, testing, and refurbishment of Marine vacuum pumps, compressors, packaged systems, and related equipment. You will resolve day-to-day technical issues, maintain accurate product configurations, support suppliers and manufacturing operations, and coordinate routine engineering changes.

You will work closely with Product Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Test Engineering, and Customer Support to provide timely technical direction while maintaining product requirements, design intent, and configuration control. You will resolve issues within established engineering requirements and escalate changes requiring product-design evaluation to the appropriate Product Design Engineer.

Responsibilities

  • Provide responsive engineering support for Marine manufacturing, assembly, inspection, testing, refurbishment, and routine production needs.
  • Review production, assembly, supplier, quality, and test issues and develop technically sound recommendations using established product requirements and engineering information.
  • Investigate drawing, bill of material, specification, material, fit, tolerance, and product-configuration discrepancies.
  • Support the evaluation of nonconforming material and proposed dispositions in coordination with Quality and the appropriate Product Design Engineer.
  • Prepare and coordinate routine engineering changes, bill of material updates, drawing corrections, and controlled documentation revisions.
  • Support component substitutions, material changes, supplier changes, and obsolescence issues by evaluating their effects on fit, form, function, manufacturability, and configuration requirements.
  • Escalate issues or proposed changes affecting product performance, design intent, customer or contract requirements, critical characteristics, or qualification status to the appropriate Product Design Engineer.

  • Coordinate with Product Design Engineering and the Automated Test Engineer when production or configuration issues affect product performance, validation requirements, or testing.
  • Maintain records of technical decisions and ensure approved changes are incorporated into controlled documentation.
  • Identify recurring production-support needs that warrant root cause analysis or formal product improvement.
  • Drive assigned production issues and routine engineering changes to documented closure, and communicate significant workload, schedule, or technical risks to the Engineering Supervisor.

  • 2+ years of experience preparing or coordinating engineering changes and maintaining product documentation in an ERP, PLM, or comparable controlled system.

  • Practical engineering judgment to resolve production and configuration issues within established product requirements and approval processes.

  • Ability to prioritize multiple technical requests based on safety, quality, production, customer, schedule, and business impact.

Job Overview

The Sustaining Engineer leads technical investigations and product and process improvement activities involving Marine vacuum pumps, compressors, packaged systems, and related manufacturing, assembly, refurbishment, and testing processes. This position is responsible for identifying root causes, developing corrective engineering actions, and using production, quality, supplier, test, and service information to improve product reliability, manufacturability, consistency, and lifecycle support.

The engineer works closely with Product Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Test Engineering, and Customer Support to resolve recurring problems and implement sustainable improvements while maintaining product requirements, design intent, and configuration control. The role coordinates with the appropriate Product Design Engineer when a proposed improvement could affect product performance, customer or contract requirements, critical characteristics, or qualification status.

What Success Looks Like

  • Leads structured technical investigations and develops practical improvement solutions supported by evidence.
  • Reduces recurring production, assembly, quality, test, refurbishment, and product issues through effective corrective actions.
  • Converts lessons learned into sustainable product, process, documentation, or standard-work improvements.
  • Recognizes when an improvement requires Product Design Engineering approval, validation, or requalification.
  • Drives corrective actions through implementation, validation, and effectiveness review rather than stopping at recommendations.

Responsibilities

  • Lead technical investigations involving recurring manufacturing, assembly, quality, test, refurbishment, supplier, and product-performance issues.
  • Apply structured problem-solving and root cause analysis methods to distinguish symptoms from underlying product, process, documentation, supplier, or test-system causes.
  • Analyze production records, nonconformance information, test results, supplier data, service information, and available product history to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop and coordinate corrective engineering actions with Product Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Test Engineering, and Customer Support.
  • Support improvement initiatives involving machining, fabrication, assembly, inspection, testing, documentation, workflow, product handling, and related manufacturing processes.
  • Evaluate opportunities to improve product manufacturability, assembly, reliability, maintainability, consistency, and lifecycle support.
  • Coordinate with the appropriate Product Design Engineer when an improvement affects design intent, product performance, customer or contract requirements, critical characteristics, or qualification status.
  • Coordinate with the Automated Test Engineer to define and execute validation activities for product and process improvements.
  • Prepare investigation reports, corrective-action documentation, engineering change requests, implementation plans, lessons learned, and reusable engineering guidance.
  • Verify the effectiveness of completed corrective actions, identify issues requiring formal product-development or strategic-improvement projects, and communicate significant progress, risks, or resource needs to the Engineering Supervisor.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • 2+ years of experience in technical problem-solving, root cause analysis, manufacturing support, product improvement, quality engineering, or sustaining engineering.
  • 2+ years Working knowledge of mechanical equipment, engineering drawings, bills of material, manufacturing processes, assembly methods, inspection, and testing.
  • 2+ years Ability to analyze technical information, identify trends, develop evidence-based conclusions, and communicate practical recommendations.
  • 2+ years Experience coordinating technical investigations, corrective actions, or improvement activities across multiple functions.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain required government security clearances.

Core Competencies

  • Applies structured problem-solving and root cause analysis methods to develop evidence-based technical conclusions.
  • Uses production data, drawings, test results, nonconformance information, supplier input, service feedback, and product history to evaluate recurring issues.
  • Develops practical corrective actions that balance technical effectiveness, manufacturability, reliability, implementation risk, and business impact.
  • Coordinates cross-functional investigations and maintains progress from problem definition through implementation and effectiveness review.
  • Recognizes when proposed actions require Product Design Engineering evaluation, controlled engineering changes, validation, or requalification.
  • Communicates investigation methods, technical findings, risks, recommendations, and results clearly to technical and operational stakeholders.

Preferences

  • Experience with vacuum pumps, compressors, packaged systems, rotating equipment, or other industrial machinery.
  • Experience with structured root cause analysis, corrective action, failure analysis, or continuous improvement methods.
  • Familiarity with machining, castings, fabrication, mechanical assembly, inspection, instrumentation, and product testing.
  • Experience using Autodesk Inventor, SAP, Windchill, or comparable engineering systems.
  • Familiarity with design for manufacturing and assembly, reliability, vibration, acoustics, materials, corrosion, or mechanical failure analysis.
  • Familiarity with government contracts, controlled technical documentation, qualification activities, or regulated change processes.

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • On-site position based in Bentleyville, PA.
  • Regular interaction with engineering, manufacturing, assembly, inspection, refurbishment, and testing activities is required while conducting investigations and supporting improvements.
  • Travel is expected to be minimal but may be required to support suppliers, customers, testing, or other business needs.

These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
Requirements:
  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Core Competencies:
  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner
Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range:
Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $35.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

Job Overview:
We are looking for a highly business-driven CRM Business Initiative Lead to own and evolve key CRM-enabled business capabilities across Sales, Service, Customer Experience, and Commercial Excellence. This role is accountable for defining and driving business capabilities that deliver measurable value, ensuring CRM processes are effective, scalable, standardized, and data-driven. The CRM Business Initiative Lead acts as the business owner of assigned capabilities—partnering closely with stakeholders to shape future-state processes, prioritize initiatives, and ensure sustainable adoption and value realization. This is not a coordination or delivery role. It is a business leadership position focused on outcomes, continuous improvement, and enabling capabilities that are ready to leverage AI, automation, and emerging digital experiences.

Responsibilities:

  • Own and evolve CRM-enabled business capabilities across Sales, Service, and Commercial Excellence.
  • Act as the primary business owner and subject matter expert.

  • Ensure AI-enabled capabilities meet business goals, governance standards, and user needs.
  • Support adoption and value realization of new digital capabilities.
