  • 3+ years of experience in CRM, Commercial Excellence, Sales Operations, Product Management, Consulting, or similar roles.


Core Competencies:

  • Strong business capability owner with a focus on outcomes and value
  • Able to translate business needs into scalable, data-driven processes
  • Analytical and data-driven in decision-making
  • Effective at influencing across business and technology teams
  • Focused on adoption, performance, and continuous improvement
  • Able to evolve capabilities to leverage AI, automation, and future interaction models


Preferences:

  • Proven experience owning business processes or capabilities.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives in complex environments.
  • Strong analytical skills with experience using KPIs and dashboards.
  • Experience working with technology and digital solutions teams.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Ability to combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Job Title: Industrial Refrigeration Test Technician
Location: Junction City, OR

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:

We are seeking a skilled, safety-focused Industrial Refrigeration Test Technician to inspect, commission, troubleshoot, and functionally test industrial glycol and refrigeration chillers prior to shipment.

This position is responsible for verifying that equipment operates safely, performs according to engineering specifications, and meets company quality standards. The ideal candidate is mechanically inclined, comfortable working with refrigeration, electrical, and control systems, and capable of diagnosing and resolving equipment issues in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform functional testing, startup, commissioning, and final quality verification of industrial refrigeration systems, chillers, and related equipment prior to shipment.
  • Review engineering documentation including wiring diagrams, piping schematics, bills of material, test procedures, and specifications to ensure equipment is configured and tested correctly.
  • Inspect, operate, and evaluate refrigeration, mechanical, electrical, and control systems while recording operating data and verifying performance against design requirements.
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, refrigeration, controls, and system-performance issues; coordinate corrective actions with Production, Engineering, and Quality teams.
  • Perform leak testing, system evacuation, refrigerant charging, refrigerant recovery, and related activities in accordance with company procedures and regulatory requirements.
  • Navigate and utilize PLCs, HMIs, controllers, variable frequency drives (VFDs), and other control interfaces to support testing, troubleshooting, and equipment verification.
  • Complete test reports, inspection records, refrigerant documentation, and other required quality records while maintaining accurate testing documentation.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives, maintain testing equipment and work areas, assist with training of team members, and perform other related duties as assigned.

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, industrial maintenance, HVAC, refrigeration, electrical, controls, or related technical environments.
  • Ability to read and interpret wiring diagrams, refrigeration schematics, piping drawings, bills of material, and technical documentation.
  • Experience using testing, diagnostic, or measurement equipment and documenting results in computer-based systems or electronic records.


Core Competencies:

  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods and regularly bend, kneel, climb, reach, and work around large industrial equipment.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation and safely handle tools, testing equipment, hoses, gauges, and other job-related materials.
  • Follow all company safety policies, PPE requirements, lockout/tagout procedures, electrical safety practices, refrigerant handling requirements, and approved testing procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free work area and promptly report unsafe conditions, equipment concerns, spills, leaks, or near misses.

Preferences:

  • Experience testing, servicing, commissioning, or troubleshooting commercial or industrial refrigeration, HVAC, process cooling, or engineered equipment.
  • EPA Section 608 Certification, technical degree, apprenticeship, military technical training, or equivalent hands-on technical experience.
  • Experience working with PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, electrical controls, compressors, pumps, heat exchangers, valves, sensors, and related industrial equipment.
  • Experience performing refrigerant recovery, evacuation, charging, leak testing, brazing, or other refrigeration-related activities; OSHA, electrical safety, or Lockout/Tagout training is a plus.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This is a fully onsite position based in a manufacturing environment and requires a strong commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence. The individual must safely work around electrical equipment, refrigeration systems, pressurized components, moving machinery, and active production operations while complying with all company safety policies and required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements.

Job Title:

Maintenance Technician I

Location:

Ivyland, PA

About Us:

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems.

Job Summary:

We are currently seeking a reliable and efficient individual to join our Maintenance team. This role will be responsible for ensuring the efficient operation of our manufacturing facility by performing routine maintenance and repairs on machinery and equipment. A Maintenance Technician works with a team to troubleshoot issues, conduct preventative maintenance, and repair and install new equipment while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is adaptable, a team player, a great communicator, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

Responsibilities:

General Maintenance:

  • Conduct weekly and monthly equipment inspections
  • Perform general cleaning of all areas of the building
  • Manage routine upkeep of exterior areas and parking lot
  • Complete non-routine cleaning according to specified job orders
  • Remove trash, cardboard, and other recycling daily
  • Handle emergency cleaning and upkeep requests
  • Ensure rooms are maintained and fully equipped
  • Perform manual repairs when necessary
  • Aid maintenance technicians in electrical, lighting, mechanical, plumbing, and machinery repairs
  • Install and troubleshoot primary facility electrical up to 440V lighting, mechanical, and plumbing
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets

Equipment Maintenance:

  • Perform routine maintenance tasks on manufacturing machinery and equipment
  • Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic issues
  • Conduct inspections to identify potential problems and implement preventive measures

Equipment Installation:

  • Assist in installing new machinery and production lines
  • Collaborate with engineers and contractors to ensure proper setup

Team Collaboration:

  • Collaborate with all team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets
  • Provide support during scheduled shutdowns and maintenance projects

Documentation:

  • Maintain detailed records of maintenance activities and repairs
  • Log equipment downtime and report any recurring issues to the Maintenance Lead and Manager

Inventory Management:

  • Monitor and report on the inventory of spare parts and maintenance supplies
  • Request replenishment as needed to maintain adequate stock levels

Training and Development:

  • Participate in training programs to improve maintenance skills and product knowledge
  • Complete environmental training program and obtain certification
  • Attend monthly EHS trainings
  • Obtain and maintain IR certification/license for harness and equipment (forklift, scissors, and boom lift)
  • Adhere to the Total Preventative Maintenance Program
  • Attend Mazak maintenance certification program
  • Follow all policies and procedures (i.e. report on time and ready to work - Start/Lunch/Breaks)

Quality Control:

  • Perform quality checks by established quality procedures and ISO requirements
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the assembly process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality

Safety Compliance:

  • Follow all safety guidelines, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Report any safety hazards or incidents to supervisors promptly
  • Training and certification in Confined Space and on Lockout Tagout
  • Participate in Waste Management Program
  • Complete all safety training required before use of any equipment
  • Survey buildings and repair mechanical systems in consistence with health and safety regulations
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000

Cleanliness and Organization:

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Follow 5S principles (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain)

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 0-3 years’ experience in Maintenance
  • Electrical and mechanical skills, preferred
  • Ability to operate a fork truck and scissor lift
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment

The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.

Job Title: Product Design Engineer

Location: Charleroi, PA

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gases, and powders – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview

As a Product Design Engineer focused on Marine Qualification & Development, you will support the design, development, qualification, and release of Marine vacuum pumps, compressors, packaged systems, and related equipment. You will have primary responsibility for newer products progressing through design completion and qualification while also supporting significant improvements to current products.

You will work closely with Test Engineering, Operations, Quality, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Project Management, and Customer Support to translate customer and contract requirements into controlled product designs. You will develop technical solutions, maintain product design documentation, address issues identified during qualification, and support the successful transition of qualified products into production.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, evaluate, and improve Marine vacuum pumps, compressors, packaged systems, and related rotating equipment.
  • Support products through design completion, initial builds, validation, qualification, controlled release, and transition into production.
  • Review customer specifications, contract requirements, applicable standards, and product requirements to determine their effect on design.
  • Develop engineering calculations, three-dimensional models, layouts, detail drawings, bills of material, specifications, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Participate in design reviews, technical risk assessments, manufacturing-readiness reviews, and qualification-readiness activities.
  • Work with the Automated Test Engineer to define validation needs, operating conditions, acceptance criteria, and required test evidence.
  • Investigate product issues discovered during manufacturing, assembly, inspection, testing, or qualification and develop appropriate design solutions.
  • Prepare, review, and support approval of engineering change requests, bill-of-material changes, drawing revisions, and related technical documentation in accordance with established approval requirements.
  • Provide technical guidance to Operations, Quality, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Test Engineering, Project Management, and Customer Support.
  • Maintain controlled engineering records and document the technical basis for significant design decisions.
  • Identify and communicate technical risks before they affect qualification, product performance, cost, or schedule.
  • Coordinate across functions to support product qualification, controlled release, and transition into production.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive experience in rotating equipment design, mechanical product design, industrial equipment design, manufacturing engineering, or a related engineering environment.
  • 3+ years Experience developing or maintaining three-dimensional models, engineering drawings, bills of material, and other controlled product documentation.
  • 3+ years Working knowledge of manufacturing processes, including machining, casting, fabrication, mechanical assembly, rotating equipment design principles, and related inspection practices.
  • 3+ years Experience maintaining engineering data and product documentation in an ERP, PLM, or comparable controlled system.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain required government security clearances.

Core Competencies

  • Application of sound mechanical engineering principles to develop practical product designs that balance performance, reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, design integrity, and cost.
  • Ability to translate customer, contract, and product requirements into controlled design outputs and qualification activities.
  • Data-driven decision making using calculations, drawings, test data, manufacturing input, and technical requirements.
  • Accuracy and traceability in models, drawings, bills of material, engineering records, product data, and change history.
  • Clear technical communication and effective collaboration across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Operations, Sourcing, Project Management, Test Engineering, and Customer Support.
  • Ownership of design and qualification activities from design completion through controlled release and production transition.
  • Proactive identification and communication of technical risks affecting qualification, product performance, cost, or schedule.

Preferences

  • Experience with vacuum pumps, compressors, packaged systems, or other rotating equipment.
  • Experience using Autodesk Inventor, SAP, Windchill, or comparable engineering systems.
  • Knowledge of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, compressible flow, or equipment-performance analysis.
  • Experience supporting product validation, qualification testing, or customer-witnessed testing.
  • Familiarity with government contracts, military specifications, controlled technical documentation, design for manufacturing and assembly, weld-joint design, vibration, acoustics, material selection, or corrosion.

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • On-site position based in Bentleyville, PA.
  • Regular on-site interaction with engineering, manufacturing, assembly, inspection, and testing activities is required.
  • Travel is expected to be minimal but may be required to support suppliers, customers, testing, or other business needs.

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.


Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ / OQ / PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.
  • Support cross-functional and cross-site quality initiatives, special projects, and foster a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.
  • Implement and maintain SPC strategy for manufactured products. 
  • Perform Process Capability Studies (Cp,Cpk) for manufactured products.
  • Act as Quality Manager when QM is offsite
 


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Quality, Life Sciences, or a related technical field
  • 1+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or a similar role within a medical device or regulated manufacturing environment
  • Must have knowledge and understanding of SPC strategies.
 


Preference: 

  • Working knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including document control, training systems, record retention, and audit support
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements
  • Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as Master Control or similar preferred
  • Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including development and revision of SOPs, work instructions, validation documents, and quality records
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Lead Auditor Certification is an advantage
  • Knowledge and understanding of Manufacturing Lean Tools (6S, Gemba, Kaizen, etc…)
 


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based
 

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $65,000-$80,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.

Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.


Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ / OQ / PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.
  • Support cross-functional and cross-site quality initiatives, special projects, and foster a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.
  • Implement and maintain SPC strategy for manufactured products. 
  • Perform Process Capability Studies (Cp,Cpk) for manufactured products.
  • Act as Quality Manager when QM is offsite
 


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Quality, Life Sciences, or a related technical field
  • 1+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or a similar role within a medical device or regulated manufacturing environment
  • Must have knowledge and understanding of SPC strategies.
 


Preference: 

  • Working knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including document control, training systems, record retention, and audit support
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements
  • Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as Master Control or similar preferred
  • Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including development and revision of SOPs, work instructions, validation documents, and quality records
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Lead Auditor Certification is an advantage
  • Knowledge and understanding of Manufacturing Lean Tools (6S, Gemba, Kaizen, etc…)
 


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based
 

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $65,000-$80,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview

As an Aseptic Technician I, you will be responsible for performing various tasks related to the aseptic filling of pharmaceutical products in ISO Class 7 rooms with ISO 4 and 5 filling hood systems. You will work closely with other members of the production team to ensure that all products are manufactured in accordance with established GMP guidelines and meet the company’s high standards of quality, safety, and efficacy. An Aseptic Technician I works under close supervision with minimal latitude for independent judgment.

Responsibilities

  • Perform aseptic filling of pharmaceutical products using ISO Class 7 clean rooms with ISO 4 and 5 filling hood systems.
  • Operate equipment, including filling machines, autoclaves, and sterilizers, according to established protocols and SOPs.
  • Perform a variety of processing duties according to Batch Production Records (BPRs) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) in the Manufacturing Department, including but not limited to cleaning and recovery of classified areas and workspaces, component preparation, weighing raw materials, compounding/formulation, filtration of solutions, aseptic filling, inspection, labeling, and packaging.
  • Prepare the clean room, including materials and resources, with the goal of eliminating errors and working in accordance with Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP).
  • Monitor and maintain aseptic conditions in the filling room, including cleaning and disinfecting equipment and surfaces.
  • Follow all safety procedures and guidelines, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Complete all necessary documentation and records, including batch records and logbooks, according to GMP guidelines.
  • Participate in training programs to maintain and improve skills and knowledge of aseptic techniques and procedures.
  • Perform all other duties as assigned by supervisor or management.

Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • One year of experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience using Microsoft Office Suite.

Core Competencies

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office software and other basic computer applications.
  • Proficiency using handheld technology, such as smartphones and iPads, and network-based systems.

Preferences

  • Knowledge of general safety and hygiene practices.
  • Ability to follow and understand written procedures and protocols.
  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to complete accurate documentation.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment while maintaining a high level of quality and safety.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Manufacturing experience in the pharmaceutical or medical device industry.
  • Experience in a clean room and aseptic manufacturing environment.
  • Experience with liquid injectable aseptic filling and finishing.
  • Mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting ability.
  • BioWork Aseptic Certification.

Job title:   Quality Engineer

Location: Alsip, IL

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.


Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ / OQ / PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.
  • Support cross-functional and cross-site quality initiatives, special projects, and foster a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.
  • Implement and maintain SPC strategy for manufactured products. 
  • Perform Process Capability Studies (Cp,Cpk) for manufactured products.
  • Act as Quality Manager when QM is offsite
 


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Quality, Life Sciences, or a related technical field
  • 1+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or a similar role within a medical device or regulated manufacturing environment
  • Must have knowledge and understanding of SPC strategies.
 


Preference: 

  • Working knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including document control, training systems, record retention, and audit support
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements
  • Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as Master Control or similar preferred
  • Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including development and revision of SOPs, work instructions, validation documents, and quality records
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Lead Auditor Certification is an advantage
  • Knowledge and understanding of Manufacturing Lean Tools (6S, Gemba, Kaizen, etc…)
 


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based
 

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $65,000-$80,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title:

Location:

Ivyland, PA

About Us:

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems.

Job Summary:

We are currently seeking a reliable and motivated individual to join our Milroyal Assembly team. This role will be responsible for assembling, inspecting, and packaging products on an assembly line or independently in a manufacturing facility. A Milroyal Assembler works with a team to ensure the efficient and accurate assembly of products while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is consistent, a team player, a great communicator, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

Responsibilities:

Assembly:

  • Assemble components and parts following detailed instructions
  • Read and understand the bill of materials and work order instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Complete assembly tasks, use various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses (may use cranes and hoists); Responsibilities may also include specialized work such as tube bending and soldering
  • Stay updated on changes in assembly processes and product specifications
  • Meet or exceed production targets and quotas
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets

Quality Control:

  • Inspect finished products for quality and adherence to specifications
  • Test and troubleshoot assemblies
  • Perform quality checks by established quality procedures and ISO requirements
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the assembly process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality

Inventory Management:

  • Monitor and request materials and components as needed for assembly
  • Keep track of inventory levels and report shortages

Training and Development:

  • Participate in training programs to improve assembly skills and product knowledge
  • Attend monthly EHS trainings
  • Follow all policies and procedures (i.e. report on time and ready to work - Start/Lunch/Breaks)

Safety Compliance:

  • Follow all safety guidelines, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Report any safety hazards or incidents to supervisors promptly
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000

Cleanliness and Organization:

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Follow 5S principles (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain)

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 0 – 2 years’ experience in assembly or manufacturing, preferred
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Fully site based
  • Climate controlled manufacturing plant
  • Protective eyewear and footwear required

Key Competencies:

  • Communication
  • Efficiency
  • Productivity
  • Accuracy
  • Teamwork
  • Integrity
  • Problem Solving
  • Decision Making
  • Detail Oriented
  • Results Driven
  • Documentation
  • Adaptability

Job Title: Material Handler


Shift: Monday - Friday 7:00am-3:30pm


Location: Southern Pines, NC (On-site)
About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gases, and powders – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end markets, including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.


Job Overview:

The Material Handler is responsible for ensuring materials are supplied where and when they are needed. The Material Handler is responsible for keeping workstations fully stocked with materials, ultimately contributing to higher overall productivity of other workers.Responsibilities:

  • Receives, ships, loads, and unloads materials/parts from suppliers or carriers. Material may be unloaded from trucks, pallets, trays, racks, and shelves by hand, with forklift, or other material handling device. Uses computer and/or barcode scanner to properly identify stock locations to retrieve parts.
  • Visually inspects incoming pieces/parts for compliance and obvious damage; informing Quality if necessary.
  • Moves material/parts from warehouse or receiving area, to designated line or stock locations. Moving stock to release, consolidate, or change part locations. (Ex: to proper stock location, to inspection area, to machine cell) while using barcode scanner and/or computers.
  • Reads work order or follows oral instructions to determine materials to be transferred; informs inventory control to update computer system when necessary (Ex: quantity mismatch, mixed parts, wrong labels)
  • Counts, weighs, and records number of units of materials received, moved, or shipped and reports inconsistencies to inventory control.
  • Operates forklift, hand truck, and/or other material handling equipment to assist in loading or moving any material. Remove any debris found on shelves throughout the warehouse.
  • Receives work orders from planners; picks parts to jobs for machine shop, assembly areas, staging for kits, and spare part sales orders using barcode scanner and/or computer.
  • Follows all ISO procedures and safety rules, including wearing personal safety equipment. Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned

Requirements:

  • 1+ years’ experience in manufacturing or distribution industry.


Core Competencies:

  • Ability to effectively share information about job duties in one-on-one and small group situations to supervisor, customers, clients, and other employees of the organization.
  • Ability to pass certification for Powered Industrial Vehicle license (such as the forklift certification).


Preferences:

  • HS Diploma or GED preferred
  • Knowledge of inventory processes.
  • Process driven and systematic in their approach to completing their work
  • Ability to identify and solve problems.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • This position will be based 100% onsite at our Southern Pines, North Carolina facility
  • Lifting: Must be able to lift up to 40 pounds occasionally with a hoist to be used on objects over 40 pounds.
  • Standing: Standing is required in periods of up to three hours at a time.
  • Stooping: Would be required to lift objects off pallets
  • Hand Dexterity: Must be able to work with hand tools, screws and gauges, as well as operating buttons on controls.
  • Carrying: Capable of carrying 40 pounds for a distance of up to 25 feet.

Location: Toledo / Northwest Ohio Territory

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview:
Our Ingersoll Rand’s Compression Systems and Services Customer Center is hiring a General Line Account Manager to join their team. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the Customer Center equipment sales and service activity for a specific territory. Traveling in a defined geographic area, this includes quoting, strategizing, prospecting, and developing relationships to achieve revenue targets, maximize profits, increase market share and maintain customer loyalty while achieving organizational goals. The position is a unique blend of supporting a major distributor and selling direct to customers.

Responsibilities:

  • Generate Revenue - Responsible for generating sales of equipment, service contracts, and service offerings with our direct end users and partners selling to a defined customer base within a geographic area. Develop existing customer base and secure new, competitive accounts to expand IR presence in the market. Provide and design compressed air solutions to fulfill industrial customer needs. Products include compressed air equipment, accessories, turnkey installations, service contracts, parts, service, rental equipment and energy audits. Keep current with all product knowledge, industry standards and training needed. Execute strategy for continuous improvement and exceeding customer satisfaction. Achieve all assigned sales targets.
  • Develop People Capabilities - Provide selling skills and product/services training for dealer sales personnel (as required) as well as personnel within customer center. Partner with services team to best understand products and services and satisfy and anticipate customer’s needs.
  • Manage Cash - Ensure that all orders obtained are error-free with correct customer documentation. Ensure resolution of all customer disputes. Manage all costs associated with selling efforts, including travel and entertainment expenditures.
  • Ensure adherence to safety rules (vehicle safety, customer site safety) in the field, as well as in the customer center.
  • Earn Customer loyalty by collaborating cross functionally. Leverage best support for customers by partnering with service team to help troubleshoot customer issues or offer unique solutions.
  • Maintain Customer Relationship Management database including face-to-face customer interactions, assets, agreements, contacts, and opportunities in order management system. Record order follow-up activities (e.g. delivery), reporting requirements (email) and database requirements. Provide feedback on market conditions. Responsible for driving and tracking sales pipeline of all account activity and daily reporting.


Requirements:

  • High School Diploma
  • 4+ years’ of experience in an industrial sales business setting


Core Competencies:

  • Excellent relationship-building and interpersonal skills, including verbal, written and presentation communication skills.
  • Establishes and builds solid relationships with customers, key institutions and team members
  • Honest, self-motivated and team oriented.
  • Able to work within a team environment and independently.
  • Mechanical and electrical expertise required.

The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.

Requirements:

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.

On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.

Job Title:

Maintenance Technician I

Location:

Ivyland, PA

About Us:

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems. 

Job Summary:

We are currently seeking a reliable and efficient individual to join our Maintenance team. This role will be responsible for ensuring the efficient operation of our manufacturing facility by performing routine maintenance and repairs on machinery and equipment. A Maintenance Technician works with a team to troubleshoot issues, conduct preventative maintenance, and repair and install new equipment while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is adaptable, a team player, a great communicator, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

Responsibilities:

 

General Maintenance:

  • Conduct weekly and monthly equipment inspections
  • Perform general cleaning of all areas of the building
  • Manage routine upkeep of exterior areas and parking lot
  • Complete non-routine cleaning according to specified job orders
  • Remove trash, cardboard, and other recycling daily
  • Handle emergency cleaning and upkeep requests
  • Ensure rooms are maintained and fully equipped
  • Perform manual repairs when necessary
  • Aid maintenance technicians in electrical, lighting, mechanical, plumbing, and machinery repairs
  • Install and troubleshoot primary facility electrical up to 440V lighting, mechanical, and plumbing
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets
 

Equipment Maintenance:

  • Perform routine maintenance tasks on manufacturing machinery and equipment
  • Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic issues
  • Conduct inspections to identify potential problems and implement preventive measures
Equipment Installation:

  • Assist in installing new machinery and production lines
  • Collaborate with engineers and contractors to ensure proper setup
Team Collaboration:

  • Collaborate with all team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets
  • Provide support during scheduled shutdowns and maintenance projects
 

Documentation:

  • Maintain detailed records of maintenance activities and repairs
  • Log equipment downtime and report any recurring issues to the Maintenance Lead and Manager
 

Inventory Management:

  • Monitor and report on the inventory of spare parts and maintenance supplies
  • Request replenishment as needed to maintain adequate stock levels
 

Training and Development:

  • Participate in training programs to improve maintenance skills and product knowledge
  • Complete environmental training program and obtain certification
  • Attend monthly EHS trainings
  • Obtain and maintain IR certification/license for harness and equipment (forklift, scissors, and boom lift)
  • Adhere to the Total Preventative Maintenance Program 
  • Attend Mazak maintenance certification program
  • Follow all policies and procedures (i.e. report on time and ready to work - Start/Lunch/Breaks)
 

Quality Control:

  • Perform quality checks by established quality procedures and ISO requirements
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the assembly process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality
 

Safety Compliance:

  • Follow all safety guidelines, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Report any safety hazards or incidents to supervisors promptly
  • Training and certification in Confined Space and on Lockout Tagout
  • Participate in Waste Management Program
  • Complete all safety training required before use of any equipment
  • Survey buildings and repair mechanical systems in consistence with health and safety regulations
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000 
 

Cleanliness and Organization:

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Follow 5S principles (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain)
 

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 0-3 years’ experience in Maintenance
  • Electrical and mechanical skills, preferred
  • Ability to operate a fork truck and scissor lift
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Fully site based
  • Climate controlled manufacturing plant
  • Protective eyewear and footwear required
Key Competencies:

 

  • Communication
  • Efficiency
  • Productivity
  • Accuracy
  • Teamwork
  • Troubleshooting
  • Problem Solving
  • Detail Oriented
  • Results Driven
  • Adaptability
  • Mechanical Skills
  • Electrical Skills

Job Overview: 
We are currently seeking a precise and detailed individual to join our Machinist team. This role will be responsible for setting up, adjusting, programming with assistance, G-coding, and operating machine tools with guidance to create products according to engineering specifications, ensuring high quality and efficiency in a manufacturing facility. A CNC Machinist works with a team to contribute to production goals and operating various machine tools to produce precision parts and components while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is consistent, a team player, productive, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

Responsibilities: 

  • Set up and run production on all machines while managing tool conditions
  • Program machines with minimal complexity, and learning to program at higher complexity with assistance utilizing Mazatrol and G and M codes
  • Follow and develop standard work for setup, inspection, and deburring
  • Adapt new procedures, techniques, tools, materials, and equipment when needed
  • Meet or exceed production targets and quotas
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets
  • Setup and operate machine tools, including lathes, milling machines, grinders, and CNC machines (CNC Horizontal, CNC Vertical, CNC Turning)
  • Set up and operate at least one category of machines (manual machining, turning centres, milling machines, mill-turn machines, grinders, etc)
  • Select and install appropriate tooling, fixtures, and materials for each job
  • Operate machines to manufacture parts, following detailed blueprints, work instructions, and quality standards
  • Conduct inspections to verify the accuracy and quality of finished products per ISO requirements.
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the machinist process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality
  • Monitor machine performance and adjust to maintain product quality and machine efficiency
  • Use precision measuring instruments such as callipers, micrometres, and gauges to ensure parts meets specified tolerances
  • Perform routine maintenance on machine tools to ensure they operate effectively and safely
  • Troubleshoot and diagnose machine issues, making minor repairs or adjustments
  • Report any significant machine malfunctions or maintenance requirements to the supervisor
  • Document inspection results in SPC data collection workbook
  • Maintain accurate records of production activities, including job setup, run times, and material usage
  • Report any deviations from specifications or quality issues to the appropriate personnel
  • Document any issues, defects, or deviations from standard procedures
  • Complete production logs, work orders, and other required paperwork accurately

Requirements: 

  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 2+ years’ experience in operating CNC machines in a manufaturing enviroment

Core Competencies: 

  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Experience in using Precision Measuring tools (Calipers, Micrometers, Gages Etc)
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Ability to problem solve, with strong verbal and written communication
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000

Preferences: 

  • 2+ years’ experience in manufacturing or other fast paced operations, preferred
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook)
  • Program machines with high complexity, independently utilizing Mazatrol and G and M codes.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Ivyland, PA no travel.

Location: Moody, AL (On-site)

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
Are you a skilled machinist with a passion for precision and innovation? At Ingersoll Rand, we are seeking a talented and dedicated Manual Machinist to join our dynamic team. This is more than just a job; it’s an opportunity to be part of a company that values creativity, excellence, and collaboration.

Responsibilities:

  • Performs set ups of large Liquid Ring Vacuum Pump components and operations of large Vertical & Horizontal Lathes used to repair and overhaul Large Liquid Rind Vacuum Pumps & Compressors.
  • Interprets blueprints/drawings to determine critical dimensions, etc. Ability to read Micrometers, Vernier Calipers, Dial Indicators & other precision measuring & test equipment as required.
  • Able to maintain low tolerances as indicated by specifications or drawings as low as .0005” at times.

Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
Requirements:
  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Core Competencies:
  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner
Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

Pay Range:
Starting Pay will range between $25.00 - $35.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

Job Overview:

The Quality Manager leads quality assurance, quality systems, and improvement activities at the Connersville manufacturing site. This role develops salaried and hourly quality employees and partners with production and site management to identify root causes, implement corrective actions, and improve quality, delivery, and cost performance.

Responsibilities:

  • Plan and direct quality personnel and resources to ensure products and services meet established requirements and customer expectations.
  • Lead and develop salaried and hourly quality employees, communicating business goals, priorities, and performance expectations.
  • Establish quality goals and improvement plans that support site quality, delivery, and cost objectives.
  • Maintain quality systems and oversee audits for compliance with quality plans, applicable regulations, and contract requirements.
  • Partner with production and site management to investigate quality issues, identify root causes, implement corrective actions, and verify effectiveness.
  • Analyze product losses, material review activity, and manufacturing costs to identify and monitor improvement opportunities.
  • Develop quality plans to monitor and report quality-related delays and control out-of-tolerance measuring equipment.
  • Maintain communication across departments and encourage employees to share information, ideas, and improvement suggestions.

Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED with at least four years of professional work experience.
  • At least three additional years of experience in quality system planning, quality improvement methods, and quality assurance.

Core Competencies:

  • Ability to lead employees, establish expectations, and develop direct reports.
  • Ability to analyze quality issues and implement measurable improvements.
  • Verbal, written, and presentation skills, including communication with executive leadership.
  • Ability to collaborate with production, management, and other departments to address customer and business needs.
  • Ability to prioritize activities and manage resources to meet quality, delivery, and cost objectives.

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • Experience with ISO 9001 quality systems and audits.
  • ISO 9001 Lead Auditor qualification.
  • SAP experience and exposure to ETQ.
  • Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt certification.
  • Supervisory experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably machining.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position is based onsite in Connersville, IN, with minimal anticipated travel.
  • Typical working hours are Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m., with some flexibility.
  • Availability by phone is required for occasional off-shift issues and when the hourly workforce works weekends.
  • The role supervises hourly employees across three shifts in a union environment.
  • Relocation assistance is not available within the current hiring budget.

Pay Range:

The pay range for this role is $90,000–$140,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

  Job Title:

 

Industrial Equipment Assembler

 

Location:

 

Ivyland, PA

 

About Us:

 

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems. 

 

Job Summary:

 

We are currently seeking a reliable and motivated individual to join our Milroyal Assembly team. This role will be responsible for assembling, inspecting, and packaging products on an assembly line or independently in a manufacturing facility. A Milroyal Assembler works with a team to ensure the efficient and accurate assembly of products while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is consistent, a team player, a great communicator, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

 

Responsibilities:

 

Assembly:

  • Assemble components and parts following detailed instructions
  • Read and understand the bill of materials and work order instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Complete assembly tasks, use various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses (may use cranes and hoists); Responsibilities may also include specialized work such as tube bending and soldering
  • Stay updated on changes in assembly processes and product specifications
  • Meet or exceed production targets and quotas
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets
 

 

Quality Control:

  • Inspect finished products for quality and adherence to specifications
  • Test and troubleshoot assemblies 
  • Perform quality checks by established quality procedures and ISO requirements
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the assembly process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality
 

Inventory Management:

  • Monitor and request materials and components as needed for assembly
  • Keep track of inventory levels and report shortages
 

Training and Development:

  • Participate in training programs to improve assembly skills and product knowledge
  • Attend monthly EHS trainings
  • Follow all policies and procedures (i.e. report on time and ready to work - Start/Lunch/Breaks)
 

Safety Compliance:

  • Follow all safety guidelines, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Report any safety hazards or incidents to supervisors promptly
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000 
 

Cleanliness and Organization:

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Follow 5S principles (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain)
 

Qualifications:

 

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 0 – 2 years’ experience in assembly or manufacturing, preferred
  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

 

  • Fully site based
  • Climate controlled manufacturing plant
  • Protective eyewear and footwear required
 

Key Competencies:

 

 

  • Communication
  • Efficiency
  • Productivity
  • Accuracy
  • Teamwork
  • Integrity
  • Problem Solving
    • Decision Making
  • Detail Oriented
  • Results Driven
  • Documentation
  • Adaptability

Job title:   Quality Engineer

Location: Alsip, IL

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
The Quality Engineer (QE) ensures that products, manufacturing processes, and Quality Management System (QMS) activities meet established quality standards and regulatory requirements. This role combines technical quality engineering with ownership of key QMS processes, including document control, training, record management, and audit readiness. The QE works cross-functionally with Engineering, Manufacturing, and other teams to support New Product Introduction (NPI) and sustaining operations, ensuring timely execution of validation, risk management, and quality deliverables. The role is also responsible for investigating and resolving nonconformances through CAPA, driving continuous improvement, and supporting the effectiveness of electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control) to ensure data integrity and efficient processes.


Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS), including document control, change management, quality records, electronic QMS (e.g., Master Control), and training, ensuring compliance with FDA, ISO, and internal requirements.
  • Review and approve change controls; oversee calibration and equipment control programs; and drive continuous improvement of QMS processes and systems.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) by ensuring compliance with validation (IQ / OQ / PQ), risk management, statistical analysis, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
  • Partner with Engineering to support sustaining manufacturing, change control, equipment maintenance, revalidation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Perform Device History Record (DHR) reviews; lead or support investigations for nonconformances and CAPAs; and drive root cause analysis, corrective actions, and right-first-time improvements.
  • Lead risk management activities, including risk assessments and pFMEA, and ensure effective mitigation strategies.
  • Lead and support internal, customer, ISO, and FDA audits; represent Quality in customer and supplier interactions; and support supplier qualification and performance monitoring.
  • Support cross-functional and cross-site quality initiatives, special projects, and foster a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.
  • Implement and maintain SPC strategy for manufactured products. 
  • Perform Process Capability Studies (Cp,Cpk) for manufactured products.
  • Act as Quality Manager when QM is offsite
 


Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Quality, Life Sciences, or a related technical field
  • 1+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or a similar role within a medical device or regulated manufacturing environment
  • Must have knowledge and understanding of SPC strategies.
 


Preference: 

  • Working knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including document control, training systems, record retention, and audit support
  • Familiarity with FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 requirements
  • Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) such as Master Control or similar preferred
  • Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including development and revision of SOPs, work instructions, validation documents, and quality records
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Lead Auditor Certification is an advantage
  • Knowledge and understanding of Manufacturing Lean Tools (6S, Gemba, Kaizen, etc…)
 


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based
 

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is $65,000-$80,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What we Offer

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.
 

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Industrial Refrigeration Test Technician
Location: Junction City, OR

 

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

 

Job Overview:

We are seeking a skilled, safety-focused Industrial Refrigeration Test Technician to inspect, commission, troubleshoot, and functionally test industrial glycol and refrigeration chillers prior to shipment.

This position is responsible for verifying that equipment operates safely, performs according to engineering specifications, and meets company quality standards. The ideal candidate is mechanically inclined, comfortable working with refrigeration, electrical, and control systems, and capable of diagnosing and resolving equipment issues in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Perform functional testing, startup, commissioning, and final quality verification of industrial refrigeration systems, chillers, and related equipment prior to shipment.
  • Review engineering documentation including wiring diagrams, piping schematics, bills of material, test procedures, and specifications to ensure equipment is configured and tested correctly.
  • Inspect, operate, and evaluate refrigeration, mechanical, electrical, and control systems while recording operating data and verifying performance against design requirements.
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, refrigeration, controls, and system-performance issues; coordinate corrective actions with Production, Engineering, and Quality teams.
  • Perform leak testing, system evacuation, refrigerant charging, refrigerant recovery, and related activities in accordance with company procedures and regulatory requirements.
  • Navigate and utilize PLCs, HMIs, controllers, variable frequency drives (VFDs), and other control interfaces to support testing, troubleshooting, and equipment verification.
  • Complete test reports, inspection records, refrigerant documentation, and other required quality records while maintaining accurate testing documentation.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives, maintain testing equipment and work areas, assist with training of team members, and perform other related duties as assigned.
 

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • 1+ years of experience in manufacturing, industrial maintenance, HVAC, refrigeration, electrical, controls, or related technical environments.
  • Ability to read and interpret wiring diagrams, refrigeration schematics, piping drawings, bills of material, and technical documentation.
  • Experience using testing, diagnostic, or measurement equipment and documenting results in computer-based systems or electronic records.

Core Competencies: 
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods and regularly bend, kneel, climb, reach, and work around large industrial equipment.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation and safely handle tools, testing equipment, hoses, gauges, and other job-related materials.
  • Follow all company safety policies, PPE requirements, lockout/tagout procedures, electrical safety practices, refrigerant handling requirements, and approved testing procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free work area and promptly report unsafe conditions, equipment concerns, spills, leaks, or near misses.
 

Preferences:

  • Experience testing, servicing, commissioning, or troubleshooting commercial or industrial refrigeration, HVAC, process cooling, or engineered equipment.
  • EPA Section 608 Certification, technical degree, apprenticeship, military technical training, or equivalent hands-on technical experience.
  • Experience working with PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, electrical controls, compressors, pumps, heat exchangers, valves, sensors, and related industrial equipment.
  • Experience performing refrigerant recovery, evacuation, charging, leak testing, brazing, or other refrigeration-related activities; OSHA, electrical safety, or Lockout/Tagout training is a plus.
   

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This is a fully onsite position based in a manufacturing environment and requires a strong commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence. The individual must safely work around electrical equipment, refrigeration systems, pressurized components, moving machinery, and active production operations while complying with all company safety policies and required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements.
