Job Title:

 

Material Handler 

 

Location:

 

Ivyland, PA

 

About Us:

 

Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems. 

 

Job Summary:

 

We are currently seeking a reliable and organized individual to join our Material Handler team. This role will be responsible for ensuring manufacturing facility’s smooth and efficient operation by managing the flow of materials, components, and supplies within a manufacturing facility. A Material Handler works with a team to ensure timely receiving, storing, and distributing materials and maintaining accurate inventory records while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is analytical, a team player, a great communicator, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

 

Responsibilities:

 

Main Responsibilities:

 

  • Transfer incoming parts from Receiving to the warehouse and assembly lines
  • Relocate parts from one department to another
  • Maintain effective communication with various departments, including Production, Procurement, and Quality Control, to ensure the availability of materials as needed
  • Replenish the lines to help maintain the required TAKT time for the cell
  • Assign and move parts to accurate locations both physically and in JD Edwards
  • Pre-draw components for work order completion
  • Assist the support process improvement activities through active participation in continuous improvement
  • Help process MRB related non-conformances
  • Verify intermittent counts of part receipts 
  • Cycle count - based on ABC rules
  • Verify non-inventory "bulk" items and have bins marked
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets
 

Material Handling:

  • Load, unload and move materials throughout the plant using forklifts, pallet jacks, and other equipment as required
  • Inspect materials for quality and quantity
  • Report any discrepancies or damages
  • Prepare materials for outbound shipments, ensure proper packaging and documentation
 

Inventory Management:

  • Track inventory levels and report shortages
  • Maintain accurate records of materials in stock and their locations
 

Documentation:

  • Complete production logs, work orders, and other required paperwork accurately
  • Document any issues, defects, or deviations from standard procedures
 

Material Storage and Issuing:

  • Organize and store materials in designated areas, ensuring they are appropriately labelled and easily accessible
  • Follow FIFO (First In, First Out) principles to manage inventory
  • Issue materials to production teams or other departments as per requisitions, ensuring that the correct quantities are provided promptly
 

Maintenance:

  • Conduct routine maintenance on material handling equipment, such as forklifts, to ensure they are in good working condition
  • Report any equipment malfunctions
 

Quality Control:

  • Inspect finished products for quality and adherence to specifications
  • Perform quality checks by established quality procedures and ISO requirements
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the assembly process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality
 

Training and Development:

  • Participate in training programs to improve material handler skills and product knowledge
  • Obtain and maintain IR certification/license for harness and equipment (Saw, forklift, and scissor lift)
  • Attend monthly EHS trainings
  • Follow all policies and procedures (i.e. report on time and ready to work - Start/Lunch/Breaks)
 

Safety Compliance:

  • Follow all safety guidelines, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Report any safety hazards or incidents to supervisors promptly
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000 
 

Cleanliness and Organization:

  • Maintain a clean and organized work area
  • Follow 5S principles (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain)
 

Qualifications:

 

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalent Diploma (GED), required
  • 0 – 2 years’ experience in Material Handling or manufacturing environment, preferred
  • Ability to operate fork trucks, preferred
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs
 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

 

  • Fully site based
  • Climate controlled manufacturing plant
  • Protective eyewear and footwear required
 

Key Competencies:

 

 

  • Communication
  • Efficiency
  • Productivity
  • Accuracy
  • Teamwork
  • Data Analysis
  • Data Validation
  • Problem Solving
  • Detail Oriented
  • Results Driven
  • Fork Truck
  • Documentation
 

 

What we Offer

 

At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond. 

 

At Milton Roy - Ivyland, we have created a culture that focuses on employee appreciation, development, and growth. We have an Activities Committee that organizes Employee Appreciation events such as monthly luncheons, employee birthday and anniversary snacks, community service efforts, and more.  We love to build teamwork with fun activities such as our annual horseshoe tournament, cornhole competition, and turkey bowl.  We focus on employee growth and development by creating individualized development plans and utilizing skills matrices and metrics to help employees succeed.  We promote from within and aid employees with their growth goals with internal training opportunities as well as access to LinkedIn Learning’s career paths and courses.

Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.


Job Overview:

The Competitive Operations Leader builds and scales competitive service execution capabilities across the Ingersoll Rand Channel, ensuring teams have the processes, training, tools, technical resources, and supply chain readiness needed to support all assets. This role connects strategy to field execution by improving agreement support, vendor and acquisition onboarding, technician enablement, and root-cause resolution across Service, Operations, Supply Chain, Product Management, Sales Enablement, and Customer Center teams.

Responsibilities:

Channel Capability Development

  • Develop and execute a roadmap to grow competitive services capability across sales channels.
  • Identify capability gaps by region and product category; implement corrective actions with Service Operations and Training teams.
  • Create and maintain technical training, job aids, service bulletins, and standardized work for competitive equipment support.

Competitive Service Agreement Execution

  • Monitor competitive service agreement execution, trends, profitability, and customer-impacting issues.
  • Serve as the escalation point for execution challenges and lead structured root-cause resolution.


Supply Chain Process Setup for New Vendors & Acquisitions

  • Partner cross-functionally to document scalable processes, close readiness gaps, and enable channels to quote, order, stock, and service competitive products.
  • Partner with Sourcing on end-to-end supply chain process setup for new competitive vendors, supplier partnerships, and acquisitions.
  • Define ordering, sourcing, stocking, fulfillment, pricing, part identification, and escalation workflows before launch or integration.

Competitive Intelligence & Crowdsourcing

  • Establish repeatable processes for collecting, validating, and sharing competitive insights and field feedback.

Training & Knowledge Management

  • Own competitive services knowledge management, including learning pathways and technical content.
  • Coordinate pilot programs and field validation of new tools, training, and execution processes.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Collaborate with Product Management, Sales Enablement, Service Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Center leadership to support launches and strategic initiatives.
  • Communicate performance metrics, key learnings, and capability improvements to leadership.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Technical Services, Operations, or related field.
  • 7+ years in industrial service, aftermarket operations, technical support, product management, service training, supply chain, or related field.


Core Competencies:

  • Strong analytical, communication, collaboration, and root-cause problem-solving skills.
  • Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority; willingness to travel as needed.

Preference:

  • Experience with compressed air systems, aftermarket service operations, service agreements, or recurring service programs.
  • Familiarity with field service processes, competitive equipment, technician training, Salesforce, Power BI, SharePoint, or learning management systems.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Hybrid position- Onsite Tuesday and Thursdays

Title: CNC Machinist
Location: Ivyland, PA (Onsite)(Milton Roy - 201 Ivyland Rd. Warminster, PA 18974)
Shift: 1st Shift Mon - Fri (7am - 330pm) - Direct Hire, Full time Role

About Us:

Job Overview: 
We are currently seeking a precise and detailed individual to join our Machinist team. This role will be responsible for setting up, adjusting, programming with assistance, G-coding, and operating machine tools with guidance to create products according to engineering specifications, ensuring high quality and efficiency in a manufacturing facility. A CNC Machinist works with a team to contribute to production goals and operating various machine tools to produce precision parts and components while adhering to safety and quality standards. The ideal candidate is consistent, a team player, productive, and can meet deadlines and prioritize multiple projects.

Responsibilities: 

  • Set up and run production on all machines while managing tool conditions
  • Program machines with minimal complexity, and learning to program at higher complexity with assistance utilizing Mazatrol and G and M codes
  • Follow and develop standard work for setup, inspection, and deburring
  • Adapt new procedures, techniques, tools, materials, and equipment when needed
  • Meet or exceed production targets and quotas
  • Collaborate with team members to optimize workflow and achieve daily and monthly targets
  • Setup and operate machine tools, including lathes, milling machines, grinders, and CNC machines (CNC Horizontal, CNC Vertical, CNC Turning)
  • Set up and operate at least one category of machines (manual machining, turning centres, milling machines, mill-turn machines, grinders, etc)
  • Select and install appropriate tooling, fixtures, and materials for each job
  • Operate machines to manufacture parts, following detailed blueprints, work instructions, and quality standards
  • Conduct inspections to verify the accuracy and quality of finished products per ISO requirements.
  • Identify and report defects or issues in the machinist process and necessary adjustments or repairs to ensure product quality
  • Monitor machine performance and adjust to maintain product quality and machine efficiency
  • Use precision measuring instruments such as callipers, micrometres, and gauges to ensure parts meets specified tolerances
  • Perform routine maintenance on machine tools to ensure they operate effectively and safely
  • Troubleshoot and diagnose machine issues, making minor repairs or adjustments
  • Report any significant machine malfunctions or maintenance requirements to the supervisor
  • Document inspection results in SPC data collection workbook
  • Maintain accurate records of production activities, including job setup, run times, and material usage
  • Report any deviations from specifications or quality issues to the appropriate personnel
  • Document any issues, defects, or deviations from standard procedures
  • Complete production logs, work orders, and other required paperwork accurately

Requirements: 

  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 2+ years’ experience in operating CNC machines in a manufaturing enviroment

Core Competencies: 

  • Experience using various hand, pneumatic, and power tools, such as screwdrivers, wrenches, drills, and presses
  • Experience in using Precision Measuring tools (Calipers, Micrometers, Gages Etc)
  • Ability to read and understand the bill of materials and work instructions, blueprints, or technical drawings
  • Ability to problem solve, with strong verbal and written communication
  • Demonstrated time management skills, strategic thinking, and adaptability
  • Lift a maximum of 35 lbs for an individual and 70 lbs for a team lift
  • Test PSI limit no greater than 30,000

Preferences: 

  • 2+ years’ experience in manufacturing or other fast paced operations, preferred
  • General computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook)
  • Program machines with high complexity, independently utilizing Mazatrol and G and M codes.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Ivyland, PA no travel.

About Us: 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician for Ingersoll Rand's Compression Systems and Services Division serves customers by installing, troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating and/or Centac and ECC air compressors, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic troubleshooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment.

Responsibilities:
In addition to performing preventative maintenance on Ingersoll Rand compressed air equipment, our service techs will interact with customers to address existing and unanticipated equipment concerns. Collaborate with Service Coordinator on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. All service technicians will assist and train apprentices and Field Service Technicians.
  • Effectively communicates verbally and in writing with customers and co-workers.
  • Provides technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems.  Including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement with limited guidance from the Master Technician.
  • Increases Ingersoll Rand customers awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services, and solutions, such as Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits and Leak Detection can benefit their operations.
Requirements:
  • 2 years+ experience of troubleshooting industrial/commercial mechanical systems.
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • Every service technician is required to be on-call, but you will not be on-call for the first 90 days to get used to the schedule. This is shared with every service tech, and it requires being available 24/7 for the 1-week duration where you will go to customer sites. On-call weeks can be as often as every 4 weeks or greater than 4 weeks, but that will be determined by the hiring manager.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling.  It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Core Competencies:
  • Able to read wiring schematics and diagrams for all equipment.
  • Advanced network systems installations (IMMC/ASC, X Series Automation).
  • Basic vibration troubleshooting.
  • Basic Air Quality (system compressor/dryer – air treatment).
  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.  Working proficiency with handheld computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Maintain proper business travel practices in a cost-efficient manner
Preferences:
  • Industrial air compressor maintenance & knowledge.
  • EPA Certification.
  • Veterans/Active-Duty Military are encouraged to apply.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
  • Service Technicians will travel daily in a 3-hour radius within our service area.

Location: Multiple positions located across the Southwest Customer Center Locations: Pomona, CA

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and the planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future!

Job Summary:

Ingersoll Rand’s Compression Systems and Services Customer Center is hiring an Account Manager to join their team. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the Customer Center equipment sales and service activity for a specific territory in the Region. Traveling in a defined geographic area, this includes quoting, strategizing, prospecting, and developing relationships to achieve revenue targets, maximize profits, increase market share and maintain customer loyalty while achieving organizational goals. The position is a unique blend of supporting a major distributor and selling direct to customers.

Responsibilities:

  • Generate Revenue - Responsible for generating sales of equipment, service contracts, and service offerings with our direct end users and partners selling to a defined customer base within a geographic area. Develop existing customer base and secure new, competitive accounts to expand IR presence in the market. Provide and design compressed air solutions to fulfil industrial customer needs. Products include compressed air equipment, accessories, turnkey installations, service contracts, parts, service, rental equipment and energy audits. Keep current with all product knowledge, industry standards and training needed. Execute strategy for continuous improvement and exceeding customer satisfaction. Achieve all assigned sales targets.
  • Develop People Capabilities - Provide selling skills and product/services training for dealer sales personnel (as required) as well as personnel within the Customer Center. Partner with services team to best understand products and services and satisfy and anticipate customer’s needs.
  • Manage Cash - Ensure that all orders obtained are error-free with correct customer documentation. Ensure resolution of all customer disputes. Manage all costs associated with selling efforts, including travel and entertainment expenditures.
  • Ensure adherence to safety rules (vehicle safety, customer site safety) in the field, as well as in the Customer Center.
  • Earn Customer loyalty by collaborating cross functionally. Leverage best support for customers by partnering with service team to help troubleshoot customer issues or offer unique solutions.
  • Maintain Customer Relationship Management database including face-to-face customer interactions, assets, agreements, contacts, and opportunities in order management system. Record order follow-up activities (e.g. delivery), reporting requirements (email) and database requirements. Provide feedback on market conditions. Responsible for driving and tracking sales pipeline of all account activity and daily reporting.

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma
  • 4+ years’ experience in an industrial sales business setting or successful completion of the Ingersoll Rand Sales Development Program (SDP).

Core Competencies:

  • Excellent relationship-building and interpersonal skills, including verbal, written and presentation communication skills.
  • Establishes and builds solid relationships with customers, key institutions and team members
  • Honest, self-motivated and team oriented.
  • Able to work within a team environment and independently.
  • Mechanical and electrical expertise required.
  • Ability to assess customer needs, analyze and interpret, perform basic equipment performance calculations, and to recommend technical solutions
  • Tech savvy; knowledge of Salesforce or other CRM software is preferred
  • Proven business and sales acumen, including the ability to prospect accounts, effectively navigate within a customer organization, value sell, and win competitive accounts
  • Must have excellent prioritization and time management skills

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or equivalent
  • Knowledge of Salesforce

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Regional travel to customer sites is required within assigned geographic territory.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations included, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, Multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.

The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $60,000 - $80,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Customer Success Manager – EcoPlant
Location: Remote – Continental United States

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

EcoPlant combines software as a service (SaaS), industrial Internet of Things (IoT) technology, and predictive analytics to monitor, control, and optimize compressed-air systems. Its platform helps customers improve energy efficiency and reliability while understanding system performance, operating costs, and savings.

Job Overview:

The Customer Success Manager serves as a key point of contact for EcoPlant customers and channel partners, helping them understand and recognize value from the platform. Beginning after system installation, this role leads customer onboarding, provides dashboard training, and coordinates ongoing support. Working closely with account managers, Technical Support, Engineering, and Product teams, the Customer Success Manager translates system data into clear insights, supports business reviews and renewal discussions, and helps improve the overall customer experience.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead customer onboarding following system installation, helping users understand the EcoPlant dashboard, system information, and platform capabilities.
  • Build and maintain relationships with customers and channel partners, serving as an ongoing contact for platform questions, training, and support needs.
  • Provide training to customer contacts and new users, supporting continued platform adoption as customer personnel, equipment, or requirements change.
  • Review platform data to help customers understand compressed-air system performance, energy consumption, operating costs, and savings.
  • Identify system performance concerns and improvement opportunities, partnering with technical resources to evaluate findings and coordinate appropriate actions.
  • Prepare and deliver quarterly or annual business reviews, as needed, to communicate customer value and align on financial, operational, and sustainability goals.
  • Support account managers and channel partners with renewal and expansion conversations by preparing performance highlights, customer value summaries, and supporting information.
  • Coordinate with Technical Support, Engineering, Operations, and R&D to address customer concerns and follow issues through resolution.
  • Document customer feedback and submit product enhancement requests to Product and R&D teams, including colleagues in Israel.
  • Establish repeatable onboarding, training, communication, and customer success practices, and support customer case studies and performance documentation.

Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 2–5 years of experience with industrial compressed-air systems.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong customer relationship skills with the ability to build trust and understand customer and channel partner priorities.
  • Clear written, verbal, and presentation communication skills when working with technical users, commercial stakeholders, and customer leadership.
  • Ability to onboard and train customers, explain platform features, and support continued adoption.
  • Technical aptitude with the ability to learn industrial systems and software and interpret technical information.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to review data, identify trends, and communicate performance and customer value.
  • Ability to collaborate across technical, commercial, and product teams and influence outcomes without direct authority.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel and PowerPoint, and the ability to learn business systems and customer-facing software.
  • Strong organization, attention to detail, initiative, and follow-through while managing competing customer needs in a remote environment.

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, or a related field.
  • Customer success, technical account management, sales engineering, customer service, or other customer-facing experience in an industrial environment.
  • Experience with industrial IoT, condition monitoring, cloud platforms, or software/services solutions.
  • Experience onboarding customers, delivering platform training, presenting business reviews, or communicating measurable customer value.
  • Experience as a compressed-air system auditor or sales engineer.
  • Participation in or completion of the Ingersoll Rand Sales Development Program.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements
This position is fully remote within the continental United States. Candidates should have access to a major airport for business travel. Travel up to 30% across North America may be required, although actual travel is expected to be infrequent and based on customer and business needs, including customer meetings and system performance reviews.

Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, including incentives, is $90,000–$145,000. The actual pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed pay range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Ingersoll Rand, it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Title: Senior Maintenance Technician
Location: Chicago, IL (Onsite)
Shift: Day Shift, 4:00 a.m.–12:30 p.m. | Full-Time, Direct Hire
 

Job Overview:

The Senior Maintenance Technician coordinates and performs high-level mechanical, electrical, thermal, and fluid power maintenance on specialized production equipment within a rubber molding manufacturing facility. This role focuses on minimizing machine downtime, diagnosing complex system failures, ensuring compliance with strict safety standards, and mentoring junior technicians. The ideal candidate possesses robust technical knowledge of high-pressure hydraulic presses, steam or electric heating platens, automated control systems, and heavy industrial machinery.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Troubleshoot, overhaul, and repair multi-stage high-pressure hydraulic molding presses, accumulators, cylinders, directional valves, and proportional pumps.
  •  Diagnose automated machinery inputs/outputs, variable frequency drives (VFDs), industrial sensors, relays, and PLC-controlled systems up to 480V.
  • Read, interpret, and troubleshoot PLC ladder logic.
  •  Inspect, maintain, and repair steam boiler lines, electric heating platens, temperature controllers, hot oil heating units, and cooling water tower circuits.
  • Lead major machinery overhauls, including replacing large bearings, gearboxes, drive shafts, and automated transport mechanisms.
  •  Safely execute heavy rigging to relocate or realign molding presses and equipment.
  •  Execute, document, and optimize preventive and predictive maintenance programs using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).
  •  Audit parts inventory and maintain accurate maintenance records.
  •  Lead emergency troubleshooting during active production breakdowns.
  • Assign daily work orders, monitor progress, and mentor junior maintenance technicians.
  •  Adhere to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), NFPA 70E, OSHA, and all company safety procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  •  Perform additional duties as assigned.
Requirements:

  •  Minimum of 5 years of industrial plant maintenance experience.
  • Minimum of 2 years of maintenance experience in a rubber molding, plastic injection molding, or heavy industrial manufacturing environment.
  •  Technical trade school degree, vocational certification, or formal mechanical/electrical apprenticeship preferred.
  • Intermediate Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
  •  Experience troubleshooting Allen-Bradley and Siemens PLCs.
  • Ability to read and interpret hydraulic schematics, electrical wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and pneumatic layouts.
  •  Verified Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) training.
  • Forklift, aerial lift, and overhead crane certifications are preferred.
  •  Proficiency using digital multimeters, insulation testers, hydraulic pressure gauges, precision micrometers, welding equipment, and heavy rigging tools.
  Core Competencies:

  •  Strong mechanical, hydraulic, electrical, and PLC troubleshooting skills.
  •  Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  •  Excellent communication and leadership skills.
  •  Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  •  Commitment to workplace safety and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to mentor and train junior maintenance technicians.
  •  Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
  Physical Demands & Working Environment:

  •  Routinely lift, carry, and manipulate materials weighing up to 75 pounds.
  •  Climb ladders, work at heights, crawl into confined spaces, and stand or walk on concrete floors for 8–12-hour shifts.
  • Work around elevated temperatures, steam systems, chemical odors, and high-noise manufacturing environments while wearing required PPE.
  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This position will be based at our Chicago, IL facility with no anticipated travel. This is a fully site-based position.

 

Pay Range:

Starting pay will range from $40.00–$45.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

Job Overview:
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Sourcing Engineer to join our Compression Systems & Services Americas Sourcing Organization. This role involves supporting the development, implementation, and management of sourcing strategies to provide optimal supply assurance, pricing, flexibility, quality, and delivery performance. The Sourcing Engineer collaborates with engineering, operations, and quality teams, as well as key suppliers, to meet cost, quality, and delivery targets while fostering positive supplier relationships.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead supplier selection, negotiations, and RFP processes, including pricing, payment terms, lead times, and inventory programs, while fostering strong supplier relationships.
  • Identify and implement cost-saving opportunities through data analysis, hands-on material reviews, and continuous improvement ideation sessions aligned with plant priorities.
  • Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams to qualify new parts, address supplier performance issues, and ensure alignment with operational strategies like localization and plant rationalization.
  • Support new product development (NPD) activities by managing preliminary project costs, driving procurement efforts, and aligning with business cases through product launch.

Title: CNC Programming & Mold Maker
Location: St. Francis, WI - Onsite (Sheridan Molding and Engineering - 4140 S Nevada Ave. St Francis, WI 53235) 
Shift: 1st Shift Mon - Fri (6am - 3pm)

 
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

 
Job Overview:
The CNC Programmer and Mold Maker will be responsible for setting up, operating, programming CNC machines to produce precision parts and components according to specifications. This role requires a strong understanding of machining processes, attention to detail, and a commitment to quality and safety.
 
Responsibilities:

  • Working with CNC Programming Software to make 2D images to measurement to run on the CNC Machines.
  • Set up, operate, and program CNC machines (e.g., mills, lathes, routers) to perform precision machining tasks.
  • Read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, and CAD files.
  • Work with a variety of materials to produce precision mold components
  • Load raw materials and tooling into machines and monitor operations.
  • Inspect finished products for quality and adherence to specifications using measuring tools (e.g., calipers, micrometers).
  • Perform routine maintenance and troubleshooting on machines.
  • Maintain accurate production records and documentation.
  • Collaborate with engineers and production staff to optimize machining processes.
  • Follow all safety protocols and maintain a clean and organized work area.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 3+ years of experience G-code or CNC programming in a manufacturing environment.

Core Competencies: 
  • Familiarity with tight tolerance work
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Good communication skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to stand for extended periods.
  • Exposure to noise, dust, and machinery in a shop environment.

Preferences: 
  • Proficiency in reading blueprints and using precision measuring instruments. 
  • Manual dexterity and ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements: 
This position will be based at our St. Francis, WI facility.

Location: Mocksville, NC (Onsite) (338 Valley Rd. Mocksville, NC 27028) 
Shift: 3rd shift, 630pm to 630am working 4 on and 4 off (Rotating Schedule) - Direct Hire - Full time role

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Maintenance Techincian is responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of the CNC machines and manuafcturing machines. This role will deal with CNC Machines and working with PLC and Electronic Compents of our manufacturing machines.

Responsibilities:

  • Makes major electrical, mechanical, and construction repairs and installation involving schematics and/or blueprint interpretation.
  • Troubleshoots drive related issues to component level for Fanuc, Siemens, Allen Bradley and other brands of controllers.
  • Determines root cause of failures and recommends preventive actions.  Communicates same through work order system comments/history.
  • Communicates consistently with internal customers regarding status of equipment in shop.
  • Advises supervisor of needs for outside services and works with service representatives on equipment and controls repair and installation. Shows competency in several crafts and performs handyman aspects in all trades.
  • Constructs sketches of mechanical or construction alterations/installations and electrical circuitry.
  • Prepares bills of material on jobs requiring major material use and initiates purchase requisitions.
  • Makes day to day work-related decisions.
  • Uses various material handling equipment such as hoists, carts, lifts, fork trucks and hand trucks in moving light to heavy weight material. 
  • Uses a variety of lock-out/tag-out devices as required per plant LOTO Plan. 

Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2+ years of experience in Electronic Manufacturing Maintenance or industrial Maintenance

Key Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Exhibits team work skills
  • Ability to stand and walk up to 8 hours continuously during a shift.
  • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs alone, or 70 lbs with assistance, repeatedly over an 8 hour shift
  • Ability to push or pull up to 35 lbs.
  • Ability to see or have vision corrected with glasses/contacts to an evaluated level of no worse than 20/35.

Preferences:

  • Associates degree or higher in Electronic Technology or must show enrollment into course work for associates degree within 12 months of employment
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair pneumatic, hydraulic, electrical, electronic, CNC machines and controls. 
  • Ability to work with concepts when detailed prints, drawings, and specifications are not available.
  • Ability to maintain technical documentation for equipment and processes.
  • Ability to maintain mechanical machine tools to include lathes, grinders, mills, drills, machining centers, and other similar equipment.
  • Ability to interpret schematics and blueprints.
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Mocksville, NC, with no anticipated travel.

Job Overview: 
The Maintenance Techincian is responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of the CNC machines and manuafcturing machines. This role will deal with CNC Machines and working with PLC and Electronic Compents of our manufacturing machines.

Responsibilities:

  • Makes major electrical, mechanical, and construction repairs and installation involving schematics and/or blueprint interpretation.
  • Troubleshoots drive related issues to component level for Fanuc, Siemens, Allen Bradley and other brands of controllers.
  • Determines root cause of failures and recommends preventive actions.  Communicates same through work order system comments/history.
  • Communicates consistently with internal customers regarding status of equipment in shop.
  • Advises supervisor of needs for outside services and works with service representatives on equipment and controls repair and installation. Shows competency in several crafts and performs handyman aspects in all trades.
  • Constructs sketches of mechanical or construction alterations/installations and electrical circuitry.
  • Prepares bills of material on jobs requiring major material use and initiates purchase requisitions.
  • Makes day to day work-related decisions.
  • Uses various material handling equipment such as hoists, carts, lifts, fork trucks and hand trucks in moving light to heavy weight material. 
  • Uses a variety of lock-out/tag-out devices as required per plant LOTO Plan. 

Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2+ years of experience in Electronic Manufacturing Maintenance or industrial Maintenance

Key Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Exhibits team work skills
  • Ability to stand and walk up to 8 hours continuously during a shift.
  • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs alone, or 70 lbs with assistance, repeatedly over an 8 hour shift
  • Ability to push or pull up to 35 lbs.
  • Ability to see or have vision corrected with glasses/contacts to an evaluated level of no worse than 20/35.

Preferences:

  • Associates degree or higher in Electronic Technology or must show enrollment into course work for associates degree within 12 months of employment
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair pneumatic, hydraulic, electrical, electronic, CNC machines and controls. 
  • Ability to work with concepts when detailed prints, drawings, and specifications are not available.
  • Ability to maintain technical documentation for equipment and processes.
  • Ability to maintain mechanical machine tools to include lathes, grinders, mills, drills, machining centers, and other similar equipment.
  • Ability to interpret schematics and blueprints.
 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:
This position will be based at our site in Mocksville, NC, with no anticipated travel.

Title: Senior Maintenance Technician
Location: Chicago, IL (Onsite)
Shift: Day Shift, 4:00 a.m.–12:30 p.m. | Full-Time, Direct Hire
 

Job Overview:

The Senior Maintenance Technician coordinates and performs high-level mechanical, electrical, thermal, and fluid power maintenance on specialized production equipment within a rubber molding manufacturing facility. This role focuses on minimizing machine downtime, diagnosing complex system failures, ensuring compliance with strict safety standards, and mentoring junior technicians. The ideal candidate possesses robust technical knowledge of high-pressure hydraulic presses, steam or electric heating platens, automated control systems, and heavy industrial machinery.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Troubleshoot, overhaul, and repair multi-stage high-pressure hydraulic molding presses, accumulators, cylinders, directional valves, and proportional pumps.
  •  Diagnose automated machinery inputs/outputs, variable frequency drives (VFDs), industrial sensors, relays, and PLC-controlled systems up to 480V.
  • Read, interpret, and troubleshoot PLC ladder logic.
  •  Inspect, maintain, and repair steam boiler lines, electric heating platens, temperature controllers, hot oil heating units, and cooling water tower circuits.
  • Lead major machinery overhauls, including replacing large bearings, gearboxes, drive shafts, and automated transport mechanisms.
  •  Safely execute heavy rigging to relocate or realign molding presses and equipment.
  •  Execute, document, and optimize preventive and predictive maintenance programs using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).
  •  Audit parts inventory and maintain accurate maintenance records.
  •  Lead emergency troubleshooting during active production breakdowns.
  • Assign daily work orders, monitor progress, and mentor junior maintenance technicians.
  •  Adhere to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), NFPA 70E, OSHA, and all company safety procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  •  Perform additional duties as assigned.
Requirements:

  •  Minimum of 5 years of industrial plant maintenance experience.
  • Minimum of 2 years of maintenance experience in a rubber molding, plastic injection molding, or heavy industrial manufacturing environment.
  •  Technical trade school degree, vocational certification, or formal mechanical/electrical apprenticeship preferred.
  • Intermediate Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
  •  Experience troubleshooting Allen-Bradley and Siemens PLCs.
  • Ability to read and interpret hydraulic schematics, electrical wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and pneumatic layouts.
  •  Verified Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) training.
  • Forklift, aerial lift, and overhead crane certifications are preferred.
  •  Proficiency using digital multimeters, insulation testers, hydraulic pressure gauges, precision micrometers, welding equipment, and heavy rigging tools.
  Core Competencies:

  •  Strong mechanical, hydraulic, electrical, and PLC troubleshooting skills.
  •  Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  •  Excellent communication and leadership skills.
  •  Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  •  Commitment to workplace safety and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to mentor and train junior maintenance technicians.
  •  Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
  Physical Demands & Working Environment:

  •  Routinely lift, carry, and manipulate materials weighing up to 75 pounds.
  •  Climb ladders, work at heights, crawl into confined spaces, and stand or walk on concrete floors for 8–12-hour shifts.
  • Work around elevated temperatures, steam systems, chemical odors, and high-noise manufacturing environments while wearing required PPE.
  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This position will be based at our Chicago, IL facility with no anticipated travel. This is a fully site-based position.

 

Pay Range:

Starting pay will range from $40.00–$45.00 per hour depending on qualifications and experience. This is a full-time, hourly position.

Job Title: Controls Application Engineer – Lone Star Turbo

Location: Houston, Texas

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Job Overview
Process Flow Technologies is hiring for a Controls Application Engineer for our Lone Star Turbo business based in Houston, TX. This role is responsible for reviewing customer inquiries, specifications, and project requirements and developing accurate technical and commercial proposals for industrial control panel systems for blowers, compressors, and related equipment.

This position is ideal for a recent engineering graduate or early-career professional interested in industrial automation, control systems, and customer-focused engineering solutions. The role provides hands on exposure to industrial control panels, PLCs, HMIs, instrumentation, and proposal development processes while working alongside experienced engineering professionals.

The Controls Application Engineer serves as the technical lead during the quotation phase, working closely with customers, sales, engineering, procurement, and manufacturing to define project scope, develop cost estimates, select major equipment and control panel components, and deliver competitive proposals. This position requires the ability to interpret customer requirements and industry standards while balancing technical solutions, project risks, manufacturability, and commercial objectives.

Responsibilities

  • Review customer RFQs, specifications, datasheets, drawings, and commercial requirements.
  • Interpret customer requirements and develop technical solutions for industrial control panels and automation systems.
  • Define scope of supply, system architecture, and major equipment requirements.
  • Develop detailed cost estimates including material, labor, engineering, testing, and subcontracted services.
  • Select and specify major control panel components including PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, instrumentation, motor control, networking equipment, and power distribution devices.
  • Prepare technical and commercial proposals, quotations, and bid documentation.
  • Identify project risks, technical exceptions, clarifications, and compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate with engineering, procurement, manufacturing, and suppliers to obtain accurate pricing and technical information.
  • Participate in customer meetings, team kickoffs, bid reviews, and technical clarification discussions.
  • Ensure proposals comply with customer specifications and applicable industry standards including NEC, UL 508A, and other project-specific requirements.
  • Maintain proposal documentation, estimating tools, pricing databases, and historical project records.
  • Contribute to ongoing improvements in estimating processes, proposal quality, and competitiveness.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or a related discipline.
  • Internship, co-op, or senior design project in industrial automation, controls, or electrical systems.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, electrical schematics, and P&IDs.

Core Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
  • Eagerness to learn industrial control panel design, proposal development, estimating, and customer specifications.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple proposals and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.

Preferred experience

  • Internship or coursework related to automation, controls, electrical design, or industrial systems.
  • Exposure to PLC platforms such as Rockwell Automation, Phoenix Contact, Siemens, Schneider Electric, or other industrial automation platforms.
  • Familiarity with AutoCAD or similar engineering software.
  • Knowledge of industrial networking, instrumentation, or SCADA systems.
  • Experience working on team-based engineering projects.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

Full-time, on-site position at 8883 West Monroe Rd, Houston, Texas 77061. May need to work outside of normal business hours as needed.

Job Overview:
We are looking for a skilled assembler to perform a variety of tasks as assigned in conjunction with the assembly of our product. You will ensure all parts fit correctly and are suitable for the final product. This position is responsible for safely performing high-level continuous work to quality standards. Assignments may change based on business demands.


Responsibilities:

  • Perform a variety of tasks to support the assembly and test of industrial machinery and compression equipment within the plant, in accordance with predetermined standard work.
  • Read, understand, and apply method sheets, assembly diagrams, and blueprints.
  • Detect quality defects and unsafe conditions.
  • Be knowledgeable and follow all applicable safety rules and procedures.
  • Interpretation of drawings and specifications to determine dimensions, identify materials for construction, and assemble components.
  • Operate power pneumatic and hand tools required for performing job duties.
  • Maintain and inspect tools and equipment and create work orders for repaired as needed.
  • Loading and unloading of equipment utilizing fork trucks, and hoists.

Job Summary
Process Flow Technologies is hiring for a Controls Application Engineer for our Lone Star Turbo business based in Houston, TX. This role is responsible for reviewing customer inquiries, specifications, and project requirements and developing accurate technical and commercial proposals for industrial control panel systems for blowers, compressors, and related equipment.

The Controls Application Engineer serves as the technical lead during the quotation phase, working closely with customers, sales, engineering, procurement, and manufacturing to define project scope, develop cost estimates, select major equipment and control panel components, and deliver competitive proposals. This position requires the ability to interpret customer requirements and industry standards while balancing technical solutions, project risks, manufacturability, and commercial objectives.

Responsibilities

  • Review customer RFQs, specifications, datasheets, drawings, and commercial requirements.
  • Interpret customer requirements and develop technical solutions for industrial control panels and automation systems.
  • Define scope of supply, system architecture, and major equipment requirements.
  • Develop detailed cost estimates including material, labor, engineering, testing, and subcontracted services.
  • Select and specify major control panel components including PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, instrumentation, motor control, networking equipment, and power distribution devices.
  • Prepare technical and commercial proposals, quotations, and bid documentation.
  • Identify project risks, technical exceptions, clarifications, and compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate with engineering, procurement, manufacturing, and suppliers to obtain accurate pricing and technical information.
  • Participate in customer meetings, team kickoffs, bid reviews, and technical clarification discussions.
  • Ensure proposals comply with customer specifications and applicable industry standards including NEC, UL 508A, and other project-specific requirements.
  • Maintain proposal documentation, estimating tools, pricing databases, and historical project records.
  • Contribute to ongoing improvements in estimating processes, proposal quality, and competitiveness.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or a related discipline. Equivalent industry experience may be considered.
  • 2+ years of experience reviewing customer specifications and developing technical proposals for industrial equipment, control systems, or engineered products.
  • 2+ years ability to interpret electrical, mechanical, process, and instrumentation documentation.
  • 2+ years of industrial control panels, PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, instrumentation, motor control systems, and automation equipment.

Key Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Knowledge of NEC, UL 508A, and applicable industrial control panel standards.
  • Experience preparing cost estimates and evaluating project scope, risk, and schedule requirements.
  • Ability to read and understand electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, P&IDs, and engineering drawings.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple proposals and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.

Preferred experience

  • Experience preparing proposals for industrial control panels, compressor systems, blower packages, turbomachinery, or process equipment.
  • Experience with Rockwell Automation, Phoenix Contact, Siemens, Schneider Electric, or other industrial automation platforms.
  • Familiarity with UL 508A panel design practices and industrial control panel manufacturing.
  • Experience using estimating, ERP, CRM, or configuration management software.
  • Knowledge of process instrumentation, industrial networking, and SCADA systems.
  • Understanding of project execution, commissioning, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), and field service activities.
  • Prior experience in applications engineering, sales engineering, or proposal engineering environments.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

Full-time, on-site position at 8883 West Monroe Rd, Houston, Texas 77061. May need to work outside of normal business hours as needed.

Job Overview: Fruitland Manufacturing is seeking an experienced CNC Machinist to join our growing team in Stoney Creek, Ontario. Due to increased production demands and additional work being brought into the facility, we are adding two Machinists to support our operations.

This is an excellent opportunity for a skilled machinist with strong CNC setup, troubleshooting, and programming experience. We are looking for professionals who can independently set up tooling, make programming adjustments, perform inspections, and ensure high-quality production while maintaining a safe and productive work environment.
The successful candidate will work primarily on CNC machining centers utilizing Fanuc controls and will play a key role in producing precision components that support mission-critical applications across multiple industries.
Please note: This position currently operates on a day shift schedule; however, candidates must be willing and able to transition to a future second-shift operation if business needs require it. A $2.00 per hour shift premium applies to second-shift assignments.

Responsibilities
  • Operate CNC horizontal, vertical, and multi-axis turning centers.
  • Perform machine setups, including tooling changes, fixture setup, program loading, and first-piece inspections.
  • Perform basic CNC programming and make adjustments directly at the machine controller.
  • Organize tooling requirements and verify fixture readiness for production jobs.
  • Troubleshoot CNC programming issues and machine fault codes.
  • Maintain precise tolerances and quality standards during production.
  • Follow all plant safety requirements and ISO procedures.
  • Log and track production activities using the GSS ERP system.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  • Collaborate with team members to achieve production and quality objectives.
Requirements
 
  • Operating CNC horizontal, vertical and multi-axis turning centers.
  • Performing basic CNC programming.
  • Setting up CNC machine including changing tools, fixtures, running programs, completing first off inspections
  • Identifying and resolving programming issues and CNC fault codes.
  • Maintaining sharp focus and attention to detail to ensure precision and quality in all operations.
  • Following all plant safety rules, ISO procedures
  • Logging and tracking time using GSS ERP system

Requirements:

  • Minimum 5+ years of CNC machining experience.
  • Strong CNC machine setup experience.
  • Experience operating CNC machining centers with Fanuc controls preferred.
  • Ability to perform basic CNC programming and troubleshooting.
  • Experience with tooling selection, fixture setup, and process optimization.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.
Qualifications:

  • Experience operating CNC horizontal, vertical, and multi-axis machining centers.
  • Strong understanding of CNC setup and production processes.
  • Ability to identify and resolve programming and machine issues.
  • Knowledge of precision measurement tools and inspection techniques.
  • Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide using whole numbers, fractions, and decimals.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational abilities.
 Preferred Qualifications: Red Seal certification in 429A General Machinist or 430A Tool and Die Maker.

Job Title: Service Supervisor, Commercial Compressed Air
Location: Indianapolis, IN (Hybrid)

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:

Take the lead in delivering exceptional customer service, developing a high-performing technical team, and driving business growth! As a Service Supervisor, you'll lead the local service operation within our compressed air business, ensuring customers receive outstanding support throughout the full lifecycle of their equipment. You'll coach and develop a team of Service Technicians responsible for installing, maintaining, and repairing rotary screw and reciprocating air compressors and compressed air system components across multiple manufacturers. Working closely with sales and service coordination teams, you'll strengthen customer relationships, improve operational efficiency, identify opportunities to expand service business, and drive overall customer satisfaction. Beyond leading daily service operations, you'll have ownership of the Service P&L for your Customer Center, directly influencing profitability, technician utilization, and business performance. This regional leadership opportunity is based in Zionsville, Indiana, just outside Indianapolis, with travel throughout the assigned service territory, including Northern Indiana (Fort Wayne, Goshen, South Bend).


Responsibilities:

  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.


Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 5+ years of relevant services experience, ideally in an industrial sales business environment.
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.


Core Competencies:

  • Solid professional communication skills both verbal and written.
  • Advanced operating knowledge with Microsoft Office and general business applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of handheld and mobile technologies (smartphones, tablets) and network-based systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of financial impacts related to process efficiency, cost control, and business performance.
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions at times requires interpretation or deviation from standard processes including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.


Preference:

  • Associate's or Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or a relevant area
  • Managing budgets and processes


Travel & Work Arrangements:

  • This role is Hybrid, with travel, from Indianapolis, IN (Zionsville)
  • Territory includes: Northern Indiana, (Fort Wayne, Goshen, South Bend)
  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Base Salary with bonus incentives
  • Regional travel approximately 20% to customer sites

This position will have some work outdoors and in mechanical or equipment rooms, will include physical demands and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling. It requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy.


What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Quality Engineer                
Location:  Monroe, LA
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
At Ingersoll Rand’s Monroe, Louisiana facility, precision-engineered products play a critical role in equipment customers depend on every day. The site manufactures and services THOMAS air compressor and vacuum pump products within an OEM portfolio serving medical, laboratory, environmental, and industrial markets. In this hands-on manufacturing environment, quality is measured not just by what leaves the line, but by how reliably the product performs for the customer—creating a meaningful opportunity to strengthen processes, systems, and overall plant performance.

We’re seeking a Quality Engineer who is a hands-on individual contributor focused on strengthening quality performance across the Monroe facility by turning quality challenges into sustainable process improvements. Rather than simply reacting to defects, this engineer will look at quality through the customer’s eyes—identifying trends, uncovering root causes, and building the processes, standards, controls, and corrective actions that prevent issues from recurring.  Partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Production, Customer Service, and Supply Chain, this role will apply proven manufacturing quality practices—including process controls, quality metrics, and customer-focused problem solving—to improve process capability, reduce cost of poor quality, address customer complaints and returns, and strengthen overall product performance.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on manufacturing quality experience, can quickly understand the operation, and is comfortable taking ownership and driving improvements with a high degree of independence. This is an opportunity for a builder—not simply a maintainer: someone energized by improving what exists, creating what is missing, and helping establish stronger, more sustainable quality practices as the operation continues to grow.

Responsibilities:
  • Lead investigations of customer complaints, warranty issues, and internal concfomromances using structured problem-solving methodologies such as 8D, 5 Why, Fishbone, and PFMEA, implementing effective corrective and preventative actions. 
  • Support and continuously improve the site's Quality Management System, ensuring compliance with ISO 9001 and applicable company quality standards.
  • Conduct internal process audits, support customer and certification audits, and drive timely resolution of findings.
  • Analyze quality, manufacturing, inspection, and warranty data to identify trends, reduce defects, minimize scrap and rework, and improve operational performance.
  • Develop and maintain quality planning and validation documentation, including PPAPs, Process Flow Diagrams, PFMEAs, Control Plans, Measurement System Analyses (MSA), and Process Capability Studies.
  • Support process validation and qualification activities, including IQ, OQ, and PQ protocols where applicable.
  • Collaborate with Engineering and Manufacturing teams to develop process controls, improve product quality, and ensure customer requirements are met.
  • Provide quality-related training and guidance, promote continuous improvement initiatives, and participate in Kaizen and operational excellence activities.

Requirements: 
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in manufacturing quality, quality engineering, or a related technical role within a manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of experience applying root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies to investigate and resolve manufacturing or product quality issues.
  • 2+ years of experience working within an ISO 9001 quality management system, including internal audits, corrective actions, or quality-system compliance activities.
  • 3+ years of experience analyzing manufacturing or quality data to identify trends, process issues, or improvement opportunities and communicating findings and recommended actions to manufacturing, engineering, or operations teams.

Core Competencies 
  • Continuous Improvement Mindset – Looks beyond immediate fixes to identify opportunities for sustainable process, product, and quality improvement. 
  • Analytical Problem Solving – Uses data, quality metrics, root cause analysis, and sound judgment to identify issues, evaluate trends, and develop effective solutions. 
  • Customer Focus – Evaluates quality through the customer’s perspective and takes action to improve product performance, reliability, and overall customer satisfaction.
  • Ownership & Follow-Through – Takes personal accountability for commitments, respects deadlines, drives actions to completion, and operates effectively without constant direction.
  • Collaboration & Influence – Builds productive relationships across Engineering, Operations, Production, Supply Chain, and other functions to resolve issues and advance quality initiatives.
  • Quality & Compliance Excellence – Maintains high standards for quality, process discipline, documentation, and compliance while supporting effective quality management systems.

Preferences: 
  • Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or similar quality certification.
  • Experience with PPAP, PFMEA, MSA, SPC, and Process Capability Studies.
  • Experience supporting ISO 9001 certified manufacturing environments.
  • Working knowledge of GD&T, blueprint reading, and metrology systems.
  • Experience in machining, assembly, pump manufacturing, or other industrial manufacturing environments.

Travel & Work Arrangements
  • This position is fully site-based at the Monroe, Louisiana manufacturing facility. 
  • Occasional travel may be required to support customer audits, supplier visits, training, or other business needs.

What We Offer 
Our benefits –At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.
