Job Title: Area Service Leader
Location: City of Industry, CA

About Us:
Ingersoll Rand thrives on a culture of innovation and a sense of ownership, committed to enhancing the lives of our employees, customers, and the planet. With over 80 renowned brands, our customers rely on our products and services to deliver high-quality flow creation and industrial solutions designed to perform in the most complex and harsh conditions. Additionally, our unwavering commitment to ownership has enabled our employees to cultivate strong customer relationships, driving them to solve the industry’s most difficult problems.

Job Overview:
The Area Service Leader position is responsible for providing the leadership for all service activities from the installation of new equipment to the implementation of a services contract through lifetime connectivity with that customer. Processes within that oversight include support of sales through contract pricing on parts and service, field service coordination, management of technicians and service supervisors, customer satisfaction, and responsibility for the revenue and margin of the parts and service business within the geography. Provides strategy for connectivity and services growth within the defined region. This position is responsible for service growth for office locations within the West Region (Southern California, Arizona & Nevada).

Responsibilities:

  • Accountable for full services portfolio performance.
  • Ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately balanced to service customers, and leverage resources across the area. This includes emergency repair (break/fix), regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components (parts), and long-term service agreements (Package Care).
  • Collaborate with the Operations Leader to ensure service coordination processes/functions are aligned with service objectives.
  • Collaborate with sales on contract pricing of parts and services to maintain and enhance profitable service operations.
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, and develop all service employees.
  • Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available.
  • Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process and technical skills, to the highest degree possible.
  • Proactively build the technician and service supervisor pipeline (internally and externally) and strategically manage your workforce to prevent resource gaps.
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team.
  • Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure a safe and productive work environment both in the shop and at customer sites.
  • Visit customers on a regular basis to build relationships and provide solutions.

Requirements:

  • 5+ years of experience in industrial product space, preferably with a diverse product portfolio including service offerings.
  • 3+ years’ management experience, preferably in a customer-facing environment.

Core Competencies:

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
  • Leadership skills are essential.
  • Must be able to manage an hourly technical workforce, including remote employees, as well as salaried staff.
  • Work is completed through other employees, so this person must excel at hiring, developing, training, coaching, leading and motivating a diverse workforce for optimal results.
  • Profit & Loss experience is critical
  • Must have experience in forecasting needs, obtaining resources, and managing budgets.
  • Collaborate and partner with the Regional Director in creation of a strategic business plan for growing the service business through internal process improvements and lean strategies to positively impact our market position.

Preferences:

  • Technical and/or mechanical capabilities are a plus.
  • Bachelor’s Degree in related discipline; Engineering, Technical, Marketing or Business preferred.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • This position will be based out of one of the West region area customer centers with regional and overnight, out of town travel required (45-70%).

The Pay Range:
The total pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $130,000 - $170,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicants will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.


What We Offer: At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment — as well as for our individual well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support needed to take charge of your health and future. Our benefits include healthcare coverage (medical, prescription, dental, and vision), wellness programs, life insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off, and an employee stock program, among other offerings. These benefits, combined with our pay transparency and inclusive culture, reflect our commitment to supporting you at work and beyond.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions.   • Ability to work effectively with manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, customer service, warranty, purchasing, and suppliers to resolve quality concerns, manage supplier corrective actions, and ensure customer quality requirements are met.

job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. Summary of Position

  This position will be responsible for verification of compliance of first article and in process components as through CMM measurement using standard work instructions.  This position will assist the Manufacturing Technicians to identify problems, troubleshoot and develop programs, update standard work and communicate as required. 


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Partners with Operators, Buyers, and Engineers to drive dimensional challenges to resolution
  • Uses 5S to improve cleanliness, reducing takt time and increasing consistent outcomes
  • Seek ways to define and resolve Red Dots such as earlier notification when program changes are needed
  • Utilizes and maintains SW and SPIs to collaborate and create consistency.
  • Perform 1st article & in-process inspections of manufacturing processes from the shop
  • Complete miscellaneous inspections as they arise
  • Maintain data documentation records based on retention requirements
  • Accurate and timely completions of DMT (defective material tags)
  • Maintain inspection files, database system and DMT tracking
  • Conduct all return material authorization (RMA) dispositions
  • Provides quality training as assigned
Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned

  Education Requirements / Certifications
  • High School Diploma or equivalent
 

Experience / Skill Requirements         
  • 2 years experience inspecting machined parts required
  • 2 years experience blueprint reading required
  • Experience using precision inspection tools/measuring equipment and familiarity with calibration requirements required
  • Proficient computer skills with Solidworks and Microsoft Office preferred
  • CMM experience preferred
 

Physical Requirements
  • Ability to lift 40 lbs repetitive
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time
  • Regular use of wrists, hands and/or fingers.
  • Close visual acuity to create/read schematics, drawings and/or a computer screen.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high
  • Work environment is on the manufacturing floor – temperatures vary substantially

job.title: Maintenance Technician I
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.







Summary of PositionLubricate machinery, change parts, or perform other routine machinery maintenance.  Actively involved in preventive maintenance program to achieve machine goals.



Essential Duties and Responsibilities
  • Install, troubleshoot, repair and maintain CNC machinery, electrical systems, pneumatic and hydraulic equipment
  • Reassemble machines after the completion of repair or maintenance work.
  • Start machines and observe mechanical operation to determine efficiency and to detect problems.
  • Inspect or test damaged machine parts, and mark defective areas or advise supervisors of repair needs.
  • Lubricate or apply adhesives or other materials to machines, machine parts, or other equipment, according to specified procedures.
  • Install, replace, or change machine parts and attachments, according to production specifications.
  • Dismantle machines and remove parts for repair, using hand tools, chain falls, jacks, cranes, or hoists.
  • Record production, repair, and machine maintenance information.
  • Read work orders and specifications to determine machines and equipment requiring repair or maintenance.
  • Set up and operate machines, and adjust controls to regulate operations.
  • Collaborate with other workers to repair or move machines, machine parts, or equipment.
  • Inventory and requisition machine parts, equipment, and other supplies so that stock can be maintained and replenished.
  • Transport machine parts, tools, equipment, and other material between work areas and storage, using cranes, hoists, or dollies.
  • Collect and discard worn machine parts and other refuse in order to maintain machinery and work areas.
  • Clean machines and machine parts, using cleaning solvents, cloths, air guns, hoses, vacuums, or other equipment.
  • Replace or repair metal, wood, leather, glass, or other lining in machines, or in equipment compartments or containers.
Education Requirements / Certifications 

  • Three (3) years' experience with CNC machine maintenance preferred
 

Experience / Skill Requirements         
  • Demonstrated experience in electrical and mechanical maintenance including motors, controls, power supplies, AC/DC theory, power distribution, PLC's, hydraulics/pneumatics, lubrication, power transmission and pumps
  • Demonstrated ability to follow all established safe work procedures including, but not limited to personal protection equipment, lockout/tag-out requirements and electrical safety
  • Read and interpret blueprints, technical parts manuals such as electrical and mechanical diagrams, and ability to effectively use and read gages, meters, calipers and other measuring tools
  • Effective and safe use of all required tools including, but not limited to, drills, saws, torches, welders, cranes & hoists, forklifts and other maintenance equipment
  • Ability to work other shifts, weekends and overtime as needed
 

Physical Requirements
  • Frequently required to sit, stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls and reach with hands and arms
  • Occasionally required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl
  • Occasionally required to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
  • Occasionally required to work near moving mechanical parts
  • Occasionally required to work in outside weather conditions and exposure to moderate cold and heat
  • Frequent exposure to various chemicals, lubricants, and grease
The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high

Job Title: Material Planner (Buyer)
Location: Mocksville, NC (Onsite)

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
Ingersoll Rand is looking to hire a Material Planner / Buyer at our Mocksville, NC plant, where we build a full line of rotary screw and centrifugal air compressors. This is a true manufacturing-floor-facing position where the best planners thrive by turning real-time demand signals into the right parts on the line. As a Material Planner you'll be responsible for purchased material planning process from placing purchase order, follow up with supplier to deliver product to production assembly lines and/or service parts. Plans engineering change and coordinates into production when appropriate. Provides other support to production and management as required. Responsible for purchased material planning process for nonstandard and drop shipments from placing purchase order, follow up with supplier to deliver product to production assembly lines and/or a drop shipment location.

Responsibilities:

  • Plan and manage purchased parts inventory by releasing, adjusting, canceling, or deferring orders based on demand, inventory levels, and production requirements.
  • Create and maintain purchase orders, partnering with suppliers to expedite or reschedule materials to meet production and inventory goals.
  • Manage service parts planning for purchased materials to support fluctuating customer demand.
  • Resolve purchase order, pricing, and invoicing issues with Accounts Payable and suppliers.
  • Maintain accurate purchasing and planning data within the ERP system, including order quantities, due dates, and order status updates.
  • Coordinate engineering changes (ECNs), ensuring effective implementation, inventory transition, and minimal cost or scrap impact.
  • Review BOM changes and maintain planning parameters, lead times, and order policies to support production requirements.
  • Represent Production Planning in cross-functional meetings and prepare planning, inventory, and management reports as needed.


Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 2+ years of experience with Material Planning and Purchasing, preferably in a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years working experience in Excel with ability to navigate formulas
  • 2+ years of ERP experience with systems such as Oracle R12, SAP, JDE


Core Competencies:

  • Material Planning & Inventory Control
  • Supplier & Purchase Order Management
  • ERP, Excel & Data Accuracy
  • Engineering Change & Production Coordination
  • Manufacturing Process & Blueprint Interpretation
  • Analytical, Mathematical & Communication Skills

Job Overview:
The Material Manager is responsible for leading all activities related to material planning, inventory control, warehousing, and inbound/outbound logistics to ensure uninterrupted production operations. This role oversees the flow of materials from suppliers to the production floor, optimizes inventory levels, and drives efficiency, accuracy, and cost control across the end to end materials function.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and optimize material planning strategies to align inventory levels, safety stock, and reorder points with production schedules and customer demand.
  • Monitor material availability, maintain inventory accuracy, conduct cycle counts, and resolve discrepancies to minimize shortages and excess inventory.
  • Partner with Procurement and suppliers to improve on-time delivery, lead times, material quality, cost efficiency, and supply continuity.
  • Oversee warehouse and logistics operations, including receiving, storage, material handling, production line delivery, freight optimization, and shipping accuracy.
  • Ensure compliance with warehouse safety standards, DOT requirements, 5S practices, and company policies while optimizing space utilization and material flow.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Production, Quality, Engineering, Finance, and Procurement to ensure material readiness, manage product changes, and resolve supply risks.
  • Lead daily tier meetings and drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Kaizen, Kanban, VMI, and other operational excellence methodologies.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the materials team while establishing performance goals and monitoring KPIs, including inventory accuracy, inventory turns, production material availability, supplier OTD, shortage rates, freight costs, and warehouse productivity.
 

 

Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field (preferred).
  • 5+ years of experience in materials management, planning, or supply chain in a manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of supervisory or leadership experience.

Competencies:

  • Strong understanding of MRP/ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, JD Edwards, etc.).
  • Expertise in inventory management principles and material flow optimization.
  • Solid knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Kanban, and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and cross functional leadership skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment.
 

  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements  

  • Fully site based in West Chester, PA

job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.

Title: Senior Buyer
Location: Mocksville, NC

Responsibilities:

  • Manage the timely and cost-effective procurement of production, inventory, and MRO materials.
  • Review material requirements and coordinate supplier deliveries to meet production schedules.
  • Select and onboard suppliers in accordance with approved sourcing and planning processes.
  • Maintain inventory targets, safety stock levels, and material planning parameters, including ABC classifications and PFEP data.
  • Support Material Planners in resolving supplier quality, delivery, and supply issues.
  • Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for material shortages and supply disruptions.
  • Identify cost savings, inventory optimization, and cash flow improvement opportunities with suppliers.
  • Manage Kanban, supplier replenishment programs, and inventory replenishment strategies.
  • Expedite critical material deliveries and maintain continuity of supply.
  • Partner with production planning to resolve material shortages and delivery constraints.
  • Monitor supplier performance and escalate issues when necessary.
  • Analyze material availability and capacity constraints to support planning decisions.
  • Maintain accurate lead times, item master data, and planning parameters within ERP systems.
  • Manage VMI/SOMI programs and coordinate with cross-functional teams to meet business objectives.
  • Communicate forecasts, replenishment plans, and performance expectations to suppliers.
  • Drive continuous improvement in supplier delivery, flexibility, and overall performance.

Core Competencies:

  • Knowledge of products, materials, specifications, and component substitutions.
  • Understanding of quality requirements, engineering changes, and certification processes.
  • Strong knowledge of supplier capabilities, manufacturing processes, and supply chain operations.
  • Experience with Kanban, JIT, and inventory replenishment methodologies.
  • Strong collaboration skills with internal teams and external suppliers.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and self-motivated with minimal supervision.
  • Strong problem-solving, multitasking, and prioritization skills.



Requirements:

  • High School diploma required.
  • 5+ years of Planner/Buyer experience in a manufacturing environment.

Preferences:

  • Experience supporting low-volume, high-mix manufacturing environments.
  • Strong supplier sourcing, network management, and supplier development experience.
  • Knowledge of production planning, material planning, and supplier scheduling.
  • Proficiency with Oracle R12 ERP and Microsoft Office.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience with inventory management, MRP, operations, and Lean manufacturing.
  • Ability to train, mentor, and support team members.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • Centrifugal compressor industry experience preferred.
  • Proven success driving continuous improvement and Lean initiatives.
  • Experience in rate-based, flow line, and job shop manufacturing environments.
  • Familiarity with visual management tools and operational excellence practices.

Job title: Material Manager

Location: West Chester, PA

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  


Job Overview:
The Material Manager is responsible for leading all activities related to material planning, inventory control, warehousing, and inbound/outbound logistics to ensure uninterrupted production operations. This role oversees the flow of materials from suppliers to the production floor, optimizes inventory levels, and drives efficiency, accuracy, and cost control across the end to end materials function.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and optimize material planning strategies to align inventory levels, safety stock, and reorder points with production schedules and customer demand.
  • Monitor material availability, maintain inventory accuracy, conduct cycle counts, and resolve discrepancies to minimize shortages and excess inventory.
  • Partner with Procurement and suppliers to improve on-time delivery, lead times, material quality, cost efficiency, and supply continuity.
  • Oversee warehouse and logistics operations, including receiving, storage, material handling, production line delivery, freight optimization, and shipping accuracy.
  • Ensure compliance with warehouse safety standards, DOT requirements, 5S practices, and company policies while optimizing space utilization and material flow.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Production, Quality, Engineering, Finance, and Procurement to ensure material readiness, manage product changes, and resolve supply risks.
  • Lead daily tier meetings and drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Kaizen, Kanban, VMI, and other operational excellence methodologies.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the materials team while establishing performance goals and monitoring KPIs, including inventory accuracy, inventory turns, production material availability, supplier OTD, shortage rates, freight costs, and warehouse productivity.
 

 

Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field (preferred).
  • 5+ years of experience in materials management, planning, or supply chain in a manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of supervisory or leadership experience.

Competencies:

  • Strong understanding of MRP/ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, JD Edwards, etc.).
  • Expertise in inventory management principles and material flow optimization.
  • Solid knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Kanban, and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and cross functional leadership skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment.
 

  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements  

  • Fully site based in West Chester, PA

About Us

Job Overview:
The Material Manager is responsible for leading all activities related to material planning, inventory control, warehousing, and inbound/outbound logistics to ensure uninterrupted production operations. This role oversees the flow of materials from suppliers to the production floor, optimizes inventory levels, and drives efficiency, accuracy, and cost control across the end to end materials function.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and optimize material planning strategies to align inventory levels, safety stock, and reorder points with production schedules and customer demand.
  • Monitor material availability, maintain inventory accuracy, conduct cycle counts, and resolve discrepancies to minimize shortages and excess inventory.
  • Partner with Procurement and suppliers to improve on-time delivery, lead times, material quality, cost efficiency, and supply continuity.
  • Oversee warehouse and logistics operations, including receiving, storage, material handling, production line delivery, freight optimization, and shipping accuracy.
  • Ensure compliance with warehouse safety standards, DOT requirements, 5S practices, and company policies while optimizing space utilization and material flow.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Production, Quality, Engineering, Finance, and Procurement to ensure material readiness, manage product changes, and resolve supply risks.
  • Lead daily tier meetings and drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Kaizen, Kanban, VMI, and other operational excellence methodologies.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the materials team while establishing performance goals and monitoring KPIs, including inventory accuracy, inventory turns, production material availability, supplier OTD, shortage rates, freight costs, and warehouse productivity.
 

 

Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field (preferred).
  • 5+ years of experience in materials management, planning, or supply chain in a manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of supervisory or leadership experience.

Competencies:

  • Strong understanding of MRP/ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, JD Edwards, etc.).
  • Expertise in inventory management principles and material flow optimization.
  • Solid knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Kanban, and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and cross functional leadership skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment.
 

  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements  

  • Fully site based in West Chester, PA

Job Overview:
The Distribution Aftermarket Leader is a strategic role responsible for driving growth in recurring revenue across all the IR Distribution channel within the compressed air and industrial services sector. This individual will work with the Distribution Sales Managers to execute service-focused strategies, and partner cross-functionally to optimize service offerings and performance. This role requires a dynamic professional with deep industry experience in the compressed air space including knowledge of centrifugal service, strong business acumen, and a passion for enabling teams and partners to deliver exceptional customer value through service engagement.

Responsibilities:

  • Work with peer distribution managers to improve aftermarket sales and drive forward distribution rotary and centrifugal parts growth.
  • Develop and execute strategic plans to increase service attachment rates and recurring revenue across all distribution channels.
  • Partner with senior distribution leadership to align sales structures and incentives with recurring revenue goals.
  • Coach and mentor Distribution Sales Managers to elevate their effectiveness in driving recurring revenue programs.
  • Oversee delivery of product and sales skills training focused on recurring revenue models and services for distributor sales teams.
  • Ensure ongoing development of distributor technicians and office personnel to support service growth initiatives.
  • Collaborate with product management to enhance recurring revenue offerings and drive distributor investment.

  • Support retail channel initiatives to increase parts sales and improve customer data capture for long-term service engagement.

Location: Buffalo, NY- Onsite

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview
Ingersoll Rand is seeking talented engineers across multiple disciplines in order to expand
its global Centrifugal Compressor Technology organization. We are seeking engineers
experienced with rotating equipment and turbomachinery design to join our team to
develop the next generation of Integrally Geared Centrifugal compressors.

Responsibilities
As part of the Centrifugal Technology team, you will be working with industry-leading
experts creating custom-engineered solutions for our client base that spans the globe.
Depending on your expertise, your primary work activities may include:
-Marketing and tendering support by developing compressor arrangements and
performance predictions that meet customer requirements and mechanical constraints.
-Aerodynamic design activities including compressor stage sizing, performance analysis,
impeller, inlet and diffuser design using 1D methods and CFD tools.
-Rotordynamic (lateral and torsional) analysis and design verification at both
preliminary (tendering) and design stages.
-Bearing, gearing and structural analyses using in-house codes and/or finite element and
simulation techniques to validate mechanical integrity and reliability.
-Optimization of rotor, bearing and drivetrain designs for centrifugal compressor
applications.
-Collaboration with project managers, mechanical engineers, manufacturing teams
through the entire project life cycle.
-Customer communication regarding analytical reports, test data reports and reviews
and root cause analysis.
-Definition of test requirements, support factory and field testing, analyze test data,
troubleshoot technical issues, and prepare technical reports.
-Support of root-cause investigations and implement corrective and preventive actions
based on experience.
-Development of new engineering methods, digital tools, and software applications that
improve ETO productivity and/or compressor performance.

Qualifications
-BS in Mechanical Engineering or Aerospace Engineering required; MS preferred.

-3+ years of industry or closely-related experience or equivalent masters level research
experience

Specific experience or coursework in Turbomachinery and 1-2 of the following areas:
-Thermal/Fluid Systems
-Rotating Equipment
-Vibration and Dynamics
-Materials and Tribology
-Numerical Methods
-CFD, Rotordynamics, FEA
-Bearing, Gearing, and Machine Design
-Programming experience and development of engineering analysis tools; familiarity
with AI-assisted engineering workflows is desirable.
-Knowledge of centrifugal compressor design, testing, performance evaluation and
troubleshooting.

Core Competencies
-Centrifugal compressor design including impellers, diffusers, and volutes
-Experience with related engineering software such as Ansys, STAR-CCM+, Numeca,
Cadence, Dyrobes, Teamcenter/NX or similar tools.
- Performance map and compressor stack up analysis
-1D Through flow inviscid and 3D CFD analysis
- Structural mechanics and analysis, FEA
- Component Lifting, Failure prevention analysis methods
- Materials Engineering including heat treatment and coatings
- Knowledge of advanced manufacturing methods
- Rotor design including bearings, gears, seals
- Rotordynamics (lateral and torsional) analysis
- Working knowledge of industry standards (API, ASME)
- Programming skills (Python, C++, VBA, JavaScript)
- Self – motivated and driven professional
- Collaborative and communicative (across functional and geographic boundaries)

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role is Min - 90000 - Max - 110000 . The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Travel & Work Requirements
Ability to Travel < 10%. The applicant shall be flexible to occasionally (<~5%) work during non-standard hours
in order to provide support to global Ingersoll Rand locations.

The applicant must have a strong command of the English language, and be capable of
clearly communicating in writing and speaking with peers, leadership, and internal /
external customers.

job.title: Quality Technician Weekends (Fri - Sun)
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.



Summary of Position

  This position will be responsible for verification of compliance of first article and in process components as through CMM measurement using standard work instructions.  This position will assist the Manufacturing Technicians to identify problems, troubleshoot and develop programs, update standard work and communicate as required. 


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Partners with Operators, Buyers, and Engineers to drive dimensional challenges to resolution
  • Uses 5S to improve cleanliness, reducing takt time and increasing consistent outcomes
  • Seek ways to define and resolve Red Dots such as earlier notification when program changes are needed
  • Utilizes and maintains SW and SPIs to collaborate and create consistency.
  • Perform 1st article & in-process inspections of manufacturing processes from the shop
  • Complete miscellaneous inspections as they arise
  • Maintain data documentation records based on retention requirements
  • Accurate and timely completions of DMT (defective material tags)
  • Maintain inspection files, database system and DMT tracking
  • Conduct all return material authorization (RMA) dispositions
  • Provides quality training as assigned
Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned

  Education Requirements / Certifications
  • High School Diploma or equivalent
 

Experience / Skill Requirements         
  • 2 years experience inspecting machined parts required
  • 2 years experience blueprint reading required
  • Experience using precision inspection tools/measuring equipment and familiarity with calibration requirements required
  • Proficient computer skills with Solidworks and Microsoft Office preferred
  • CMM experience preferred
 

Physical Requirements
  • Ability to lift 40 lbs repetitive
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time
  • Regular use of wrists, hands and/or fingers.
  • Close visual acuity to create/read schematics, drawings and/or a computer screen.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high
  • Work environment is on the manufacturing floor – temperatures vary substantially

job.title: Maintenance Technician I
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.







Summary of PositionLubricate machinery, change parts, or perform other routine machinery maintenance.  Actively involved in preventive maintenance program to achieve machine goals.



Essential Duties and Responsibilities
  • Install, troubleshoot, repair and maintain CNC machinery, electrical systems, pneumatic and hydraulic equipment
  • Reassemble machines after the completion of repair or maintenance work.
  • Start machines and observe mechanical operation to determine efficiency and to detect problems.
  • Inspect or test damaged machine parts, and mark defective areas or advise supervisors of repair needs.
  • Lubricate or apply adhesives or other materials to machines, machine parts, or other equipment, according to specified procedures.
  • Install, replace, or change machine parts and attachments, according to production specifications.
  • Dismantle machines and remove parts for repair, using hand tools, chain falls, jacks, cranes, or hoists.
  • Record production, repair, and machine maintenance information.
  • Read work orders and specifications to determine machines and equipment requiring repair or maintenance.
  • Set up and operate machines, and adjust controls to regulate operations.
  • Collaborate with other workers to repair or move machines, machine parts, or equipment.
  • Inventory and requisition machine parts, equipment, and other supplies so that stock can be maintained and replenished.
  • Transport machine parts, tools, equipment, and other material between work areas and storage, using cranes, hoists, or dollies.
  • Collect and discard worn machine parts and other refuse in order to maintain machinery and work areas.
  • Clean machines and machine parts, using cleaning solvents, cloths, air guns, hoses, vacuums, or other equipment.
  • Replace or repair metal, wood, leather, glass, or other lining in machines, or in equipment compartments or containers.
Education Requirements / Certifications 

  • Three (3) years' experience with CNC machine maintenance preferred
 

Experience / Skill Requirements         
  • Demonstrated experience in electrical and mechanical maintenance including motors, controls, power supplies, AC/DC theory, power distribution, PLC's, hydraulics/pneumatics, lubrication, power transmission and pumps
  • Demonstrated ability to follow all established safe work procedures including, but not limited to personal protection equipment, lockout/tag-out requirements and electrical safety
  • Read and interpret blueprints, technical parts manuals such as electrical and mechanical diagrams, and ability to effectively use and read gages, meters, calipers and other measuring tools
  • Effective and safe use of all required tools including, but not limited to, drills, saws, torches, welders, cranes & hoists, forklifts and other maintenance equipment
  • Ability to work other shifts, weekends and overtime as needed
 

Physical Requirements
  • Frequently required to sit, stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls and reach with hands and arms
  • Occasionally required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl
  • Occasionally required to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
  • Occasionally required to work near moving mechanical parts
  • Occasionally required to work in outside weather conditions and exposure to moderate cold and heat
  • Frequent exposure to various chemicals, lubricants, and grease
The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high

Job title: Material Manager

About Us

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview:
The Material Manager is responsible for leading all activities related to material planning, inventory control, warehousing, and inbound/outbound logistics to ensure uninterrupted production operations. This role oversees the flow of materials from suppliers to the production floor, optimizes inventory levels, and drives efficiency, accuracy, and cost control across the end to end materials function.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and optimize material planning strategies to align inventory levels, safety stock, and reorder points with production schedules and customer demand.
  • Monitor material availability, maintain inventory accuracy, conduct cycle counts, and resolve discrepancies to minimize shortages and excess inventory.
  • Partner with Procurement and suppliers to improve on-time delivery, lead times, material quality, cost efficiency, and supply continuity.
  • Oversee warehouse and logistics operations, including receiving, storage, material handling, production line delivery, freight optimization, and shipping accuracy.
  • Ensure compliance with warehouse safety standards, DOT requirements, 5S practices, and company policies while optimizing space utilization and material flow.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Production, Quality, Engineering, Finance, and Procurement to ensure material readiness, manage product changes, and resolve supply risks.
  • Lead daily tier meetings and drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Kaizen, Kanban, VMI, and other operational excellence methodologies.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the materials team while establishing performance goals and monitoring KPIs, including inventory accuracy, inventory turns, production material availability, supplier OTD, shortage rates, freight costs, and warehouse productivity.
 

 

Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field (preferred).
  • 5+ years of experience in materials management, planning, or supply chain in a manufacturing environment.
  • 3+ years of supervisory or leadership experience.

Competencies:

  • Strong understanding of MRP/ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, JD Edwards, etc.).
  • Expertise in inventory management principles and material flow optimization.
  • Solid knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Kanban, and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Effective communication and cross functional leadership skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment.
 

  Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements  

  • Fully site based in West Chester, PA

job.title: Quality Technician Weekends (Fri - Sun)
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.



Summary of Position

  This position will be responsible for verification of compliance of first article and in process components as through CMM measurement using standard work instructions.  This position will assist the Manufacturing Technicians to identify problems, troubleshoot and develop programs, update standard work and communicate as required. 


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Partners with Operators, Buyers, and Engineers to drive dimensional challenges to resolution
  • Uses 5S to improve cleanliness, reducing takt time and increasing consistent outcomes
  • Seek ways to define and resolve Red Dots such as earlier notification when program changes are needed
  • Utilizes and maintains SW and SPIs to collaborate and create consistency.
  • Perform 1st article & in-process inspections of manufacturing processes from the shop
  • Complete miscellaneous inspections as they arise
  • Maintain data documentation records based on retention requirements
  • Accurate and timely completions of DMT (defective material tags)
  • Maintain inspection files, database system and DMT tracking
  • Conduct all return material authorization (RMA) dispositions
  • Provides quality training as assigned
Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned

  Education Requirements / Certifications
  • High School Diploma or equivalent
 

Experience / Skill Requirements         
  • 2 years experience inspecting machined parts required
  • 2 years experience blueprint reading required
  • Experience using precision inspection tools/measuring equipment and familiarity with calibration requirements required
  • Proficient computer skills with Solidworks and Microsoft Office preferred
  • CMM experience preferred
 

Physical Requirements
  • Ability to lift 40 lbs repetitive
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time
  • Regular use of wrists, hands and/or fingers.
  • Close visual acuity to create/read schematics, drawings and/or a computer screen.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high
  • Work environment is on the manufacturing floor – temperatures vary substantially

The ideal candidate is customer-focused, detail-oriented, and eager to develop their skills. Through training, coaching, and hands-on experience, the Associate will build proficiency and gain independence in managing daily responsibilities.

• Assist with customer quotations, order entry, and delivery coordination under the guidance of experienced team members.

• Organization and Time Management: Ability to manage daily tasks, track customer requests, and follow established processes.
• Computer Proficiency: Ability to use Microsoft Office and learn SAP and other business systems.
• Problem Solving: Ability to identify questions or issues, seek guidance, and support resolution.
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work with team members and other departments to support customer and business needs.
• Learning and Development: Willingness to learn new products, processes, and systems through training and hands-on experience.

Preferences

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, or a technical-related field.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to stand, walk, or sit for extended periods.
• Ability to communicate information effectively through verbal and written communication, including conveying detailed instructions.
• Ability to operate a computer.
• Work is performed in an office environment.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

• This position is based in Springfield, Missouri.
• Travel is expected only in rare circumstances.

The pay range for this role is $45,000–$60,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

This role leads commercial activities for customers in healthcare, life sciences, and pharmaceutical manufacturing, building relationships and identifying opportunities to grow sales.

Candidates with PPE knowledge will have the opportunity to develop their respiratory product expertise through training and hands-on experience.

Job Overview

Ingersoll Rand is seeking a skilled and motivated Repair Technician to join our Houston Service Center team. This position is responsible for performing complete repairs and rebuilds on customer equipment, including Roots and non-Roots blowers, pumps, compressors, and other rotating equipment.


Responsibilities

The primary responsibility of the Repair Technician is to perform complete repairs on customer equipment for Roots and non-Roots equipment in the Service Center. The Repair Technician will be responsible for working within the overall Service Center team to accomplish the goals of the business in the areas of EHS, Quality, On-Time Delivery, Operating Costs, and Productivity improvements. Additional responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Performs necessary disassembly, diagnosis, inspection, and reassembly to a wide variety of blowers, pumps, and compressors (Roots and non-Roots units). Inspection may include visual and/or instrument examination. Evaluates the condition of existing parts/components, for possible reuse or replacement.
  • Willingness to work with other employees in a team environment.
  • Performs any tests such as slip or leak tests, including MT and PT examinations (magnetic particle and penetrant testing).
  • As required, operates any/all Roots equipment necessary to accomplish the repair and rebuild of all customer units.
  • Completes written records, such as check sheets, clearances, pressure tests, inspection reports, etc., required by job order.
  • Operates various torches to perform heating or cutting in the disassembly and repair of units.
  • As required, secures units and/or parts, and prepares for shipment. Duties include some painting and foam packing.
  • Operates fork truck, overhead crane, company car or pickup truck, for the purpose of loading, unloading, or transporting parts/units to, from, and within the Service Center.
  • Maintains a clean and orderly work area, including such duties as sweeping, emptying trash containers, spillage cleanup, and disposing of scrap parts in the shop, and stacking and organizing parts/units in storage/staging areas within the Service Center.
  • Observes plant rules and safe working practices.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience repairing large industrial equipment.
  • Ability to lift 25 pounds during normal work activities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience repairing or rebuilding rotating equipment, including pumps, compressors, and blowers.
  • Experience with mechanical disassembly, inspection, troubleshooting, and reassembly.
  • TIG or arc welding qualifications.
  • Experience operating machine tools such as mills, lathes, or drill presses.
  • Strong understanding of workplace safety and quality procedures.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams to improve processes and efficiency.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Good interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively in a team environment.

Summary of Position

  This position will be responsible for verification of compliance of first article and in process components as through CMM measurement using standard work instructions.  This position will assist the Manufacturing Technicians to identify problems, troubleshoot and develop programs, update standard work and communicate as required. 


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Partners with Operators, Buyers, and Engineers to drive dimensional challenges to resolution
  • Uses 5S to improve cleanliness, reducing takt time and increasing consistent outcomes
  • Seek ways to define and resolve Red Dots such as earlier notification when program changes are needed
  • Utilizes and maintains SW and SPIs to collaborate and create consistency.
  • Perform 1st article & in-process inspections of manufacturing processes from the shop
  • Complete miscellaneous inspections as they arise
  • Maintain data documentation records based on retention requirements
  • Accurate and timely completions of DMT (defective material tags)
  • Maintain inspection files, database system and DMT tracking
  • Conduct all return material authorization (RMA) dispositions
  • Provides quality training as assigned
Demonstrates excellence in completion of all other duties as assigned

  Education Requirements / Certifications
  • High School Diploma or equivalent
 

Experience / Skill Requirements         
  • 2 years experience inspecting machined parts required
  • 2 years experience blueprint reading required
  • Experience using precision inspection tools/measuring equipment and familiarity with calibration requirements required
  • Proficient computer skills with Solidworks and Microsoft Office preferred
  • CMM experience preferred
 

Physical Requirements
  • Ability to lift 40 lbs repetitive
  • Ability to stand for long periods of time
  • Regular use of wrists, hands and/or fingers.
  • Close visual acuity to create/read schematics, drawings and/or a computer screen.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to high
  • Work environment is on the manufacturing floor – temperatures vary substantially

Job Title: Account Manager
Location: Remote - Territory - Winchester, VA to Roanoke, VA on I-81

About Us:
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
Ingersoll Rand’s Compression Systems and Services Customer Center is hiring a General Line Account Manager to join their team. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the Customer Center equipment sales and service activity for a specific territory. Traveling in a defined geographic area, this includes quoting, strategizing, prospecting, and developing relationships to achieve revenue targets, maximize profits, increase market share and maintain customer loyalty while achieving organizational goals. The position is a unique blend of supporting a major distributor and selling direct to customers.

Responsibilities:

  • Generate Revenue - Responsible for generating sales of equipment, service contracts, and service offerings with our direct end users and partners selling to a defined customer base within a geographic area. Develop existing customer base and secure new, competitive accounts to expand IR presence in the market. Provide and design compressed air solutions to fulfil industrial customer needs. Products include compressed air equipment, accessories, turnkey installations, service contracts, parts, service, rental equipment and energy audits. Keep current with all product knowledge, industry standards and training needed. Execute strategy for continuous improvement and exceeding customer satisfaction. Achieve all assigned sales targets.
  • Develop People Capabilities - Provide selling skills and product/services training for dealer sales personnel (as required) as well as personnel within the Customer Center. Partner with services team to best understand products and services and satisfy and anticipate customer’s needs.
  • Manage Cash - Ensure that all orders obtained are error-free with correct customer documentation. Ensure resolution of all customer disputes. Manage all costs associated with selling efforts, including travel and entertainment expenditures.
  • Ensure adherence to safety rules (vehicle safety, customer site safety) in the field, as well as in the Customer Center.
  • Earn customer loyalty by collaborating cross functionally. Leverage best support for customers by partnering with service team to help troubleshoot customer issues or offer unique solutions.
  • Maintain Customer Relationship Management database including face-to-face customer interactions, assets, agreements, contacts, and opportunities in order management system. Record order follow-up activities (e.g. delivery), reporting requirements (email) and database requirements. Provide feedback on market conditions. Responsible for driving and tracking sales pipeline of all account activity and daily reporting.


Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • 2+ years of an industrial sales business setting or successful completion of the Ingersoll Rand Sales Development Program (SDP).


Core Competencies:

  • Excellent relationship-building and interpersonal skills, including verbal, written and presentation communication skills.
  • Establishes and builds solid relationships with customers, key institutions and team members
  • Honest, self-motivated and team oriented.
  • Able to work within a team environment and independently.
  • Mechanical and electrical expertise required.
  • Ability to assess customer needs, analyze and interpret, perform basic equipment performance calculations, and to recommend technical solutions
  • Tech savvy; knowledge of Salesforce or other CRM software is preferred
  • Proven business and sales acumen, including the ability to prospect accounts, effectively navigate within a customer organization, value sell, and win competitive accounts
  • Must have excellent prioritization and time management skills


Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, engineering technology, business or equivalent
  • Knowledge of Salesforce


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

This position will be remote, and may travel within the territory about 50% of the time. A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided. Must possess a valid driver’s license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations included, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, Multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.

Pay Range:
The pay range for this role, not including incentive opportunities, is $60,000 - $75,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicant will be eligible to receive (discretionary/nondiscretionary) annual bonuses and incentive compensation.

Job Title: Cost Accountant, Manufacturing
Location: Buffalo, NY (Hybrid)

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview: 
Build on Your Accounting Strengths. Expand Your Impact in Cost Accounting. Join our growing manufacturing operation in the greater Buffalo, NY area as our Cost Accountant where you’ll apply your accounting expertise and strengthen your cost accounting skills while helping drive decisions in a complex manufacturing environment. Our facility manufactures a diverse range of large-scale Multi Stage Geared (MSG) air compressors and aftermarket remanufactured products that support customers across a variety of industries. As a key member of the finance team, you’ll contribute to the facility’s financial operations—supporting accurate cost accounting processes, informing business decisions, and driving continuous improvement.

This onsite opportunity is ideal for a proactive accounting professional with costing knowledge, exposure, or hands-on experience who enjoys tackling complex tasks and collaborating with peers and leadership. You’ll bring a positive attitude, strong attention to detail, exceptional organizational skills, and sound judgment to manage competing priorities effectively. If you’re energized by understanding what drives manufacturing costs and turning that insight into better business outcomes, this is an opportunity to grow your expertise and make a meaningful contribution.

Responsibilities:
  • Drive reliable and meaning Standard Costing within the plant including:
    • Daily costing updates for manufactured and purchased parts
    • Execute the annual cost roll for material, labor and overhead
    • Supporting new product development cost estimates and analysis
    • Activities and analysis to improve overall accuracy of product cost
    • Analyze and report variances such as PPV, Labor, and Freight.
  • Partner with on-going cost reviews (monthly/quarterly models, manufacturing variances and all other cost analysis)
  • Support month-end, quarter-end and year-end closing activities
  • Complete/Review monthly account reconciliations and financial performance analysis
  • Execute and Improve close processes and the environment of control
  • Monitor processes and controls relating to financial transactions, recommending and implementing improvements with the Controller and business partners.
  • Support Sarbanes-Oxley compliance and work directly with internal/external audit teams
  • Support Operations teams in project and productivity execution
  • Work closely with non-finance team members to drive cost improvements and analysis in all production activities (leveraging Lean manufacturing concepts in the pursuit of continuous improvements)
  • GRNI Process: Work with team to process GRNI, to keep within an acceptable level and in alignment with company policy.
  • Analyze/Report/Close Capital Projects
  • Partner in Annual Budget, Quarterly Forecasting, and Monthly Financial Projections.
  • Provide Meaningful Business Analysis
  • Support and execute ad hoc projects as assigned by the Plant Controller

Requirements:
  • Bachelor degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • 3+ years of progressive accounting experience, ideally in a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications proficiently.
  • 1+ years of experience using an ERP system or for accounting or financial processes.
  • 1+ years of cost accounting exposure, knowledge or expertise. 

Core Competencies
  • Manufacturing Cost Accounting and Standard Costing: Demonstrated ability to maintain reliable standard costs for manufactured and purchased components, execute annual cost rolls, develop new-product cost estimates, and improve product-cost accuracy.
  • Cost and Manufacturing Variance Analysis: Ability to analyze and report purchase price variance (PPV), labor variance, freight variance, manufacturing variance, and other production-related cost drivers, translating findings into meaningful business analysis.
  • Financial Close, Reconciliation, and Internal Controls: Experience supporting month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities; completing account reconciliations; reviewing financial performance; and improving accounting processes and the control environment.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership and Communication: Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, and build productive working relationships with internal and external customers. Ability to collaborate across Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, auditors, and other business partners to support cost analysis, financial reporting, productivity initiatives, and operational decision-making.
  • Budgeting, Forecasting, and Continuous Improvement: Experience supporting annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, monthly financial projections, capital-project analysis, and continuous improvement initiatives within a complex manufacturing operation.

Preferences:
  • Advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.
  • Experience analyzing and interpreting large data sets.
  • Experience using SAP in a manufacturing or cost-accounting environment.
  • Professional certification such as:
    • Certified Management Accountant (CMA)
    • Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
    • Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing methodology and its application to cost reduction and continuous improvement.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • Position is based in our Buffalo site.
  • Hybrid schedule available

The pay range for this role is $65,000 - $85,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title: Service Supervisor, Commercial Compressed Air
Location: Livonia, MI

About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview: 
The Service Supervisor in the compressed air commercial segment is responsible for leading the local service function for the full life cycle of the equipment to achieve exceptional customer satisfaction. This encompasses supporting the sales team to grow the business, collaborating with service coordination, and managing a Service Technician team that installs, repairs and maintains all makes of rotary screw and reciprocating air compressors and compressed air system components. The Service Supervisor also has responsibility for the Service P&L for their Customer Center.

Responsibilities:
  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
 
Requirements: 
  • High School Diploma or GED 
  • 7+ years of relevant services experience (primarily with industrial equipment).
  • 3+ years’ experience in managing teams of people with relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
  • 3+ years of progressive customer service leadership experience, including conflict resolution, effective communication, and negotiation

Location: Buffalo, NY (Hybrid)

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. Job Overview: 
Build on Your Accounting Strengths. Expand Your Impact in Cost Accounting. Join our growing manufacturing operation in the greater Buffalo, NY area as our Cost Accountant where you’ll apply your accounting expertise and strengthen your cost accounting skills while helping drive decisions in a complex manufacturing environment. Our facility manufactures a diverse range of large-scale Multi Stage Geared (MSG) air compressors and aftermarket remanufactured products that support customers across a variety of industries. As a key member of the finance team, you’ll contribute to the facility’s financial operations—supporting accurate cost accounting processes, informing business decisions, and driving continuous improvement.

This onsite opportunity is ideal for a proactive accounting professional with costing knowledge, exposure, or hands-on experience who enjoys tackling complex tasks and collaborating with peers and leadership. You’ll bring a positive attitude, strong attention to detail, exceptional organizational skills, and sound judgment to manage competing priorities effectively. If you’re energized by understanding what drives manufacturing costs and turning that insight into better business outcomes, this is an opportunity to grow your expertise and make a meaningful contribution.

Responsibilities:
  • Drive reliable and meaning Standard Costing within the plant including:
    • Daily costing updates for manufactured and purchased parts
    • Execute the annual cost roll for material, labor and overhead
    • Supporting new product development cost estimates and analysis
    • Activities and analysis to improve overall accuracy of product cost
    • Analyze and report variances such as PPV, Labor, and Freight.
  • Partner with on-going cost reviews (monthly/quarterly models, manufacturing variances and all other cost analysis)
  • Support month-end, quarter-end and year-end closing activities
  • Complete/Review monthly account reconciliations and financial performance analysis
  • Execute and Improve close processes and the environment of control
  • Monitor processes and controls relating to financial transactions, recommending and implementing improvements with the Controller and business partners.
  • Support Sarbanes-Oxley compliance and work directly with internal/external audit teams
  • Support Operations teams in project and productivity execution
  • Work closely with non-finance team members to drive cost improvements and analysis in all production activities (leveraging Lean manufacturing concepts in the pursuit of continuous improvements)
  • GRNI Process: Work with team to process GRNI, to keep within an acceptable level and in alignment with company policy.
  • Analyze/Report/Close Capital Projects
  • Partner in Annual Budget, Quarterly Forecasting, and Monthly Financial Projections.
  • Provide Meaningful Business Analysis
  • Support and execute ad hoc projects as assigned by the Plant Controller

Requirements:
  • Bachelor degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • 3+ years of progressive accounting experience, ideally in a manufacturing environment.
  • 2+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications proficiently.
  • 1+ years of experience using an ERP system or for accounting or financial processes.
  • 1+ years of cost accounting exposure, knowledge or expertise. 

Core Competencies
  • Manufacturing Cost Accounting and Standard Costing: Demonstrated ability to maintain reliable standard costs for manufactured and purchased components, execute annual cost rolls, develop new-product cost estimates, and improve product-cost accuracy.
  • Cost and Manufacturing Variance Analysis: Ability to analyze and report purchase price variance (PPV), labor variance, freight variance, manufacturing variance, and other production-related cost drivers, translating findings into meaningful business analysis.
  • Financial Close, Reconciliation, and Internal Controls: Experience supporting month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities; completing account reconciliations; reviewing financial performance; and improving accounting processes and the control environment.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership and Communication: Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, and build productive working relationships with internal and external customers. Ability to collaborate across Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, auditors, and other business partners to support cost analysis, financial reporting, productivity initiatives, and operational decision-making.
  • Budgeting, Forecasting, and Continuous Improvement: Experience supporting annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, monthly financial projections, capital-project analysis, and continuous improvement initiatives within a complex manufacturing operation.

Preferences:
  • Advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.
  • Experience analyzing and interpreting large data sets.
  • Experience using SAP in a manufacturing or cost-accounting environment.
  • Professional certification such as:
    • Certified Management Accountant (CMA)
    • Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
    • Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing methodology and its application to cost reduction and continuous improvement.

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • Position is based in our Buffalo site.
  • Hybrid schedule available

The pay range for this role is $65,000 - $85,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview:
If you’re ready to make a measurable impact, take ownership as a Collections Analyst managing a diversified accounts receivable portfolio for Ingersoll Rand within our Shared Services team. In this role, you’ll drive results by resolving disputes, strengthening customer relationships, and ensuring healthy cash flow across domestic and international accounts. We’re seeking an early-career Accounts Receiveable / Finance professional with proven collections experience ideally managing 200+ accounts and a $3–5M portfolio, who is eager to drive change in a dynamic environment.The ideal candidate is inquisitive, self-motivated, and proactive in identifying opportunities for improvement. Leveraging advanced collection tools and strong analytical skills, you’ll uncover challenges, implement solutions, and collaborate closely with customers and sales teams to deliver performance.

If you thrive on problem-solving, accountability, and seeing the direct impact of your work, this is your opportunity to step forward and lead.

Responsibilities:

  • Use available collection software tools (Getpaid) to assist in executing effective strategies and initiatives to achieve continuous receivable delinquency improvement that contributes to a lower Days Sales Outstanding (DSO).
  • Manage domestic and/or international accounts receivable accounts by analyzing, identifying, and reporting problem accounts.
  • Monitor past due customer accounts, contact customers, and resolve issues that may delay timely payment.
  • Identify issues for escalation and request credit holds.
  • Develop and maintain business relationships with customers and sales office personnel.
  • Customer account reconciliation and identifying and tagging disputed items within assigned portfolio.
  • Tracking and ensuring timely clearing of these disputed items is required.
  • Conduct monthly meetings with Field Sales leadership to drive dispute resolution if required.
  • Ensures timely and accurate responses to: customer inquiries, documentation issues, billing errors, payment application errors, disputes, program changes, and new sale requests/opportunities.

  • Associates Degree in Accounting / Finance
  • 1+ years of experience working in accounts receivable / collections
  • 1+ years ERP accounting software experience
  • 1+ years of experience working within Microsoft Office Suite products
  • 1+ years of demonstrated experience collaborating with internal and external customers


Core Competencies:

job.description:
