Job Title: Electrical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization
Location: Sidney, OH

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview:
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in this true ground-floor opportunity. The Electrical Design Engineer, Power Generation Containerization will help design, integrate, and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the electrical architecture, system integration, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.

The Electrical Design Engineer will own key aspects of the electrical design and integration of large generator systems, including generator enclosures, power connections, controls access, electrical equipment layout, and overall packaged-system integration. These are not small commercial generators, but large-scale diesel generator systems designed to provide critical backup power for data center environments where reliability, uptime, and continuity are essential. As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from design and integration through validation, manufacturing readiness, and commercialization. The role will partner closely with the Mechanical Engineer, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, suppliers, project management, and the Sidney plant to ensure the complete packaged solution meets both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings electrical design experience in power generation, large generator systems, data center electrical infrastructure, mission-critical backup power, industrial equipment, or modular/containerized power systems. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, 2MW+ systems, diesel generator sets, and environments where code compliance, serviceability, and reliability are critical is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.

Responsibilities:

Electrical System Design

  • Design electrical systems for containerized and modular power generation packages supporting data center applications.
  • Develop electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, wiring drawings, cable schedules, panel layouts, and system architecture documentation.
  • Design and integrate:
  • Diesel and natural gas generator systems
  • Generator paralleling systems
  • Switchgear and switchboards
  • Medium- and low-voltage distribution equipment
  • Automatic transfer switches (ATS)
  • UPS interfaces
  • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
  • Auxiliary systems including HVAC, lighting, monitoring, and fire protection
  • Perform electrical calculations including:
  • Load flow analysis
  • Equipment sizing
  • Short-circuit studies
  • Voltage drop calculations
  • Protective device coordination

Data Center Power Solutions

  • Develop solutions that support mission-critical data center reliability requirements including N, N+1, and 2N architectures.
  • Support integration with customer electrical infrastructure and utility interconnection requirements.
  • Design systems to meet data center expectations for uptime, maintainability, scalability, and serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal stakeholders to evaluate custom power generation and backup power solutions.
  • Support electrical integration for modular and prefabricated power systems used in hyperscale and colocation data centers.

Product Development & Standardization

  • Drive development of standardized containerized power generation platforms for data center markets.
  • Create and maintain engineering specifications, design standards, and best practices.
  • Conduct design reviews and support FMEA, reliability analysis, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including hybrid power systems, energy storage, microgrids, and renewable energy integrations.

Testing, Validation & Commissioning

  • Support prototype development, testing, and validation activities.
  • Develop and review Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) protocols.
  • Participate in commissioning and startup activities for customer projects.
  • Troubleshoot electrical integration issues during manufacturing, deployment, and field operation.

Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work directly with data center customers, consultants, contractors, and equipment suppliers.
  • Provide technical leadership during project execution and customer design reviews.
  • Support sales and business development teams with technical proposals and engineering evaluations.
  • Coordinate with manufacturing and sourcing teams to ensure successful product implementation.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive electrical design experience ideally in power generation, critical facilities, industrial systems, modular infrastructure, or related industries.
  • 3+ years experience interpreting electrical specifications and customer technical requirements.
  • 2+ years experience designing power distribution systems and power generation equipment.
  • 2+ years of proficienct experience in AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, SolidWorks Electrical, or similar design platforms.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
  • Generator systems
  • Electrical protection and coordination
  • Low-voltage and medium-voltage power distribution
  • Electrical codes and standards

Core Competencies:

  • Emergency and standby power systems
  • Generator controls and synchronization
  • Utility interconnection
  • Switchgear and switchboards
  • Protective relaying and system coordination
  • Medium-voltage distribution systems
  • Containerized power solutions
  • Energy storage integration
  • Mission-critical infrastructure
  • Data center electrical architecture


Preferences:

  • 5+ years of experience supporting data center, mission-critical, or power generation industries.
  • Experience with:
  • Data center electrical infrastructure
  • Generator paralleling systems
  • Medium-voltage switchgear
  • Microgrid applications
  • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
  • Knowledge of data center design practices and redundancy architectures.
  • Familiarity with PLC controls, SCADA systems, and power monitoring systems.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers such as Microsoft, AWS, Google, Meta, or other colocation providers.

Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
  • Relocation assistance available
  • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm


Pay Range - The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Job Overview

Process Flow Technologies is hiring for a Electrical Controls Engineer for our Lone Star Turbo business based in Houston, TX. This role designs, develops, tests, and supports PLC-based industrial control systems, including HMI and SCADA applications, for blowers, compressors, and associated equipment.

The Electrical Controls Engineer manages assigned controls software projects from requirements definition and design through programming, testing, and customer-site startup. This position works directly with customers and engineering teams to deliver safe, reliable, and maintainable solutions while independently managing assigned work with minimal oversight.

Responsibilities

  • Translate customer and project requirements into control software solutions, control narratives, and system design documentation.
  • Develop and maintain PLC programs, HMI/SCADA applications, and equipment control strategies.
  • Manage assigned controls software projects from requirements and design through implementation, testing, and optimization.
  • Develop and execute software validation and acceptance testing, including customer-facing Factory Acceptance Testing and Site Acceptance Testing.
  • Support customer-site startup, commissioning, equipment tuning, and troubleshooting.
  • Maintain software revisions, reusable code, change records, and technical documentation.
  • Collaborate with customers and cross-functional teams, communicate progress and risks, and improve control software reliability and maintainability.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field.
  • 2+ years of experience in industrial automation, controls engineering, or control system software development.
  • 2+ years of Hands-on experience with one or more PLC platforms, including Rockwell Automation, Siemens, Phoenix Contact, or Schneider Electric.

Core Competencies

  • Proficiency in Structured Text programming, Ladder Logic and Function Block Diagram programming.
  • Knowledge of control system fundamentals, PLC hardware, industrial instrumentation, analog and digital I/O, actuators, and VFD/motor control.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, P&IDs, control panel drawings, and network architecture documentation.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Ability to gather requirements, develop technical solutions, and work directly with customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to independently manage assigned projects, prioritize work, and meet deadlines.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred experience

  • HMI and SCADA development experience.
  • Customer-facing Factory Acceptance Testing and Site Acceptance Testing.
  • Industrial equipment startup, commissioning, and tuning.
  • Modular programming, reusable code, user-defined data types, and software change management.
  • Electrical control panel design fundamentals.

Full-time, on-site position at 8883 West Monroe Rd, Houston, Texas 77061. May need to work outside of normal business hours as needed.

Willingness and ability to travel to customer sites for startup, commissioning, and technical support.

Job Overview:

The Shipping & Receiving Associate performs a variety of shipping, receiving, inventory control, and material handling functions in support of manufacturing operations. Assignments may include parts picking and packing, inbound receiving, inventory transactions, fork truck operation, painting for shipment, and custom crating for LTL freight, based on operational needs.

This role requires strong attention to detail, accuracy, accountability, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision while supporting inventory accuracy, production flow, and on-time shipment of products.

Responsibilities:

(Assigned based on operational need; employees may be reassigned between functions)

Receiving – Incoming Receiving Clerk

  • Receive incoming materials against purchase orders and packing lists
  • Verify part numbers, quantities, and condition of received materials
  • Perform ERP receiving transactions and assign inventory locations accurately
  • Ensure received materials are delivered to the correct location or personnel
  • Work with Purchasing and other departments to resolve receiving discrepancies
  • Support receipt of outside process parts and finished goods

Receiving – Fork Truck Driver / Inventory Control

  • Operate fork trucks or manually move materials to assigned storage locations
  • Put away materials accurately and efficiently
  • Perform inventory moves, transfers, and adjustments in SAP
  • Maintain accurate inventory location control
  • Support cycle counts and inventory accuracy initiatives

Shipping – Parts Picker / Packer

  • Pick and pack parts accurately for customer and internal shipments
  • Verify part numbers, quantities, and shipment contents prior to packaging
  • Process shipments using UPS, FedEx, and other small-parcel systems
  • Identify and resolve part number, quantity, or documentation discrepancies
  • Ensure shipments are properly packaged, labeled, and staged

Shipping – LTL Crater / Packer

  • Pick large pumps or assemblies from stock for freight shipment
  • Measure products and build custom wooden crates as required
  • Use hand tools, measuring devices, pallet jacks, and fork trucks as needed
  • Secure products properly to prevent damage during transportation
  • Coordinate with shipping personnel to meet LTL and freight schedules

Shipping – Painter

  • Prepare, mask, and paint parts or assemblies for shipment
  • Confirm completion of paint operations in job travelers or systems
  • Ensure painted parts meet appearance and protection requirements
  • Stage painted parts to shipping or back to production as required
  • Maintain cleanliness and safety in paint and prep areas

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 1+ years of experience in a manufacturing setting

Core Competencies (All Assignments):

  • Follow standard work instructions, warehouse procedures, and safety requirements
  • Maintain accurate control of part numbers, quantities, and inventory locations
  • Perform SAP transactions accurately and in a timely manner
  • Identify, investigate, and escalate inventory, quantity, or documentation discrepancies
  • Support production and shipping schedules by ensuring materials and shipments are processed correctly
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment
  • Communicate effectively with production, purchasing, shipping, and supervision
  • Actively uphold safety standards and report unsafe conditions or practices
  • Perform other related duties as assigned based on operational needs

Preferences:

(Depending on Assignment) Experience in shipping, receiving, warehouse operations, and inventory control, including use of UPS, FedEx, or similar shipment processing systems.

  • Proficiency with ERP systems and basic computer applications; ability to learn SAP, shipping, and inventory platforms (SAP experience is a plus).
  • Background in manufacturing or industrial environments, with hands-on experience using fork trucks, hand tools, and building custom packaging or crates.
  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and organizational/timemanagement skills.

Job Overview:

Responsibilities:

  • Read print drawings to determine dimensions, design, and materials for construction.

  • Operates pneumatic and manual presses to assist in assembly operation, which includes setting up the presses
  • Set-up and operate identification equipment (stampers, labelers, etc.)
  • Test product for compliance to meet specifications using manual and automatic test equipment
  • Paint, label and pack completed product for shipment

  • Report changes in work orders, bill of materials, and pick lists to team lead.
  • Contribute to department/cell communication boards
  • Check off and sign work order cover sheets
  • Complete daily hour by hour production sheet
  • Maintain work area in accordance with 5S standards
  • Identify and report all safety issues to team lead
  • Participate and/or lead continuous improvement events and training
  • Suggest ideas for overall improvements to the area processes
  • Cross-train across multiple product lines
  • All other duties as assigned by the supervisor/team leader.

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 1+ years of experience in a manufacturing setting

  • Knowledge of and willingness to comply with all general work rules, policies and procedures, including safety guidelines and procedures.

  • Ability to learn to operate all equipment associated with the job; including, but not limited to, power hand tools, forklifts, skyjacks, cranes, and measuring devices.
  • Ability to identify routine problem causation, and correct routine problems, and willingness to learn.

Preferences:

  • 2+ years of experience in a manufacturing setting preferred.
  • Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions in English, short correspondence, and memos, such as supervisory instructions, safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, procedure manuals, and work orders
  • Ability to effectively share information about job duties in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees
  • Familiar with and ability to utilize all hand tools including wrenches, sockets, hammers, tape measures, crimpers, cutters, and steel banding.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude to use equipment and maintain general understanding of business process.
  • Familiar with and can utilize power tools.
  • Forklift certification is required to operate forklift equipment, but is not a required job responsibility for assembly

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position will be based on-site

SAFETY REQUIREMENTS While performing the duties of this job, the employee must wear OSHA approved safety glasses, hearing protection and steel toe safety shoes. Gloves are required to be worn when handling or moving parts. OSHA approved hearing protection (ANSI approved ear plugs) is required when on the shop floor. Painters must wear a respirator.

  • The following is a summary of the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) that was performed for this job:
  • Hazard communication, fire safety, Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE), & detailed JSA training will be reviewed before any job assignment. The JSA describes identified hazards and what protection the employee must take to protect employees from injury.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; use hands to finger; handle, or feel; walk; reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear
  • The employee must regularly lift and/or move boxes that weigh up to 50 pounds. The employee may be required to lift and/or move bar stock/baskets that vary in weight above these amounts. The employee must get assistance from other co-workers or by using a material handling device, forklift, or hand truck when lifting items
  • The employee is frequently required to climb or balance; and to stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception

WORK ENVIRONMENT:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to moving mechanical parts, toxic or caustic chemicals, airborne particles and vibration from hammering of parts and using hand tools
  • Since it is a manufacturing environment, the noise level is usually loud due to the different machinery being operated (i.e. forklifts, hand tools, machines in other departments) and the testing that occurs. Normal noise exposure in the area ranges from 80-90 d BA; hearing protection is required while on the plant floor

Job Overview:

The Assembly & Material Support Operator performs a combination of product assembly and material/parts support functions within a cell-based manufacturing environment. This role requires strong attention to detail, reliability, and the ability to work independently while supporting team objectives, safety, and continuous improvement.

(Assigned based on operational need; employees may be reassigned between functions)

Parts Picker

Job Title: Mechanical Engineer, Power Generation Containerization
Location: Sidney, OH

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview
Help build the next generation of mission-critical power in a true ground-floor opportunity. The Mechanical Engineer – Power Generation Containerization will help design and launch a new line of large-scale, containerized power generation solutions supporting mission-critical data centers. Ingersoll Rand is building a new data center power generation vertical, and this engineer will help shape the mechanical architecture, product platform, and manufacturing strategy behind it. The role will translate existing product knowledge from Ingersoll Rand’s acquired Australian business and North American partners into in-house designs that can be manufactured efficiently and at scale in Sidney, Ohio.

The Mechanical Engineer will own key aspects of the mechanical design and integration of these large generator systems, including structural assemblies, enclosures, cooling systems, fuel and base tanks, equipment layouts, and overall mechanical packaging. These are complex systems built around large diesel engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, controls, and serviceable layouts designed to provide critical backup power where uptime and cooling continuity are essential. As an early member of this growing technical team, the engineer will have meaningful hands-on ownership from concept and CAD design through manufacturing readiness and commercialization. The role will work closely with electrical engineering, applications engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, project management, sales, and the Sidney plant to ensure solutions meet both customer requirements and manufacturing needs.

The ideal candidate brings mechanical design experience in power generation, large industrial equipment, modular systems, or complex packaged equipment. Experience with generator packaging or containerization, large diesel generators, 2MW+ systems, cooling systems, fuel tanks, enclosures, or applicable UL requirements is especially valuable. For an engineer who wants to do more than support an established product line, this is an opportunity to help build one from the ground up—with significant technical ownership, strong company investment, and meaningful growth potential.

Responsibilities:

Mechanical Design & Engineering

  • Design containerized and modular power generation solutions for data center backup and prime power applications.
  • Develop 3D models, detailed drawings, assemblies, fabrication packages, and engineering documentation using CAD software.
  • Design and integrate:
  • Generator enclosures and power modules
  • ISO container-based power systems
  • Structural support systems and equipment skids
  • Fuel storage and fuel delivery systems
  • Air intake and exhaust systems
  • Ventilation and cooling systems
  • Acoustic attenuation systems
  • Fire protection interfaces
  • Service access and maintenance provisions
  • Perform engineering calculations related to structural integrity, airflow, cooling performance, vibration, noise attenuation, and equipment support.


Data Center Solutions Engineering

  • Design power generation enclosures and modules to support mission-critical data center applications.
  • Ensure equipment layouts support uptime, maintainability, safe operations, and rapid serviceability.
  • Collaborate with customers and internal teams to develop custom solutions that meet data center site constraints and operational requirements.
  • Support designs for N, N+1, and 2N redundancy architectures.
  • Evaluate and optimize designs for deployment within hyperscale and colocation environments.


Thermal Management & Cooling

  • Develop cooling and ventilation solutions for high-performance generator systems.
  • Perform airflow analysis and thermal assessments to ensure proper equipment operation across varying environmental conditions.
  • Support integration of HVAC equipment, engine cooling packages, and auxiliary thermal management systems.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cooling efficiency and reduce energy consumption.


Product Development & Standardization

  • Support development of standardized containerized power generation platforms.
  • Drive design improvements focused on reliability, manufacturability, quality, cost, and serviceability.
  • Participate in design reviews, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and root cause investigations.
  • Evaluate new technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods to improve product performance.


Manufacturing & Testing Support

  • Provide engineering support for prototype builds and production manufacturing.
  • Resolve mechanical design issues during fabrication, assembly, and field deployment.
  • Support Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), validation testing, and commissioning activities.
  • Review supplier drawings and support qualification of mechanical components and assemblies.


Customer & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with electrical, controls, acoustics, and thermal engineering teams to ensure complete system integration.
  • Participate in technical reviews with customers, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Support sales and project teams with technical evaluations, proposals, and feasibility assessments.
  • Assist field service organizations with troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.


Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of progressive mechanical development design experience ideally in power generation, industrial equipment, modular systems, heavy equipment, or related industries.
  • 2+ years experience with 3D CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, CATIA, Inventor, or similar platforms, with bility to develop engineering documentation and manufacturing drawings.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated knowledge in:
  • Structural design
  • Sheet metal fabrication
  • Welded assemblies
  • Airflow and ventilation systems
  • Thermal management principles
  • Mechanical packaging concepts

Core Competencies

  • Power generation equipment packaging
  • Containerized power solutions
  • Structural and mechanical design
  • Thermal management systems
  • Airflow and ventilation engineering
  • Acoustic engineering and noise reduction
  • Fuel system integration
  • Vibration isolation
  • Design for manufacturability (DFM)
  • Reliability and maintainability engineering
  • Data center infrastructure requirements
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Preferences:

  • 5+ years of experience in power generation, mission-critical infrastructure, modular construction, or data center industries.
  • Experience designing:
  • Generator enclosures
  • Containerized equipment packages
  • Cooling systems
  • Fuel systems
  • Acoustic attenuation solutions
  • Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
  • Knowledge of ISO container standards and transportation requirements.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center customers.
  • Understanding of engine cooling systems, exhaust systems, and vibration isolation.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.


Travel & Work Arrangements

  • Position is based onsite in Sidney, OH
  • Relocation assistance available
  • Standard work hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm


Pay Range
The base pay range for this role is $100,000 - $130,000 annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What We Offer

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Bring marketing campaigns to life and turn customer interest into business growth. As a Demand Generation Specialist, you will develop and execute integrated campaigns across the Compression Systems and Services (CSS) North America portfolio of brands.

You will join a collaborative, data-driven marketing team and partner with colleagues across marketing, product, and sales to reach the right audiences, generate qualified leads, and strengthen sales pipeline. This role offers the opportunity to manage multiple campaigns, solve problems, and use performance insights to improve results across the customer journey.

  • Partner with brand, product, sales, channel, and aftermarket teams to develop targeted messaging, audiences, and campaign approaches.
  • Coordinate campaign assets across email, landing pages, paid media, content offers, nurture programs, and sales follow-up materials.

Job Title: Centrifugal Service Technician 

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Las Vegas, NV; Tulsa, OK; and Edmond, OK

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range 
The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) will be responsible for increasing revenue and achieving sales targets of Nash, Garo and Runtech products in the assigned geographic territory. The RSM will work closely with the manufacturers representative network to identify the addressable market and generate opportunities within the territory. RSM will maintain regular communication and constructive relationships with senior leadership, Customers, Channel Partners and other internal and external stakeholders. A strong understanding of the selling process, a technical acumen and outstanding written and verbal communication skills are essential in this role. RSM must have the skill sets defined below to competently discuss, share knowledge, train and troubleshoot our products to a variety of stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage and Develop Channel Partners: Build, manage, and develop a robust network of Channel Partners to drive the sale of Nash, Garo & Runtech products. Assess partner competencies to identify strengths and areas of improvement, develop action plans, and appoint new partners in underperforming areas to meet business goals.
  • Collaborate with Stakeholders to Drive Strategy: Work closely with Channel Partner Principals, OEMs, Product Management, and the National Sales Manager to develop and execute territory strategies that align with revenue, margin, and growth targets.
  • Lead Sales Activities and Pipeline Development: Identify, qualify, and pursue opportunities through cold calls, market research, and maintaining a network of industry contacts. Drive sales activity through Channel Partners to achieve measurable outcomes and maintain a documented pipeline via Salesforce.
  • Provide Technical and Product Support: Offer product education and technical assistance to customers, including troubleshooting, installation guidance, and identifying causes of product malfunctions to maintain the high-quality image of Nash, Garo and Runtech products.
  • Engage in the Sales Cycle and Account Management: Actively participate in all stages of the sales cycle, including quoting, account management, reviewing commercial terms of sale, and assisting with collections. Establish measurable goals for targeted accounts and provide regular updates on progress and opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Cross-Functional Teams: Work with internal teams such as Engineering, Product Management, and Operations to ensure seamless implementation, new product commercialization, and effective account growth.
  • Lead Customer Engagement and Presentations: Schedule, facilitate, and lead presentations to customers while attending industry trade shows and conferences to establish contacts, identify trends, and proactively develop leads.
  • Oversee Channel Partner Network: Supervise a large network of Channel Partner organizations across multiple states, ensuring alignment with Nash, Garo and Runtech's standards and objectives.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree 
  • 5+ years relevant product sales experience. 

Core Competencies:

  • Channel Sales Expertise: Strong understanding of channel sales strategies, including managing manufactures representative, driving revenue growth, and achieving measurable results through collaboration.
  • Product and Market Knowledge: Expertise in rotating equipment, with working knowledge of vacuum/compression and the ability to articulate the value proposition of Nash, Garo and Runtech products in customer terms.
  • Strategic Thinking and Planning: Ability to assess market opportunities, develop actionable strategies, and set specific, measurable goals to drive growth and profitability.
  • Customer-Centric Approach: Skilled at building strong relationships, understanding customer needs, and providing tailored solutions to ensure high satisfaction and repeat business.
  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient in providing technical support, troubleshooting product issues, and guiding customers through product selection, installation, and maintenance.
  • Strong Communication and Collaboration: Excellent interpersonal, negotiation, and persuasion skills to foster positive relationships with customers, Channel Partners, and internal teams.
  • Time and Task Management: Highly organized with strong time management skills, ensuring timely execution of tasks while balancing multiple priorities effectively.
  • Business Acumen: High level of business and financial acumen, enabling informed decision-making and alignment with organizational goals.
  • Self-Motivation and Discipline: Demonstrates intrinsic motivation, a disciplined work style, and the ability to work independently while contributing as part of a team.
  • Technology Proficiency: Skilled in using Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook), Enterprise Resource Planning (SAP) and CRM tools like Salesforce to document and manage sales opportunities.

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering.
  • Vacuum, air compression, blowers or any rotating equipment sales experience.
  • 5+ years outside sales experience.
  • Experience with Salesforce.
  • Experience with SAP.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Remote with up to 50% overnight travel.
  • Company car, laptop computer and cell phone provided.

Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and the planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gases, and powders – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview
Ingersoll Rand’s Compression Systems and Services Customer Center is hiring a General Line Account Manager to drive equipment and service sales throughout New York City and surrounding counties. This remote, territory-based position combines supporting distributors and selling directly to industrial customers through prospecting, quoting, account development, and consultative selling.

The Account Manager will build relationships with customers and engineering firms, recommend compressed-air solutions, and identify opportunities to influence equipment specifications. Working closely with service and operations teams, this position supports customers throughout the sales cycle, including post-order coordination through delivery, installation, and startup.

Responsibilities

  • Generate revenue through sales of compressed-air equipment, accessories, turnkey installations, service contracts, parts, service, rental equipment, and energy audits.
  • Develop existing customer accounts and secure new, competitive business through prospecting, territory planning, customer visits, and value-based selling.
  • Assess customer applications and recommend compressed-air solutions that address equipment performance, reliability, operating costs, and business needs.
  • Build relationships with engineering firms and customer decision-makers to influence specifications and increase inclusion of Ingersoll Rand solutions in project bids.
  • Prepare accurate quotes, proposals, and order documentation; negotiate pricing and commercial terms within company guidelines.
  • Support distributors and Customer Center personnel with product, service, and selling-skills training as needed.
  • Partner with service and operations teams to resolve customer issues and coordinate post-order activities through delivery, installation, and equipment startup.
  • Maintain accurate CRM records, sales pipelines, forecasts, and follow-up activities while managing selling expenses and adhering to vehicle, customer-site, and Customer Center safety requirements.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • 4+ years of experience in an industrial sales business setting or successful completion of the Ingersoll Rand Sales Development Program.

Core Competencies

  • New Business Development: Ability to prospect, identify opportunities, access decision-makers, and win competitive accounts.
  • Consultative Selling: Ability to assess customer needs and present solutions based on operational value and customer objectives.
  • Technical Aptitude: Ability to interpret technical information, perform basic equipment performance calculations, and recommend solutions with appropriate technical support.
  • Customer Account Management: Ability to develop relationships, expand existing accounts, and maintain customer loyalty.
  • Communication: Strong verbal, written, and presentation skills when working with customers, engineering firms, distributors, and internal teams.
  • Problem Solving: Ability to evaluate customer concerns and coordinate practical solutions with service and technical resources.
  • Territory Management: Ability to work independently, prioritize customer activity, and maintain disciplined pipeline management and forecasting.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to partner with service, operations, and other internal teams to support customer requirements and successful execution.

Preferences

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Business, or a related field.
  • Mechanical and electrical expertise.
  • Knowledge of Salesforce.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This is a remote, territory-based position covering New York City’s five boroughs and surrounding counties. Candidates must reside within and be familiar with the assigned territory.
  • Regional travel to customer sites is required, with the expectation of returning home nightly.
  • A company vehicle and fuel card will be provided.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license for a minimum of 12 months and meet company driving eligibility requirements. Driving history review includes major or frequent violations such as DUI within the previous five years, hit-and-run, license suspension, reckless/careless driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions within the previous three years.

Pay Range
The base salary range for this role, not including commission opportunities is $60,000 - $170,000. The pay range takes into account a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location. Hired applicants will be eligible to receive commission compensation.

What We Offer
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment — as well as for our individual well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support needed to take charge of your health and future.

Our benefits include healthcare coverage (medical, prescription, dental, and vision), wellness programs, life insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off, and an employee stock program, among other offerings. These benefits, combined with our pay transparency and inclusive culture, reflect our commitment to supporting you at work and beyond.

Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE:IR), driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset, is dedicated to helping make life better for our employees, customers and communities. Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 80+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Overview:
The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) will be responsible for increasing revenue and achieving sales targets of Nash, Garo and Runtech products in the assigned geographic territory. The RSM will work closely with the manufacturers representative network to identify the addressable market and generate opportunities within the territory. RSM will maintain regular communication and constructive relationships with senior leadership, Customers, Channel Partners and other internal and external stakeholders. A strong understanding of the selling process, a technical acumen and outstanding written and verbal communication skills are essential in this role. RSM must have the skill sets defined below to competently discuss, share knowledge, train and troubleshoot our products to a variety of stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage and Develop Channel Partners: Build, manage, and develop a robust network of Channel Partners to drive the sale of Nash, Garo & Runtech products. Assess partner competencies to identify strengths and areas of improvement, develop action plans, and appoint new partners in underperforming areas to meet business goals.
  • Collaborate with Stakeholders to Drive Strategy: Work closely with Channel Partner Principals, OEMs, Product Management, and the National Sales Manager to develop and execute territory strategies that align with revenue, margin, and growth targets.
  • Lead Sales Activities and Pipeline Development: Identify, qualify, and pursue opportunities through cold calls, market research, and maintaining a network of industry contacts. Drive sales activity through Channel Partners to achieve measurable outcomes and maintain a documented pipeline via Salesforce.
  • Provide Technical and Product Support: Offer product education and technical assistance to customers, including troubleshooting, installation guidance, and identifying causes of product malfunctions to maintain the high-quality image of Nash, Garo and Runtech products.
  • Engage in the Sales Cycle and Account Management: Actively participate in all stages of the sales cycle, including quoting, account management, reviewing commercial terms of sale, and assisting with collections. Establish measurable goals for targeted accounts and provide regular updates on progress and opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Cross-Functional Teams: Work with internal teams such as Engineering, Product Management, and Operations to ensure seamless implementation, new product commercialization, and effective account growth.
  • Lead Customer Engagement and Presentations: Schedule, facilitate, and lead presentations to customers while attending industry trade shows and conferences to establish contacts, identify trends, and proactively develop leads.
  • Oversee Channel Partner Network: Supervise a large network of Channel Partner organizations across multiple states, ensuring alignment with Nash, Garo and Runtech's standards and objectives.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree 
  • 5+ years relevant product sales experience. 

Core Competencies:

  • Channel Sales Expertise: Strong understanding of channel sales strategies, including managing manufactures representative, driving revenue growth, and achieving measurable results through collaboration.
  • Product and Market Knowledge: Expertise in rotating equipment, with working knowledge of vacuum/compression and the ability to articulate the value proposition of Nash, Garo and Runtech products in customer terms.
  • Strategic Thinking and Planning: Ability to assess market opportunities, develop actionable strategies, and set specific, measurable goals to drive growth and profitability.
  • Customer-Centric Approach: Skilled at building strong relationships, understanding customer needs, and providing tailored solutions to ensure high satisfaction and repeat business.
  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient in providing technical support, troubleshooting product issues, and guiding customers through product selection, installation, and maintenance.
  • Strong Communication and Collaboration: Excellent interpersonal, negotiation, and persuasion skills to foster positive relationships with customers, Channel Partners, and internal teams.
  • Time and Task Management: Highly organized with strong time management skills, ensuring timely execution of tasks while balancing multiple priorities effectively.
  • Business Acumen: High level of business and financial acumen, enabling informed decision-making and alignment with organizational goals.
  • Self-Motivation and Discipline: Demonstrates intrinsic motivation, a disciplined work style, and the ability to work independently while contributing as part of a team.
  • Technology Proficiency: Skilled in using Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook), Enterprise Resource Planning (SAP) and CRM tools like Salesforce to document and manage sales opportunities.

Preferences:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering.
  • Vacuum, air compression, blowers or any rotating equipment sales experience.
  • 5+ years outside sales experience.
  • Experience with Salesforce.
  • Experience with SAP.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Remote with up to 50% overnight travel.
  • Company car, laptop computer and cell phone provided.

The pay range for this role is $160,000 - $190,000. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.  

What We Offer:

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Job Title: Centrifugal Service Technician 

Location: Dallas, TX; San Antonio, TX; Pomona, CA; San Diego, CA; Phoenix, AZ; Las Vegas, NV; Tulsa, OK; and Edmond, OK

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Summary 

  • The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 3 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  
     

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 5 years. 
  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.
  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 
Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range 
The pay range for this role is $35.00-$65.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What we Offer

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. Centrifugal Service Technician 
Location: Buena Park, CA

About Us 

Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Job Summary 

The Centrifugal Service Technician – Compression Technologies and Services serves customers by installing, trouble shooting, repairing and maintaining our centrifugal compressor product lines including Centac and Turbo Air models, along with additional compressed air system components. You will use precision measuring tools for diagnostic trouble shooting of compressed air equipment. In addition, you need to have knowledge of all operations and parts manuals associated with all equipment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Provide technical assistance on equipment pre-commissioning and start-ups, installations, and repairs of compressed air systems, including “hands-on” work to assure equipment operates to customer’s requirement. 

  • Read wiring schematics and diagrams for equipment, research complex technical issues, and find/implement solutions.  

  • Document service and installation activities by completing work orders for each job, performing maintenance checklists, and maintaining daily time sheets. 

  • Maintain rapport with customers by suggesting improved methods and techniques and recommending system improvements. Increase Ingersoll Rand customer’s awareness of how Ingersoll Rand products, services and solutions; such as Package CARE, Preventative Maintenance, Diagnostics, Audits, and Leak Detection, can benefit their operations. 

  • Conduct safety assessments of a continuously changing work environment. Ensure proper operation of compressed air equipment by completing preventative maintenance requirements and 47-point inspections on a wide variety of compressors, refrigerated dryers, desiccant dryers and additional compressed air components. 

  • Work with Service Coordinator and operations teams on ordering and gathering parts and supplies necessary to complete installations and repairs. 

  • Explain practices, procedures, and policies to reach agreement with suppliers and others outside of the job area. 

  • Conduct basic vibration and air quality troubleshooting. 

Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years of Centrifugal compressor experience. 

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.  

Core Competencies 

  • Operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage. Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 

  • Excellent verbal/written communication skills and customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 

  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years. 

  • Ability to work in diverse conditions including but not limited to mechanical equipment rooms with exposure to noisy operating equipment, exposure to extreme weather conditions, precarious places, and risk of electrical shock (high voltage) with NFPA or equivalent standards.

  • This position is highly physical and requires regular use of hands, fingers, walking, stooping, and kneeling, and requires employees to regularly lift and or move weight limits in line with the safety policy. 

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

Daily travel to customer sites, occasional overtime, and occasional overnight stays required. 

Pay Range

Starting Pay will range between Min - 50,000.00 - Max - 104,000.00. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title: Procurement Supervisor            
Location: Sedalia, MO
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.  

Job Overview:
Step into a visible opportunity with Gardner Denver, Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, part of Ingersoll Rand, where your work will directly influence product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia facility. Bring your leadership and purchasing experience to an environment where the scale is significant and career opportunities extend well beyond a single location.

As Procurement Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of buyers supporting a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment with hundreds of thousands of SKUs, millions of dollars in material activity, and a network of domestic and international suppliers. You will strengthen team performance through employee development, accountability, workload management, succession planning, and process improvement—all while helping achieve critical operational and supplier-performance goals.

This opportunity is designed for a proven people manager who enjoys being present with the team, coaching employees, solving problems, and improving how work gets done. You should bring progressive purchasing experience and practical knowledge of purchase orders, supplier relationships, material procurement, and purchasing processes. Experience with ERP or MRP systems and strong Excel skills will also be important to your success. Manufacturing experience is valuable but not required.

If you have advanced within purchasing, directly managed and developed employees, addressed performance and accountability matters, and succeeded in a complex, high-volume environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement: Responsible for Managing a Team that Plans, purchases and controls the level of inventory necessary to effectively meet the Master Production Schedule and order backlog while reducing inventory levels.  Establishes inventory levels.  Assists in development of the production plan based upon sales orders, forecasts and historical demand for product.  Negotiate purchased material delivery schedules. 
  • Forecasts: Reviews shortage forecasts and initiates activities to expedite delivery.  Reviews production schedules to adjust forecast of materials demand.  Works with engineering and production in developing material planning required to forecast product requirements. 
  • Suppliers: Develops relationships with suppliers to ensure product is available at an appropriate cost.  Sources alternative suppliers of critical parts and components to insure dependable and cost effective supply. 
  • Customer Supply:  Plans and purchases materials for customer and planned requirements in order to support on-time customer shipments.  Uses historical sales to forecast new sales.   
  • Quality:  Works with engineering to insure specifications are met on all purchased parts.  Analyzes and identifies supplier quality trends to prevent problems.  Finds alternative sources for products and/or parts. 
  • Management:  Develops and maintains a high performance team through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience in purchasing, buying, materials management, or a related function. 
  • 3+ years of progressive purchasing or buying experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas and data analysis. 
  • 2+ years of experience supervising or managing employees, including performance management. 
  • 2+ years of experience using an ERP system, such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or a comparable platform.

Core Competencies
  • Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Uses data, sound judgment, and root-cause analysis to resolve purchasing, inventory, supplier, and material-availability challenges.
  • People Leadership and Development: Builds team capability through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Accountability and Performance Management: Establishes measurable goals, addresses performance concerns directly, and creates a culture of ownership and consistent follow-through.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Communicates clearly across all levels and partners effectively with suppliers, Engineering, Production, Sales, and other operational teams.
  • Planning and Organization: Effectively prioritizes competing demands, balances team workloads, and manages multiple purchasing activities in a complex, high-volume environment.
  • Project and Process Management: Organizes work effectively, tracks progress, and improves purchasing processes to support inventory, delivery, quality, and cost objectives.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Develops productive supplier partnerships while maintaining appropriate accountability for cost, quality, availability, and delivery performance.
  • Adaptability and Composure: Remains responsive and solutions-focused while managing shortages, shifting priorities, supplier issues, and changing production requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • International purchasing
  • SAP experience / exposure
  • APICS certification 

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is onsite in Sedalia, MO

Job Overview: 
The Field Service Technician is responsible for providing field technical support for IR products, striving to be customer focused, fully responsive, and successful in meeting the 24/7 technical service needs of customers. Develop a collaborative relationship with the balance of IR to establish this area as the “go-to” place for technical field service knowledge.  Focus on providing valued solutions to customers, utilizing IR services as well as IR’s products. The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.
  • Suggest improvements to processes and procedures in order to improve customer response time and accuracy of all data
  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.
  • Generate sales leads from customers who could benefit from additional support in order to improve solutions provided, improve relationships, and grow IR installed base, collect information for the Customer Relationship Management [CRM] system and provide information to Sales for additional opportunities; and improve global visibility of IR Aftermarket in the CRM system

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • The job includes an assigned vehicle for work use, so the candidate must have a valid license and be able to pass a Motor Vehicle background check.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written) 
  • Excellent collaboration skills
  • Strong computer skills in Microsoft® Word, Excel, PowerPoint 
  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner
  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team
  • Ability to create and maintain strong relationships with customers, employees and Sales Reps
  • High moral and ethical standards; integrity is continuously apparent
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world” 

Preferences:

  • Bilingual in Spanish is highly desired
  • Some technical schooling, classwork toward a degree in a technical area
  • Background evidencing positions with increasing responsibility and leadership
  • Experience specifying replacement parts for highly engineered equipment and products
  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling
  • Troubleshoot vibration, system, and aerodynamic problems in equipment
 

Physical Requirements:

  • Prolonged Standing: Ability to stand for 8–12 hours daily.
  • Frequent Bending: Regular kneeling, crouching, crawling, and stooping.
  • Climbing Ability: Safely ascend ladders, scaffolding, and stairs while wearing fall protection.
  • Manual Dexterity: Fine motor skills to handle small tools.
  • Awkward Positions: Working in tight, cramped, or confined spaces.
  • Overhead Reaching: Extending arms overhead for extended periods.
  • Visual Acuity: Close vision, color vision, and depth perception.
  • Weather Exposure: Working in extreme heat, cold, or rain.
  • Driving Endurance: Operating a service vehicle for long hours.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position is remote. The selected candidate will need to be based in Florida or the southeastern U.S. near a major airport.
  • Up to 80% travel, with possibility of international travel

Job Overview:

The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.
  • Suggest improvements to processes and procedures in order to improve customer response time and accuracy of all data
  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • The job includes an assigned vehicle for work use, so the candidate must have a valid license and be able to pass a Motor Vehicle background check.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written) 
  • Excellent collaboration skills
  • Strong computer skills in Microsoft® Word, Excel, PowerPoint 
  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner

  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world”

  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling
  • Troubleshoot vibration, system, and aerodynamic problems in equipment
 

Physical Requirements:

  • Prolonged Standing: Ability to stand for 8–12 hours daily.
  • Frequent Bending: Regular kneeling, crouching, crawling, and stooping.
  • Climbing Ability: Safely ascend ladders, scaffolding, and stairs while wearing fall protection.
  • Manual Dexterity: Fine motor skills to handle small tools.
  • Awkward Positions: Working in tight, cramped, or confined spaces.
  • Overhead Reaching: Extending arms overhead for extended periods.
  • Visual Acuity: Close vision, color vision, and depth perception.
  • Weather Exposure: Working in extreme heat, cold, or rain.

  • This position is remote. The selected candidate will need to be based in Florida or the southeastern U.S. near a major airport.
  • Up to 80% travel, with possibility of international travel
