Job Overview:
The Field Service Technician is responsible for providing field technical support for IR products, striving to be customer focused, fully responsive, and successful in meeting the 24/7 technical service needs of customers. Develop a collaborative relationship with the balance of IR to establish this area as the “go-to” place for technical field service knowledge. Focus on providing valued solutions to customers, utilizing IR services as well as IR’s products. The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.
  • Suggest improvements to processes and procedures in order to improve customer response time and accuracy of all data
  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.
  • Generate sales leads from customers who could benefit from additional support in order to improve solutions provided, improve relationships, and grow IR installed base, collect information for the Customer Relationship Management [CRM] system and provide information to Sales for additional opportunities; and improve global visibility of IR Aftermarket in the CRM system


Requirements:

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • The job includes an assigned vehicle for work use, so the candidate must have a valid license and be able to pass a Motor Vehicle background check.


Core Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written)
  • Excellent collaboration skills
  • Strong computer skills in Microsoft® Word, Excel, PowerPoint
  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner
  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team
  • Ability to create and maintain strong relationships with customers, employees and Sales Reps
  • High moral and ethical standards; integrity is continuously apparent
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world”


Preferences:

  • Bilingual in Spanish is highly desired
  • Some technical schooling, classwork toward a degree in a technical area
  • Background evidencing positions with increasing responsibility and leadership
  • Experience specifying replacement parts for highly engineered equipment and products
  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling
  • Troubleshoot vibration, system, and aerodynamic problems in equipment

Physical Requirements:

  • Heavy Lifting: Must be able to lift up to 50–75 pounds regularly.
  • Prolonged Standing: Ability to stand for 8–12 hours daily.
  • Frequent Bending: Regular kneeling, crouching, crawling, and stooping.
  • Climbing Ability: Safely ascend ladders, scaffolding, and stairs while wearing fall protection.
  • Manual Dexterity: Fine motor skills to handle small tools.
  • Awkward Positions: Working in tight, cramped, or confined spaces.
  • Overhead Reaching: Extending arms overhead for extended periods.
  • Visual Acuity: Close vision, color vision, and depth perception.
  • Weather Exposure: Working in extreme heat, cold, or rain.
  • Driving Endurance: Operating a service vehicle for long hours.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • This position is remote. The selected candidate will need to be based in Florida or the southeastern U.S. near a major airport.
  • Up to 80% travel, with possibility of international travel


Pay Range: The pay range for this role is $65,000k - $85,000k annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

Job Title: Chiller Test Engineer
Location: Junction City, OR

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.

Job Overview

The Chiller Test Engineer is responsible for planning, executing, monitoring, and documenting performance, reliability, safety, and validation testing of commercial and industrial chiller systems. This role supports product development, product validation, regulatory compliance, quality improvement, and continuous innovation by ensuring chillers meet customer requirements, industry standards, and company performance specifications. The engineer collaborates closely with Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Controls, and Laboratory teams to deliver accurate and timely test results.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute test plans, procedures, and protocols for air-cooled and water-cooled chiller products.
  • Conduct performance, functional, reliability, endurance, acoustic, and environmental testing of HVAC equipment.
  • Configure and operate laboratory equipment, instrumentation, data acquisition systems, and controls used for chiller testing.
  • Collect, analyze, and interpret test data to verify compliance with design specifications and industry standards.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical, refrigeration, electrical, and controls-related issues identified during testing.
  • Identify root causes of product performance issues and provide engineering recommendations for corrective actions.
  • Prepare detailed technical reports summarizing test conditions, results, conclusions, and recommendations.
  • Coordinate laboratory schedules, test setup activities, and resource requirements to support product development timelines.
  • Support certification and compliance testing to applicable standards such as AHRI, ASHRAE, UL, CE, and other regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with design engineers to validate new product designs, design modifications, and cost-reduction initiatives.
  • Monitor laboratory equipment calibration and ensure test procedures comply with quality and safety requirements.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives related to testing processes, laboratory operations, and product performance.
  • Support manufacturing and field issue investigations through testing and data analysis.
  • Maintain accurate technical documentation and test records.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, HVAC Engineering, or related engineering discipline is preferred
  • 3+ years of engineering experience in HVAC, refrigeration, thermal systems, product testing, or laboratory environments.


Core competencies

  • Experience with test instrumentation, sensors, data acquisition systems, and performance measurement techniques.
  • Knowledge of vapor compression refrigeration cycles, heat transfer principles, and HVAC systems.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience interpreting engineering drawings, specifications, and wiring diagrams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel for data analysis.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and testing priorities simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience testing commercial HVAC equipment, chillers, heat pumps, or refrigeration systems.
  • Familiarity with AHRI, ASHRAE, UL, ISO, and related industry standards.
  • Experience with LabVIEW, MATLAB, Python, Minitab, or similar data analysis tools.
  • Knowledge of PLCs, building automation systems, or embedded controls.
  • Understanding of refrigeration components including compressors, heat exchangers, expansion devices, and controls.
  • Experience with Design Verification Testing (DVT), Product Validation Testing (PVT), and reliability testing.

Technical Competencies

  • Refrigeration and HVAC systems
  • Chiller performance testing
  • Data acquisition and analysis
  • Root cause analysis
  • Test method development
  • Product validation
  • Controls and instrumentation
  • Thermal systems engineering
  • Regulatory compliance testing
  • Problem-solving and continuous improvement


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully onsite in Junction City, OR
  • Minimal travel expected.

What We Offer

Job title: Production Coordinator

Location: Southern Pines, NC (onsite)

About Us

Ingersoll Rand is a Fortune 500 company with a passion for making lives better. We do this by living our values, and through a relentless focus on the success of our customers and partnering with our employees to think and act like owners. We believe in sustainability through the development and distribution of a broad range of global brands designed to meet the needs of our customers in both efficient and responsible ways. Ingersoll Rand is a diverse and inclusive environment. For more information visit: www.irco.com.

Job Overview:
We are looking for a driven and organized Production Coordinator to support our manufacturing operations. In this role, you will coordinate daily workflow, communicate production goals, assign responsibilities, manage schedules, and provide coaching and mentorship to team members. You will help ensure a safe working environment, maintain quality standards, achieve production targets, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced environment, effectively manages multiple priorities, and consistently delivers results.

Responsibilities:

  • Train, develop, and support assemblers to ensure a thorough understanding of departmental procedures, work instructions, and quality requirements.
  • Maintain production scheduling systems and productivity tracking tools while collaborating with cross-functional departments to meet operational objectives.
  • Monitor and evaluate team member performance, recommend development opportunities, assign projects that build skills and capabilities, and conduct annual performance evaluations.
  • Identify, track, communicate, and help resolve material shortages, equipment issues, and other production-related concerns that may impact operations.
  • Communicate production goals and delivery expectations to ensure on-time performance targets are understood and achieved.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in responding to changing business needs, priorities, and responsibilities.
  • Conduct quality inspections and audits in accordance with established quality procedures, customer requirements, and ISO standards.
  • Participate in Material Review Board (MRB) activities and contribute to quality improvement initiatives and problem-solving discussions.
  • Promote and maintain a safe work environment by adhering to all safety policies and ensuring proper use of required personal protective equipment (PPE).

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills are a must
  • 1-2 years of assembly experience with 3 years supervisory experience
  • Understanding of KPI (key performance indicators)
  • Understanding of Lean principles and responsibilities
  • Proficient computer knowledge (i.e. log on credentials (SSO), JD Edwards, and Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel)
  • Ability to lift up to 35lbs

Core Competencies:

  • Advanced operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.? Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases.
  • Advanced verbal/written communication skills
  • Advanced customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements

  • Fully site based
  • Climate controlled manufacturing plant
  • Protective eyewear and footwear required

Title: Assembler
Location: Mocksville, NC (Onsite) (338 Valley Rd. Mocksville, NC 27028)
Shift: 2nd shift (Monday - Friday -2pm - 10pm) Full Time, Direct Hire

Job Overview:
This is a Rotary Test Technician role supporting the build and functional test of rotary screw and centrifugal air compressor packages. This is more than just a job; it’s an opportunity to be part of a company that values creativity, excellence, and collaboration



Responsibilities:

  • Use computer software programs for controlling tests and analyze test data per acceptance criteria.
  • Layout, assemble, and install required electrical supply cabling, instrumentation, hose connections to water cooling systems, and compressed air outlet piping.
  • Troubleshoot and repair or replace instrumentation and/or product hardware due to test failures and read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, assembly instructions, bills of material, and quality control documents.
  • Ensures that all tools used in performing job duties are within calibration, as stated on calibration sticker. Where discrepancies arise, immediate notification of supervisor occurs and performs job duties with limited supervision.
  • Uses problem solving skills (identify problems and respond correctly). Shall be capable of performing disassembly and rebuild of air ends, or sensitive rotating assemblies.
  • Exhibits a high degree of manual dexterity with great attention to detail and workmanship and demonstrate use of calipers, dial, indicators, precision measuring devices.


Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate and 2 years of testing experience in a manufacturing, aerospace, or similar environment
  • Repetitive assembly operations, grasping, standing, lifting, bending, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position.
  • Able to stand for extended periods – 8 hours minimum and able to stoop, bend, crawl, and being able to maneuver in tight spaces.
  • Ability to read blueprints, schematics, and electrical wiring diagrams.
  • Ability to use correct tooling, fixturing and equipment to perform work tasks to engineering specifications.



Core Competencies:

  • Strong problem-solving skills (identify problems and respond correctly).



Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • This position will be fully site based at our facility in Mocksville, NC.

We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Job Overview:
Step into a visible opportunity with Gardner Denver, Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, part of Ingersoll Rand, where your work will directly influence product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia facility. Bring your leadership and purchasing experience to an environment where the scale is significant and career opportunities extend well beyond a single location.

As Procurement Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of buyers supporting a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment with hundreds of thousands of SKUs, millions of dollars in material activity, and a network of domestic and international suppliers. You will strengthen team performance through employee development, accountability, workload management, succession planning, and process improvement—all while helping achieve critical operational and supplier-performance goals.

This opportunity is designed for a proven people manager who enjoys being present with the team, coaching employees, solving problems, and improving how work gets done. You should bring progressive purchasing experience and practical knowledge of purchase orders, supplier relationships, material procurement, and purchasing processes. Experience with ERP or MRP systems and strong Excel skills will also be important to your success. Manufacturing experience is valuable but not required.

If you have advanced within purchasing, directly managed and developed employees, addressed performance and accountability matters, and succeeded in a complex, high-volume environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement: Responsible for Managing a Team that Plans, purchases and controls the level of inventory necessary to effectively meet the Master Production Schedule and order backlog while reducing inventory levels.  Establishes inventory levels.  Assists in development of the production plan based upon sales orders, forecasts and historical demand for product.  Negotiate purchased material delivery schedules. 
  • Forecasts: Reviews shortage forecasts and initiates activities to expedite delivery.  Reviews production schedules to adjust forecast of materials demand.  Works with engineering and production in developing material planning required to forecast product requirements. 
  • Suppliers: Develops relationships with suppliers to ensure product is available at an appropriate cost.  Sources alternative suppliers of critical parts and components to insure dependable and cost effective supply. 
  • Customer Supply:  Plans and purchases materials for customer and planned requirements in order to support on-time customer shipments.  Uses historical sales to forecast new sales.   
  • Quality:  Works with engineering to insure specifications are met on all purchased parts.  Analyzes and identifies supplier quality trends to prevent problems.  Finds alternative sources for products and/or parts. 
  • Management:  Develops and maintains a high performance team through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience in purchasing, buying, materials management, or a related function. 
  • 3+ years of progressive purchasing or buying experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas and data analysis. 
  • 2+ years of experience supervising or managing employees, including performance management. 
  • 2+ years of experience using an ERP system, such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or a comparable platform.

Core Competencies
  • Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Uses data, sound judgment, and root-cause analysis to resolve purchasing, inventory, supplier, and material-availability challenges.
  • People Leadership and Development: Builds team capability through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Accountability and Performance Management: Establishes measurable goals, addresses performance concerns directly, and creates a culture of ownership and consistent follow-through.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Communicates clearly across all levels and partners effectively with suppliers, Engineering, Production, Sales, and other operational teams.
  • Planning and Organization: Effectively prioritizes competing demands, balances team workloads, and manages multiple purchasing activities in a complex, high-volume environment.
  • Project and Process Management: Organizes work effectively, tracks progress, and improves purchasing processes to support inventory, delivery, quality, and cost objectives.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Develops productive supplier partnerships while maintaining appropriate accountability for cost, quality, availability, and delivery performance.
  • Adaptability and Composure: Remains responsive and solutions-focused while managing shortages, shifting priorities, supplier issues, and changing production requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • International purchasing
  • SAP experience / exposure
  • APICS certification 

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is onsite in Sedalia, MO

What We Offer

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Customers lean on us for our technology-driven excellence in mission-critical flow creation and industrial solutions across 40+ respected brands where our products and services excel in the most complex and harsh conditions. Our employees develop customers for life through their daily commitment to expertise, productivity and efficiency. For more information, visit www.IRCO.com.

Job Title: Field Service Technician

Location: Northern Indiana or Ohio preferred - Remote
About Us 
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future.


Job Overview: 
The Field Service Technician is responsible for providing field technical support for IR products, striving to be customer focused, fully responsive, and successful in meeting the 24/7 technical service needs of customers. Develop a collaborative relationship with the balance of IR to establish this area as the “go-to” place for technical field service knowledge.  Focus on providing valued solutions to customers, utilizing IR services as well as IR’s products. The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.
  • Suggest improvements to processes and procedures in order to improve customer response time and accuracy of all data
  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.
  • Generate sales leads from customers who could benefit from additional support in order to improve solutions provided, improve relationships, and grow IR installed base, collect information for the Customer Relationship Management [CRM] system and provide information to Sales for additional opportunities; and improve global visibility of IR Aftermarket in the CRM system

Requirements:

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • The job includes an assigned vehicle for work use, so the candidate must have a valid license and be able to pass a Motor Vehicle background check.

Core Competencies:

  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written) 
  • Excellent collaboration skills
  • Strong computer skills in Microsoft® Word, Excel, PowerPoint 
  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner
  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team
  • Ability to create and maintain strong relationships with customers, employees and Sales Reps
  • High moral and ethical standards; integrity is continuously apparent
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world” 

Preferences:

  • Bilingual in Spanish is highly desired
  • Some technical schooling, classwork toward a degree in a technical area
  • Background evidencing positions with increasing responsibility and leadership
  • Experience specifying replacement parts for highly engineered equipment and products
  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling
  • Troubleshoot vibration, system, and aerodynamic problems in equipment
 

Physical Requirements:

  • Heavy Lifting: Must be able to lift up to 50–75 pounds regularly.
  • Prolonged Standing: Ability to stand for 8–12 hours daily.
  • Frequent Bending: Regular kneeling, crouching, crawling, and stooping.
  • Climbing Ability: Safely ascend ladders, scaffolding, and stairs while wearing fall protection.
  • Manual Dexterity: Fine motor skills to handle small tools.
  • Awkward Positions: Working in tight, cramped, or confined spaces.
  • Overhead Reaching: Extending arms overhead for extended periods.
  • Visual Acuity: Close vision, color vision, and depth perception.
  • Weather Exposure: Working in extreme heat, cold, or rain.
  • Driving Endurance: Operating a service vehicle for long hours.

Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements 

  • This position is remote. The selected candidate will need to be based in Florida or the southeastern U.S. near a major airport.
  • Up to 80% travel, with possibility of international travel 

Pay Range: The pay range for this role is $65,000k - $85,000k annually. The pay range considers a wide range of factors that include a candidate’s skills; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and geographic location.

What We Offer 
At Ingersoll Rand, we embrace a culture of personal ownership — taking responsibility for our company, our communities, and our environment, as well as our individual health and well-being. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to empower you with the tools and support necessary to take charge of your health, ensuring that together, we can continue to make life better. Our range of benefits includes health care options like medical and prescription plans, dental and vision coverage, as well as wellness programs. Additionally, we provide life insurance, a robust 401(k) plan, paid time off, and even an employee stock grant, among other offerings. These benefits are our commitment to you, so you can be your best at work and beyond.

Job Overview

The Quality Control Lead oversees inspection activities to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, internal quality standards, customer specifications, and the company’s quality management system. Reporting to the Site Quality Manager, this role coordinates daily inspector schedules and workflow, supports outgoing material and product inspections, mentors inspectors, and partners with management, internal departments, and customers on quality matters. Strong working knowledge of ISO 13485 and the FDA quality system requirements referenced in 21 CFR 820 is expected.

Responsibilities

• Coordinate daily schedules, assignments, inspection workflow, and shipment priorities for Quality Inspectors; lead visual and dimensional inspection, quality testing, and Device History Record (DHR) review.
• Review and approve inspection records, nonconformance reports, and related documentation; maintain quarantine locations and ensure proper disposition of parts and materials.
• Train and mentor inspectors through onboarding and on-the-job instruction; participate in inspector interviews and provide the Quality Manager with objective feedback on development, training, and performance.
• Partner with manufacturing, engineering, logistics, purchasing, maintenance, and QC to support the quality assurance program; assist internal and external audits with inspection documentation and evidence of compliance.
• Support root cause investigations, nonconformance reports, corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs), risk management, process failure mode and effects analysis (pFMEA), and Control Plans.
• Assist in developing dimensional and quality control process sheets and work instructions; partner with Engineering on vision system measurement teaching files, and lead Gage R&R studies and other QC validation activities.
• Follow cleanroom, gowning, contamination control, traceability, line clearance, process control, safety, housekeeping, and 5S procedures; meet Flexan standards for quality, cleanliness, and productivity.
• Accurately enter daily ERP data, including time, work orders, operations, indirect work, quantities produced, and deviations; identify improvements to inspection methods, defect reduction, productivity, and waste reduction.

Requirements

• Experience in quality inspection within a medical device manufacturing environment.
• Strong knowledge of ISO 13485 and the FDA quality system requirements referenced in 21 CFR 820, with the ability to support compliance with established QMS processes.
• Ability to analyze information and data to identify product or compliance risks and support management decisions.
• Strong computer skills and familiarity with Microsoft Windows applications.
• Ability to work in a cleanroom and follow gowning requirements, including hair covering and appropriate personal protective equipment.
• Ability to meet the role’s physical demands, with or without reasonable accommodation: frequently lift or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally up to 50 pounds; occasionally sit, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.

Core Competencies

• Clear written and verbal communication; professional interactions with coworkers, managers, customers, and all levels of the organization.
• Leadership of employees who may not be direct reports; effective organization, goal setting, prioritization, follow-up, multitasking, and attention to detail.
• Reliable attendance, teamwork, respectful communication, and follow-through; recognize strong performance and address or report safety, performance, interpersonal, and equipment concerns promptly.
• Ownership, integrity, humility, customer focus, and commitment to inspired teams; proactively identify opportunities to improve quality, productivity, waste reduction, and morale.

Travel and Work Arrangements Requirements

Fully onsite at Flexan in Salt Lake City, Utah. First shift, Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–3:30 p.m. Mountain Time, with overtime as needed. This is a non-exempt position at a non-union site. The work environment includes cleanroom operations and occasional exposure to moving mechanical parts.

Job Overview:
We are seeking a skilled, safety-focused Service Technician to install, commission, maintain, diagnose, and repair industrial glycol and refrigeration chillers at customer locations. This position serves as a technical representative of the company and is responsible for restoring equipment performance, resolving customer concerns, and documenting service work accurately. The ideal candidate combines strong refrigeration, electrical, mechanical, and controls knowledge with sound judgment, professional communication, and the ability to work independently in the field.

Responsibilities:

  • Install, commission, inspect, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair industrial chillers, refrigeration systems, and related equipment at customer sites.
  • Review service documentation, engineering drawings, wiring diagrams, manuals, and specifications to support effective field service activities.
  • Diagnose and resolve refrigeration, mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and controls-related issues using systematic troubleshooting methods and performance testing.
  • Perform refrigerant handling activities including leak detection, pressure testing, recovery, evacuation, charging, and system performance verification in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Configure, troubleshoot, and verify PLCs, HMIs, variable frequency drives (VFDs), alarms, safety systems, control logic, and communication networks.
  • Provide technical support, customer training, and clear communication regarding equipment conditions, repair recommendations, operational best practices, and follow-up actions.
  • Complete preventive maintenance, warranty repairs, equipment modifications, component replacements, field corrective actions, and accurate service documentation.
  • Coordinate with internal teams, identify replacement parts needs, maintain service tools and equipment, participate in on-call support, and uphold professional customer service standards.


Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Working knowledge of common hand tools, power tools, multimeters, gauges, vacuum pumps, refrigerant scales, and electronic leak detectors.
  • Ability to read electrical schematics, refrigeration piping diagrams, technical manuals, and written service procedures.
  • Ability to perform basic electrical and refrigeration calculations and interpret operating data.
  • Ability to diagnose problems using a logical, safe, and step-by-step process.
  • Ability to work independently, manage time, make field decisions within established authority, and request support when needed.
  • Basic computer skills and ability to complete digital reports, email communication, timekeeping, and service documentation.
  • Willingness and ability to travel, including overnight travel, according to business and customer needs.
  • Ability to work flexible hours and participate in after-hours service coverage when required.
  • Valid driver's license and an acceptable driving record consistent with company requirements.


Core Competencies:

  • Strong mechanical and electrical aptitude with experience troubleshooting equipment or systems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues to customers.
  • Reliable attendance, professional conduct, and a strong safety mindset.


Preferences:

  • Previous commercial or industrial HVAC, refrigeration, chiller, field-service, commissioning, or industrial-maintenance experience.
  • EPA Section 608 Universal Certification or the ability to obtain certification within an established timeframe.
  • Experience recovering, evacuating, charging, and documenting refrigerants in accordance with applicable requirements.
  • Strong understanding of refrigeration principles, including pressure-temperature relationships, superheat, subcooling, heat transfer, and system capacity.
  • Experience servicing compressors, pumps, heat exchangers, expansion valves, solenoid valves, pressure controls, and temperature sensors.
  • Knowledge of three-phase power, control voltage, motors, contactors, relays, transformers, circuit protection, and variable-frequency drives.
  • Experience using multimeters, clamp meters, megohmmeters, micron gauges, refrigerant scales, data loggers, and electronic leak detectors.
  • Experience navigating, programming, configuring, or troubleshooting PLCs, HMIs, programmable controllers, or building-management communication systems.
  • Experience with glycol systems, process cooling, custom-engineered equipment, or large industrial chillers.
  • Brazing experience or brazing certification.
  • OSHA, NFPA 70E, lockout/tagout, fall-protection, lift, rigging, or other relevant safety training.
  • Technical degree, HVAC or refrigeration apprenticeship, military technical training, or equivalent hands-on experience.


Travel & Work Arrangements/Requirements:

  • Approximately 75–90% travel is expected. Most travel is outside Oregon, with assignments across the United States. Local or regional assignments may also require overnight stays. Candidates must be comfortable with frequent travel and time away from home.

About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Job Overview

We are seeking a skilled Data Center Thermal Application Engineer to support the design, integration, and deployment of advanced cooling solutions in modern data centers. This role will play a critical part in enabling high-density workloads (AI/ML, HPC) by working closely with Coolant Distribution Unit (CDU), Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and Fan Array/Wall system suppliers to deliver efficient, scalable, and reliable cooling architectures. This position requires strong expertise in liquid cooling systems, airflow management, and system-level thermal integration, along with the ability to collaborate with external partners and internal cross-functional teams.


Responsibilities:

  • Design and implement thermal solutions leveraging liquid cooling (CDUs, direct-to-chip) and high-performance air-cooling systems (Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler, fan walls/arrays)
  • Candidate would need to be familiar with chiller sizing criteria and the refrigeration cycle, as that is definitely a major part of the need here.
  • Define system-level cooling architectures integrating CDU loops, facility water systems, and rack-level cooling solutions
  • Evaluate and optimize airflow strategies, including cold aisle/hot aisle containment and fan wall deployment
  • Perform thermal calculations, system sizing, and redundancy planning
  • Support site-specific solution design by assessing customer requirements, heat loads, and facility constraints
  • Provide technical guidance during installation, commissioning, and troubleshooting
  • Collaborate with field teams and customers to resolve thermal performance issues and optimize system operation
  • Develop application notes, design guides, and best practices for deployment

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering or Thermal Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience in data center cooling, thermal engineering, or HVAC systems
  • 1+ years of experience hands-on experience with at least one of the following:
  • CDUs and liquid cooling systems (direct-to-chip, liquid loops)
  • Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler
  • Fan arrays/walls or large-scale airflow systems


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with hyperscale or colocation data center environments
  • Candidate would need to be familiar with chiller sizing criteria and the refrigeration cycle, as that is definitely a major part of the need here.
  • Familiarity with AI/HPC high-density rack (>30–100kW+) cooling challenges
  • Knowledge of controls and monitoring of CDU systems (BMS/DCIM integration)
  • Experience in commissioning and field deployment of cooling systems
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or certifications in data center design (CDCDP/CDCS)
  • Proficiency in CFD and thermal simulation tools
  • Strong understanding of heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and chilled water systems
  • Experience working with external suppliers or OEM partners in a technical capacity
  • Knowledge of ASHRAE TC9.9 guidelines and data center standards
  • Strong communication skills with ability to work across internal teams and external vendors

Core Competencies

  • Strong program and project management capability
  • Leadership and influence across matrixed organizations
  • Financial and commercial acumen
  • Risk management and problem-solving
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management
  • High attention to detail and execution discipline
  • Use CFD and system modeling tools (e.g., 6SigmaDCX, ANSYS Icepak, FloTHERM) to validate thermal performance
  • Analyze liquid flow characteristics, pressure drops, and heat exchanger performance
  • Conduct lab and field validation, including thermal testing of CDU, Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and airflow systems
  • Continuously improve system efficiency, energy usage (PUE), and reliability
  • Work closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, and data center infrastructure teams
  • Support procurement and quality teams in supplier selection and qualification
  • Contribute to product development and roadmap planning for next-generation cooling solutions
  • Act as the primary technical interface with CDU, Dry Cooler/Adiabatic Dry Cooler and fan array/wall system suppliers
  • Review vendor designs, specifications, and performance data to ensure alignment with system requirements
  • Coordinate integration testing, factory acceptance testing (FAT), and site acceptance testing (SAT)

Travel & Work Requirements

  • 25%-40% travel (project sites, factory inspections, FAT/SAT, customer reviews

Job Title: Service Supervisor 
Location: Aurora, CO.

About Us  
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and the planet. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. 

Job Overview
Step into a fast-paced, customer-focused environment as our Service Supervisor in the compressed air commercial segment. You’ll oversee the local service function across the full equipment life cycle while partnering with the sales team to drive business growth. A solutions-oriented leader, you’ll guide your team in maintaining and repairing rotary screw and reciprocating air compressors, as well as compressed air system components. This role empowers you to think like an owner, taking charge of the Service P&L, making sound business decisions, and enabling your Customer Center to achieve performance goals while raising the bar in service excellence. At the core of this role is your ability to be an exceptional leader; someone who sees the big picture, hones in on the details, and elevates team performance. Take the next step in your career and lead a team where your decisions shape success and your leadership sets the standard.

Responsibilities  

  • Effectively attract, coach, counsel, train, develop, and retain all service employees. Drive continuous improvement through company performance management process and technical product training programs available. Develop employee skill levels, including customer service, process improvement, and technical skills to the highest degree possible.  
  • Collaborate with the service coordination function to respond efficiently to customers, ensure technicians’ training and skill level is appropriately matched to service customers, and ensure resources are effectively leveraged across the service area to maximize Service Technician utilization. This includes balancing customer requests for emergency repair, regular maintenance contracts, scheduled work and upgrades, installations, replacement components, and long-term service agreements.  
  • Collaborate with the sales function to consult on service agreements; attend customer meetings to win new and grow existing; service business; provide service support for installations; and drive new service business through Service Technician generated leads, quotes, and requests for proposals.    
  • Maximize cash flow by ensuring invoices are generated immediately upon completion of work and warranty claims are filed accurately and timely, managing expense budgets, and increasing utilization of the service team. Ensure that standard service work processes are created and followed. Improve transactional processes impacting the customer experience and increase overall customer satisfaction.  
  • Effectively manage service team inventory to maintain accuracy, reduce year-end write-offs, and maintain SOX compliance through detailed reporting and regular cycle counts.   
  • Ensure environmental, health and safety compliance within service team. Provide training to all employees to ensure all service personnel follow and maintain safe and productive work habits in the shop, as well as at the customer site.  
  • Other duties as assigned to support the service business and ensure customer satisfaction.   
Requirements 

  • High school diploma or GED required with relevant work experience
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in an industrial sales business setting. 
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in managing teams of people, processes and budgets strongly preferred, or an equivalent combination of relevant experience coaching, training and mentoring as a peer-leader.   
Core Competencies 
  • Advanced customer service skills including conflict resolution, communication, negotiation, etc. 
  • Leadership skills with the ability to inspire, develop, and hold teams accountable
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills 
  • Solid operating knowledge of Microsoft office software and other basic computer usage.
  • Proficiency with hand held computer (i.e. Smartphone, iPad) and network bases. 
  • Must possess a valid driver's license for a minimum of 12 months, with no major or frequent traffic violations including, but not limited to: DUI in the previous 5 years, Hit & Run, License Suspension, Reckless/Careless Driving, or multiple smaller infractions or preventable collisions in the previous 3 years.

Job Overview:
Help shape the finances behind a growing manufacturing operation. Ingersoll Rand is seeking a Plant Controller for its Junction City, Oregon site. As a trusted partner to plant leadership and the production team, you’ll turn financial insight and firsthand operational knowledge into greater cost efficiency, revenue growth, stronger margins, and improved net working capital. With demand from the data center market driving plans for increased production and workforce growth, Junction City is entering an exciting new chapter. You’ll help set its financial direction, give leaders clearer visibility into performance, and build the financial discipline needed to scale.

Work alongside production leaders on the plant floor to connect daily decisions with financial results. You’ll investigate production and purchase price variances, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns while bringing clarity to cost rollups, inventory valuation, reserves, and the metrics that matter most to the plant. Bring your accounting and finance expertise, curiosity, and business judgment to a role where the numbers lead to action. You’ll identify trends, solve root causes, strengthen analytics, and manage plant accounting while helping leaders improve performance and plan for growth.

Ready for your next step? You’ll lead a small site-based team, with a planned transition and direct knowledge transfer to help you take ownership of daily and weekly responsibilities within approximately three to six months. Prior Plant Controller experience is not required. An Assistant Controller, Senior Cost Accountant, Cost Accounting Manager, or similar professional with hands-on manufacturing experience and leadership potential could thrive here. If you can point to the KPIs you’ve improved and the measurable impact of your work, this is your chance to influence a growing plant’s performance and build your future with Ingersoll Rand.

Responsibilities:

  • Management Reporting: Deliver month-end analysis that explains financial results, trends, risks, opportunities, and their implications. Prepare the monthly operating review and report on weekly shipping trends, order rates, backlog, and net working capital metrics, including inventory performance.
  • Controls and Compliance: Maintain a strong control environment through adherence to SOX requirements and proactive partnership with internal and external auditors. Identify and resolve control gaps, and build a culture of compliance across the team. Key processes include revenue cutoff, warranty and obsolescence reserves, other valuation reserves, and account reconciliations.
  • ERP Process Improvement: Improve Epicor configurations and automation by strengthening internal processes and establishing standard work.
  • Forecasting and Budgeting: Partner with finance and business stakeholders to deliver timely, accurate forecasts and assess P&L and balance sheet risks and opportunities. Forecast bookings, revenue growth, production variances, overhead spending, and capital investments.
  • CSS and Corporate Partnership: Respond promptly to requests from shared financial services, corporate FP&A, and CSS leadership to support business performance.
  • Operational Business Partnership: Partner with plant and cross-functional leaders to provide analysis and decision support that advances annual operating plan targets. Participate in and lead IRX (Ingersoll Rand Execution Excellence) processes that support tactical and strategic objectives.
  • Team Leadership and Development: Align the team around corporate objectives, develop talent, and build the coverage needed for business continuity. Coach and mentor direct and indirect reports through succession planning, development plans, and the removal of barriers to engagement and progress.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related business concentration.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in accounting, finance, controllership, or cost-accounting
  • 3+ years experience with Excel using complex formulas, PivotTables, data analysis, reconciliations, and / or financial modeling.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated ability analyzing financial performance, identifying root causes, and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
  • 2+ years experience with ERP systems such as Epicor or something similar


Core Competencies

  • Manufacturing Cost Accounting: Working knowledge of manufacturing cost accounting, including standard costs and cost rollups, inventory reserves and valuation, production variances, purchase price variance, labor and overhead efficiency, and inventory turns.
  • Analytical Thinking: Ability to interpret complex financial data, derive actionable insights, and communicate key findings clearly and concisely to team members at all levels.
  • Problem-Solving and Continuous Improvement: Proactively identifies issues, evaluates root causes, and implements effective solutions with a focus on continuous improvement.
  • Manufacturing Accounting Acumen: Strong numerical and analytical skills, with a careful, structured approach to applying accounting principles within a manufacturing environment.
  • Collaboration and Influence: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to support cross-functional initiatives, build productive working relationships, and influence stakeholders across the organization.
  • Leadership: Ability to drive performance through others, support colleagues in pursuit of shared team goals, and maintain accountability for deliverables.
  • Communication and Coaching: Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain financial concepts clearly and influence and coach teams toward financial and operational objectives.
  • Time and Priority Management: Ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and manage multiple projects efficiently while meeting established deadlines and deliverables.


Preferences:

  • MBA or professional certification such as CMA, CFA, or CPA.
  • Experience in SOX compliance requirements, financial or operational audits, and audit engagements.
  • Demonstrated project-management experience
  • Experience using Epicor

job.title: Director, Product Quality
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.




Product Quality Leader – Customer Impact & Reliability Excellence

The Product Quality Leader owns the organization’s response to product quality issues that affect customers. The role sets priorities, drives escalation and resolution, and establishes preventive systems that reduce recurrence and strengthen product reliability.

Working across Product Management, Engineering, Manufacturing Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Support, Services, and Executive Leadership, the role advances organizational quality performance through proactive risk identification, defect prevention, systemic process weakness correction and continuous improvement. Success is reflected in fewer customer disruptions, stronger product quality and reliability performance, and the organization’s ability to deliver consistently superior customer product experience.

---

Key Responsibilities

The role’s responsibilities fall into four areas: preventing quality risks, leading the response to customer-impacting events, strengthening quality governance and accountability, and embedding lessons learned into product and process standards.

  • Champion a prevention-focused quality culture by ensuring quality is designed, validated, and monitored throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Proactively validate quality controls to identify and mitigate risks before they result in customer impact
  • Develop and execute a zero-tolerance strategy for delivered product startup and launch-related quality issues.
  • Develop and maintain standardized quality performance metrics and KPIs across all production facilities.
  • Institutionalize problem-solving (e.g. 9-Step) and knowledge-sharing processes by embedding lessons learned into standards, procedures, and operating practices.
  • Define clear ownership, accountability, and performance expectations for quality-related deliverables.
  • Identify and eliminate process deficiencies that contribute to recurring product quality and reliability issues and verify that the resulting controls prevent recurrence.
  • Establish governance, escalation criteria, and response protocols for critical product quality incidents.
  • Lead rapid containment, mitigation, communication, and resolution efforts for customer-impacting quality events.
  • Ensure corrective actions address root causes and drive sustainable, systemic improvements.
  • Establish and maintain a Repeat Issue Prevention Program focused on reducing the recurrence of customer-impacting defects.
  • Partner with Engineering and Product Management to prioritize quality and reliability risks within product roadmaps and lifecycle planning, preventing known defect patterns from reoccurring in future New Product Development (NPD) releases.
  • Ensure Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), fault-tree analysis, and reliability risk assessments are embedded as standard practices for critical products and services.

---

Success Measures

  • Reduction in customer-impacting product incidents.
  • Faster resolution of high-severity customer escalations.
  • Improved customer satisfaction and retention.
  • Reduction in recurring quality issues.
  • Increased product reliability and field performance.
  • Effective execution of corrective and preventive actions.
  • Improved organizational accountability and quality culture.
  • Continuous and accretive recognition of progress and effectiveness as captured in Employee Engagement surveys.

---

Key Competencies

  • Customer Advocacy
  • Continuous Improvement Mindset
  • Change Leadership
  • Data-Driven Decision Making
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Root Cause Analysis
  • Quality Systems Management
  • Strategic Thinking
  • Excellent Communication and Executive Presence

---

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Quality Management, Computer Science, Business, or related field.
  • 10+ years of experience in product quality, engineering, technical support, or operational leadership roles.
  • 5+ years of leadership experience managing cross-functional teams.
  • Proven experience leading resolution of critical customer-impacting issues.
  • Strong expertise in quality management systems, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Knowledge of reliability engineering, incident management, and customer support operations.
  • Experience working cross functionally and directly with executive leadership and strategic customers.
  • Demonstrated success in driving organizational change and accountability.

  • Clear and concise communicator (both oral and written)

  • Proven time management, organizational, problem solving, and prioritization skills to successfully complete responsibilities in a timely manner
  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team

Physical Requirements:

job.title: Materials Planning Manager
job.description:
Ingersoll Rand is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.




Job Overview:
This is a high-impact leadership opportunity at our Mocksville manufacturing plant, where the Materials Planning team plays a critical role in keeping production moving and customers supplied. Mocksville is entering an exciting period of growth, with new products and additional Gardner Denver product lines expected to transition into the facility. The Materials Planning Manager will have a visible and direct impact on production flow, inventory health, product-launch success, customer delivery, and the plant’s ability to scale effectively.

As the Materials Planning Manager, you will lead and develop a team of buyer/planners supporting a diverse operation that includes pack assembly, rotary assembly, remanufacturing, and machine shop activity. The plant manages a broad supplier base and a complex mix of short lead-time, book-and-turn orders and long lead-time, engineer-to-order projects. This is not a desk-only leadership position. You will remain close to the operation, helping the team anticipate supply gaps and drive execution across promise-date accuracy, past-due purchase orders, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, inventory turns, and over-entitlement reduction. You will also maintain a small hands-on purchasing portfolio supporting gears, pinions, and bull gears.

We are looking for a hands-on materials, purchasing, or planning leader who can see around corners, bring discipline to a complex ERP/MRP environment, and turn competing priorities into clear execution. The right leader will combine urgency and accountability with empathy—staying connected to the team, coaching both experienced and developing buyer/planners, identifying risks early, and helping employees navigate the daily pressures of manufacturing materials management. If you thrive in a fast-moving manufacturing environment and want your leadership to make a meaningful operational difference, this role offers the opportunity to strengthen planning discipline, improve inventory performance, support successful product launches, and ensure the right parts arrive at the right time.

Responsibilities

Materials Planning and Supply Continuity:

  • Lead site material planning activities to ensure the timely availability of materials required to support production operations.
  • Own the stocking and replenishment strategy for all site raw materials.
  • Lead the site inventory optimization strategy, balancing material availability, inventory investment, and operational requirements.
  • Serve as the escalation point when Material Planners are unable to resolve supply, delivery, inventory, or supplier-related issues effectively.


Team Leadership and Development:

  • Lead, coach, and develop the Materials Planning team, establishing clear expectations for performance, accountability, and execution.
  • Ensure team members are properly trained and effectively utilizing ERP/MRP tools, planning processes, and Ingersoll Rand standard work.
  • Support employee development through regular coaching, structured training, and individual development plans.


Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement:

  • Champion Lean principles and continuous improvement across Materials Planning functions.
  • Strengthen planning discipline, standard work, problem-solving, and root-cause corrective action practices.
  • Drive improvements in material availability, inventory performance, planning accuracy, and overall team productivity.


Cross-Functional Leadership:

  • Serve as the Materials Planning liaison across Production, Procurement, Supplier Quality, Quality Assurance, Engineering, Accounts Payable, Finance, and other functional groups.
  • Coordinate resolution of issues involving supplier quality, goods received not invoiced, invoice discrepancies, engineering changes, new product development, and other material-related business needs.
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to identify supply risks, resolve constraints, and support production, product launches, and customer delivery requirements.


Team's Responsibilities -

  • Material Planning and Inventory Management
  • Maintain material plans within the planning time fence to ensure continuity of supply.
  • Review open material requirements and proactively identify shortages, supply gaps, and inventory risks.
  • Maintain optimal inventory levels and appropriate safety stock for assigned parts.
  • Maintain accurate ABC classifications and other planning inputs required for the Plan for Every Part process.
  • Communicate forecasts, demand requirements, and replenishment plans to suppliers.
  • Maintain accurate item-master lead times based on supplier performance, process improvements, current constraints, product-family demand, and business priorities.
  • Purchasing and Supplier Management
  • Perform timely and cost-conscious procurement of production, inventory, and maintenance, repair, and operations materials.
  • Review and analyze requisitions to confirm required quantities, specifications, delivery dates, and other purchasing requirements.
  • Monitor supplier performance related to delivery, quality, responsiveness, and pricing.
  • Expedite, de-expedite, or adjust purchase orders as needed to align material availability with production demand.
  • Promptly communicate supplier delivery, quality, pricing, or capacity concerns and drive timely resolution.
  • Escalate recurring or significant supplier-performance issues to Procurement and Materials Planning leadership.
  • Shortage Management and Production Support
  • Proactively identify and manage material shortages, including documenting root causes and supporting corrective actions.
  • Coordinate with Production Planners when materials cannot be delivered as promised and develop alternative supply or scheduling solutions.
  • Analyze material and capacity availability to support accurate customer promise dates for sales orders.
  • Work with applicable functional groups to resolve complex delivery requirements, competing priorities, and material constraints.
  • Quality, Invoice, and Transaction Resolution
  • Partner with Quality Assurance and Supplier Quality to resolve supplier-related quality issues.
  • Coordinate with suppliers and Accounting to resolve invoicing, receipt, pricing, and payment discrepancies.
  • Ensure material-related transactional issues are addressed promptly to prevent supply disruption or inaccurate financial records.
  • Productivity and Cost Improvement
  • Identify and implement cost-reduction, inventory-improvement, and productivity initiatives aligned with corporate goals.
  • Maintain an active pipeline of improvement projects and accurate financial records for productivity reporting and benefit tracking.


Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 5+ years of prior people management experience, ideally managing buyer/planner, purchasing, materials, planning, scheduling, or similar supply chain teams.
  • 5+ years’ experience working in a manufacturing environment, such as industrial, assembly, machining, purchased-parts-heavy, or engineer-to-order manufacturing.
  • 4+ years of experience in materials planning, purchasing, buyer/planner functions, master scheduling, and/or supply planning, or related manufacturing supply chain execution.
  • 3+ years of demonstrated experience using ERP/MRP systems to support materials planning activities such as managing promise dates, purchase orders, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, inventory signals, and planning execution.
  • 2+ years’ experience in Excel skills to include utilizing formulas at an intermediate to advanced level


Core Competencies

  • Hands-On People Leadership: Ability to coach, support, and hold a buyer/planner team accountable through regular engagement, one-on-ones, clear communication, and a balanced leadership style.
  • Materials Planning & Purchasing Execution: Strong understanding of purchasing, planning, promise dates, past-due POs, expedites, de-expedites, cancellations, supplier follow-up, and purchased-parts support in a manufacturing environment.
  • ERP/MRP & Replenishment Systems: Ability to use ERP/MRP systems, Excel, and planning data to interpret demand signals, manage supply gaps, support pull or non-MRP replenishment where applicable, and make sound planning decisions.
  • Manufacturing Operations & Complex Production Environments: Experience supporting manufacturing operations, ideally including assembly, machining, engineer-to-order, job shop, mixed-model, or long lead-time environments.
  • Inventory, Lean & Visual Performance Management: Ability to drive inventory turns, reduce excess or over-entitlement, support lean planning practices, and use visual management tools or performance tracking systems to improve execution and accountability.


Preferences:

  • MBA and/orBachelor Concentration in Business or Supply Chain Management
  • APICS or CPIM certification
  • ERP Experience in Oracle R12
  • Experience managing a large, diverse, or complex supplier/materials portfolio
  • Experience in engineer-to-order, long lead-time, complex BOM, or mixed-model manufacturing environments
  • Experience driving inventory turns, inventory reduction, excess inventory reduction, or over-entitlement improvement


Travel and Work Arrangements

  • This position is based onsite in Mocksville, NC

Job Overview: 
The Field Service Technician is responsible for providing field technical support for IR products, striving to be customer focused, fully responsive, and successful in meeting the 24/7 technical service needs of customers. Develop a collaborative relationship with the balance of IR to establish this area as the “go-to” place for technical field service knowledge.  Focus on providing valued solutions to customers, utilizing IR services as well as IR’s products. The job also carries a variety of incentive plans that are paid out annually. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Provide technical support during repair and/or installation, at customers’ sites, of IR’s equipment to ensure standards are met and the integrity of the equipment is maintained.
  • Ensure safe work practices are followed, reporting all safety incidents and near misses on a timely basis and maintaining the goal of “zero” lost time incidents
  • Work to improve responsiveness to customers by being available to make sales calls, perform technical walk downs, and provide solutions to customers that distinguish IR’s proposals and capabilities
  • Complete required reports, including Service Reports, Customer Call Reports, Expense Reports and Time Sheets, on a timely basis in order to provide appropriate follow-up to customers, including accurate invoicing for services.

  • Comply with Department Guidelines and Procedures in order to maintain appropriate standards of service provided to customers
  • Maintain proficiencies using vibration analysis and laser alignment equipment for balancing, testing, etc.
  • Generate sales leads from customers who could benefit from additional support in order to improve solutions provided, improve relationships, and grow IR installed base, collect information for the Customer Relationship Management [CRM] system and provide information to Sales for additional opportunities; and improve global visibility of IR Aftermarket in the CRM system

  • 3 years of relevant technical background including millwright, maintenance, engineering, field service experience, or equivalent experience

  • Ability to resolve conflict, to apply critical thinking to solve problems and to escalate when needed
  • Highly organized with ability to work independently as well as part of a team
  • Ability to create and maintain strong relationships with customers, employees and Sales Reps
  • High moral and ethical standards; integrity is continuously apparent
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Comfortable and effective working in the “virtual world” 

Preferences:

  • Bilingual in Spanish is highly desired
  • Some technical schooling, classwork toward a degree in a technical area
  • Background evidencing positions with increasing responsibility and leadership
  • Experience specifying replacement parts for highly engineered equipment and products
  • Experience in industrial sales or technical selling

Physical Requirements:

Job Title: Procurement Supervisor            
Location: Sedalia, MO
 
About Us
Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Job Overview:
Step into a visible opportunity with Gardner Denver, Industrial Technology and Services, LLC, part of Ingersoll Rand, where your work will directly influence product performance, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence at our Sedalia facility. Bring your leadership and purchasing experience to an environment where the scale is significant and career opportunities extend well beyond a single location.

As Procurement Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of buyers supporting a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment with hundreds of thousands of SKUs, millions of dollars in material activity, and a network of domestic and international suppliers. You will strengthen team performance through employee development, accountability, workload management, succession planning, and process improvement—all while helping achieve critical operational and supplier-performance goals.

This opportunity is designed for a proven people manager who enjoys being present with the team, coaching employees, solving problems, and improving how work gets done. You should bring progressive purchasing experience and practical knowledge of purchase orders, supplier relationships, material procurement, and purchasing processes. Experience with ERP or MRP systems and strong Excel skills will also be important to your success. Manufacturing experience is valuable but not required.

If you have advanced within purchasing, directly managed and developed employees, addressed performance and accountability matters, and succeeded in a complex, high-volume environment, this could be an excellent next step in your career.

Responsibilities:
  • Procurement: Responsible for Managing a Team that Plans, purchases and controls the level of inventory necessary to effectively meet the Master Production Schedule and order backlog while reducing inventory levels.  Establishes inventory levels.  Assists in development of the production plan based upon sales orders, forecasts and historical demand for product.  Negotiate purchased material delivery schedules. 
  • Forecasts: Reviews shortage forecasts and initiates activities to expedite delivery.  Reviews production schedules to adjust forecast of materials demand.  Works with engineering and production in developing material planning required to forecast product requirements. 
  • Suppliers: Develops relationships with suppliers to ensure product is available at an appropriate cost.  Sources alternative suppliers of critical parts and components to insure dependable and cost effective supply. 
  • Customer Supply:  Plans and purchases materials for customer and planned requirements in order to support on-time customer shipments.  Uses historical sales to forecast new sales.   
  • Quality:  Works with engineering to insure specifications are met on all purchased parts.  Analyzes and identifies supplier quality trends to prevent problems.  Finds alternative sources for products and/or parts. 
  • Management:  Develops and maintains a high performance team through recruitment, training, coaching and establishing goals and objectives.

Requirements:
  • High school diploma or GED with relevant experience in purchasing, buying, materials management, or a related function. 
  • 3+ years of progressive purchasing or buying experience. 
  • 3+ years of experience using Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas and data analysis. 
  • 2+ years of experience supervising or managing employees, including performance management. 
  • 2+ years of experience using an ERP system, such as SAP, Oracle, JDE, or a comparable platform.

Core Competencies
  • Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving: Uses data, sound judgment, and root-cause analysis to resolve purchasing, inventory, supplier, and material-availability challenges.
  • People Leadership and Development: Builds team capability through hands-on coaching, clear expectations, meaningful feedback, employee development, and succession planning.
  • Accountability and Performance Management: Establishes measurable goals, addresses performance concerns directly, and creates a culture of ownership and consistent follow-through.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Communicates clearly across all levels and partners effectively with suppliers, Engineering, Production, Sales, and other operational teams.
  • Planning and Organization: Effectively prioritizes competing demands, balances team workloads, and manages multiple purchasing activities in a complex, high-volume environment.
  • Project and Process Management: Organizes work effectively, tracks progress, and improves purchasing processes to support inventory, delivery, quality, and cost objectives.
  • Supplier Relationship Management: Develops productive supplier partnerships while maintaining appropriate accountability for cost, quality, availability, and delivery performance.
  • Adaptability and Composure: Remains responsive and solutions-focused while managing shortages, shifting priorities, supplier issues, and changing production requirements.

Preferences:
  • Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field.
  • International purchasing
  • SAP experience / exposure
  • APICS certification 

Travel and Work Arrangements 
  • This role is onsite in Sedalia, MO
